steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat. Cross your arms over your chest or rest your fingertips lightly beside your head.
Breathe out and curl your head, shoulders and upper back off the floor, leading with your ribs rather than yanking your neck.
Stop about three-quarters of the way up, before your torso is upright, so your abs stay loaded.
Lower back down slowly, one section of your spine at a time, and start the next rep before you fully relax.
Set the seat so the pads sit on your upper chest or the handles are at shoulder height. Choose a light weight to start.
Sit tall, grip the handles and brace your stomach. Keep your feet secured under the rollers if the machine has them.
Breathe out and curl your ribs down towards your hips, rounding your upper back. Let your abs do the work, not your arms.
Pause briefly, then let the weight rise back slowly until you feel a stretch through your stomach without the stack touching down.
Kneel on a mat holding the wheel handles under your shoulders. Tuck your pelvis slightly and brace as if about to be poked in the stomach.
Roll the wheel forward slowly, letting your hips and arms extend together while your lower back stays flat, not sagging.
Go only as far as you can hold that flat back. Early on that may be a short distance, which is fine.
Pull the wheel back towards your knees using your abs, keeping your arms straight, and breathe out as you return.

advanced-kettlebell-windmill.muscles: Primary: Abs · Secondary: Glutes, Hamstrings, Shoulders
steps: Press a kettlebell overhead with one arm and lock the elbow. Turn both feet about 45 degrees away from the working arm.
Keep your eyes on the bell. Push your hips out towards the loaded side and hinge sideways, sliding your free hand down the inside of your leg.
Lower until your free hand nears the floor or your hamstrings stop you, keeping the top arm vertical and your back long.
Drive through your hips to stand back up, bell still locked out overhead. Start light; the shoulder has to stay stable throughout.
Lie on your back with hands lightly behind your head and legs raised, knees bent. Press your lower back gently into the floor.
Curl your shoulders up and bring one knee towards your chest while the other leg straightens out low.
Rotate so the opposite elbow moves towards the bent knee. Turn from your ribs rather than pulling on your head.
Switch sides in a smooth pedalling motion, breathing steadily, and keep your shoulders off the floor throughout.
Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing your thighs. Keep your elbows close to your ribs.
Curl one dumbbell up, keeping your palm facing inward the whole time, until your forearm is near vertical.
Lower it under control to a straight arm, then curl the other side.
Keep your torso still. If you have to swing to lift it, the weight is too heavy.
Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat and slightly wider than your hips. Arms long by your sides.
Lift your head and shoulders a little off the floor and hold them there.
Crunch sideways to reach one hand towards the heel on that side, then return to centre.
Alternate sides in a steady rhythm, breathing out on each reach and keeping your shoulders off the floor.
Set a bench to a moderate incline and sit back against it with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight down, palms forward.
Keep your upper arms still and curl one dumbbell up towards your shoulder. The incline puts a strong stretch on the biceps at the bottom.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly all the way to a straight arm.
Repeat with the other arm. Keep your head and shoulders against the bench rather than lifting forward.

alternate-leg-diagonal-bound.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Abductors, Adductors, Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Stand on one leg with a slight bend in the knee and hips back, arms ready to swing. Learn this with small, easy bounds first.
Push off hard and jump diagonally forward and to the side, landing on the opposite foot.
Land softly on the ball of the foot, knee tracking over toes, and absorb the landing through your hips.
Rebound straight into the next diagonal bound the other way, using your arms for rhythm. Stop when landings get sloppy.
Stand or sit between two low cable pulleys with a handle in each hand held at shoulder height, palms forward.
Brace your stomach and keep your ribs down so your lower back does not arch.
Press one handle straight up overhead until the arm is nearly locked, while the other stays at your shoulder.
Lower it back under control and press with the other arm, alternating sides.
Stand tall with a light dumbbell in each hand at your sides. Soften your knees and brace your stomach.
With a slight bend in the elbow, raise one dumbbell out in front of you to about shoulder height.
Lower it slowly, then raise the other arm, or alternate front and side raises if you are working the whole shoulder.
Keep your torso still and your shoulders down away from your ears. Lighter weights work best here.

alternating-floor-press.muscles: Primary: Chest · Secondary: Abs, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Lie on the floor with knees bent, holding a kettlebell in each hand at chest level, upper arms resting on the floor.
Brace your stomach and press one kettlebell straight up until the arm is locked, wrist straight.
Lower it under control until your upper arm touches the floor, then press the other side.
Keep the non-working bell steady at your chest. Get the bells into position one at a time, close to your body.

alternating-hang-clean.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Biceps, Calves, Forearms, Glutes, Lower back, Traps
steps: Stand with a kettlebell in each hand hanging between your legs. Hinge at the hips with a flat back. Start light while you learn the path.
Drive your hips forward and pull one bell up close to your body, letting it roll around your hand into the rack at your shoulder.
Keep the elbow tucked and the wrist straight so the bell lands softly rather than banging your forearm.
Lower it back between your legs with control and clean the other bell, alternating sides.
Clean two kettlebells to the rack position, resting on the outside of your forearms at shoulder height.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your stomach so your lower back stays neutral.
Press one kettlebell overhead until the arm is locked, biceps near your ear, while the other stays racked.
Lower it back to your shoulder under control, then press the other side.

alternating-kettlebell-row.muscles: Primary: Mid back · Secondary: Biceps, Lats
steps: Hold a kettlebell in each hand and hinge forward at the hips with a flat back until your torso is fairly low. Knees soft.
Let the bells hang under your shoulders. Brace your stomach to protect your lower back.
Row one kettlebell up to your side, pulling your elbow back and squeezing your shoulder blade in.
Lower it slowly to a straight arm, then row the other side. Keep your torso from twisting.

alternating-renegade-row.muscles: Primary: Mid back · Secondary: Abs, Biceps, Chest, Lats, Triceps
steps: Set up in a push-up position with hands gripping two kettlebells under your shoulders and feet a bit wider than hip width.
Brace your stomach and squeeze your glutes so your hips stay level and do not rotate.
Push one bell into the floor and row the other up to your ribs, elbow close to your body.
Lower it back down gently and repeat on the other side. Use bells that sit flat and will not roll.

anti-gravity-press.muscles: Primary: Shoulders · Secondary: Mid back, Traps, Triceps
steps: Set an incline bench to a low-moderate angle and lie face down on it, holding a light barbell at your shoulders with an overhand grip.
Keep your chest on the pad and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Press the bar out in front of you, in line with your body, until your arms are straight.
Bring it back to your shoulders slowly. This is about upper-back and shoulder control, so keep the load modest.
Sit on a bench with back support, holding dumbbells in front of your shoulders with palms facing you, elbows tucked in.
Brace your stomach and press the dumbbells up, rotating your palms outward as they rise.
Finish with arms nearly locked overhead and palms facing forward.
Reverse the path on the way down, rotating back so your palms face you at the bottom.
Lie on a flat bench holding a light dumbbell in each hand at your thighs, palms up, elbows slightly bent.
Sweep both dumbbells out to the sides and up in a wide arc, like making a snow angel, until they meet above your head.
Keep the elbow bend fixed and move slowly. Stop earlier if your shoulders complain at the top.
Reverse the arc back to your thighs, feeling your chest work as the weights come back down and in.

atlas-stone-trainer.muscles: Primary: Lower back · Secondary: Biceps, Forearms, Glutes, Hamstrings, Quads
steps: Stand over the trainer with feet about hip width apart, the stone or implement centred between your feet.
Squat down and wrap your arms around it, hands reaching underneath, with your back as flat as you can manage.
Drive through your legs and hips to lift it into your lap, then stand up by pushing your hips forward.
Lower it under control. Learn the pattern with a light implement before adding weight.

atlas-stones.muscles: Primary: Lower back · Secondary: Abs, Adductors, Biceps, Calves, Forearms, Glutes, Hamstrings, Mid back, Quads, Traps
steps: Straddle the stone, hinge down and wrap your arms around it with your fingers spread underneath. Use tacky if your gym allows it.
Pull the stone off the ground by driving your hips back up, rolling it onto your thighs into a lap position.
Get a fresh grip high on the stone, then drive your hips forward hard and extend up to load it onto the platform.
Start with a light stone and a low platform; this is a skill lift, and a rounded back here needs to be trained gradually.

axle-deadlift.muscles: Primary: Lower back · Secondary: Forearms, Glutes, Hamstrings, Mid back, Quads, Traps
steps: Stand with the thick axle bar over your mid-foot, feet hip width apart. Grip it just outside your legs with a double overhand grip.
Push your hips back, flatten your back, and pull the slack out of the bar. Take a big breath and brace hard.
Push the floor away and stand up, keeping the bar close to your legs, finishing tall with hips and knees locked.
Lower it by hinging back first, then bending the knees once it passes them. The thick bar is a grip test, so expect lighter loads.

back-flyes-with-bands.muscles: Primary: Shoulders · Secondary: Mid back, Triceps
steps: Stand holding a band in front of you at chest height with straight arms, hands about shoulder width apart.
Keep a small bend in the elbows and pull the band apart by moving your arms out to the sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together as your hands reach in line with your body.
Return slowly to the start, keeping tension on the band the whole way.

backward-drag.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Forearms, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back
steps: Attach a sled to straps or a handle and hold it in front of you, facing the sled, with arms straight.
Sit into a quarter squat with your chest up and weight on your heels.
Walk backwards in short, quick steps, driving through the front of each foot and pulling the sled with you.
Keep your back flat and arms long throughout. Clear the path behind you before you start.
Stand facing away from where you will throw, holding a medicine ball at your waist. Check the space behind you is clear.
Hinge and dip into a partial squat, lowering the ball between your knees with your back flat.
Drive through your legs and hips explosively and swing the ball up and back over your head.
Let go as your arms pass overhead and let your body extend fully. Use a light ball while you learn the timing.
Place the board on a flat, clear surface near a wall or rail you can grab.
Step on with feet about hip width apart and knees soft, holding the support until you feel steady.
Let go and keep the board level by making small adjustments through your ankles, knees and hips.
Hold for a set time, looking ahead rather than down. Step off carefully when you are done.
Lie on your back with your heels on an exercise ball and arms out to the sides on the floor.
Squeeze your glutes and lift your hips so your body forms a straight line from shoulders to heels.
Keeping your hips up, pull your heels towards you, rolling the ball in until your knees are bent.
Roll it back out slowly to straight legs, still keeping your hips off the floor.

band-assisted-pull-up.muscles: Primary: Lats · Secondary: Abs, Forearms, Mid back
steps: Loop a band over a pull-up bar and pull it through itself. Place one knee or foot in the bottom loop.
Hang from the bar with hands a little wider than your shoulders, arms straight and stomach braced.
Pull your chest towards the bar by driving your elbows down until your chin clears it.
Lower yourself slowly to straight arms. Keep a hand on the band as you step out so it does not snap back.

band-good-morning.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Glutes, Lower back
steps: Stand on a band with feet hip width apart and loop the other end behind your neck, resting across your upper back.
Keep a soft bend in your knees and your back flat. Brace your stomach.
Hinge forward by pushing your hips back until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings, keeping your spine neutral.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall again, squeezing your glutes at the top.

band-good-morning-pull-through.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Glutes, Lower back
steps: Anchor a band low behind you, face away from it and hold the band between your legs with both hands.
Step forward until there is tension, set your feet a bit wider than your hips and soften your knees.
Hinge back, letting the band pull your hands back between your legs while your back stays flat.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall, squeezing your glutes. Your arms just hold on; your hips do the work.
Anchor a band low to one side and loop it around the ankle nearer the anchor. Hold something steady for balance.
Step away until the band has tension, with the banded leg out to the side.
Sweep that leg in across your body, keeping your torso upright and the leg fairly straight.
Let it return to the side slowly. Turn around to work the other leg.

band-pull-apart.muscles: Primary: Shoulders · Secondary: Mid back, Traps
steps: Hold a light band in front of you at shoulder height with straight arms and an overhand grip, hands about shoulder width apart.
Keep your ribs down and your shoulders away from your ears.
Pull the band apart by moving your hands out to the sides until it touches your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Return slowly to the start without letting the band go slack.
Lie on a bench or the floor with a band anchored low behind your head. Hold the ends with arms pointing up over your chest.
Keep your upper arms still and bend your elbows, letting your hands move back towards your forehead.
Straighten your arms against the band's pull until they are locked out again.
Move slowly in both directions, keeping your elbows pointing up rather than flaring out.

barbell-ab-rollout.muscles: Primary: Abs · Secondary: Lower back, Shoulders
steps: Load a barbell with round plates and stand behind it, feet hip width apart. Bend down and grip it about shoulder width apart.
Brace hard, tuck your pelvis slightly and roll the bar forward, letting your hips follow.
Go only as far as you can keep your lower back from sagging. Standing rollouts are very demanding, so most people build up from the knees.
Pull the bar back towards your feet with your abs, keeping your arms straight.

barbell-ab-rollout-on-knees.muscles: Primary: Abs · Secondary: Lower back, Shoulders
steps: Load a barbell with round plates and kneel behind it on a mat, gripping it about shoulder width apart with straight arms.
Brace your stomach and tuck your pelvis slightly so your lower back is flat.
Roll the bar forward slowly, extending your hips and shoulders together, until your body is nearly parallel to the floor or your back starts to arch.
Pull back to the start using your abs, breathing out as you come in.
Lie on the bench with your eyes under the bar and feet flat. Grip slightly wider than your shoulders. Set the safeties or use a spotter.
Pull your shoulder blades back and down, take a breath and brace, then unrack the bar over your shoulders.
Lower it under control to your lower chest, elbows at a moderate angle to your body rather than flared out.
Press it back up and slightly towards your face until your arms are straight. Rack it once you have finished.
Stand tall with a barbell held at thigh height, hands about shoulder width apart, palms facing forward.
Keep your elbows by your sides and curl the bar up towards your shoulders.
Squeeze your biceps at the top without letting your elbows drift forward.
Lower the bar slowly to straight arms. Keep your torso still rather than leaning back to lift it.
Set a bench to an incline and lie back on it, holding a barbell at arm's length with an underhand grip.
Let your arms hang straight down towards the floor, elbows pointing down.
Curl the bar up towards your shoulders, keeping your upper arms still.
Lower it slowly to a full stretch. Keep the weight modest as the stretched position is demanding.

barbell-deadlift.muscles: Primary: Lower back · Secondary: Calves, Forearms, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lats, Mid back, Quads, Traps
steps: Stand with the bar over your mid-foot, feet hip width apart. Hinge down and grip it just outside your legs.
Bend your knees until your shins touch the bar, flatten your back and pull the slack out of the bar. Breathe in and brace hard.
Push the floor away and stand up, keeping the bar close to your legs, finishing tall with hips locked.
Lower by pushing your hips back first, then bending your knees once the bar passes them. Reset your brace each rep.

barbell-full-squat.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back
steps: Set the bar in a rack at mid-chest height and set the safety pins just below your bottom position. Rest it across your upper back.
Step back, set your feet around shoulder width with toes slightly out. Breathe in and brace hard.
Squat down by bending your knees and hips together, knees tracking over your toes, until your hips drop below your knees.
Drive up through your whole foot, keeping your chest up, until you are standing tall. Breathe and re-brace between reps.
Sit on the floor with a padded barbell over your hips. Lie back with knees bent and feet flat, close to your glutes.
Hold the bar in place with both hands and brace your stomach.
Drive through your heels and lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower your hips back to the floor under control.
This variation lowers the bar towards your neck, so use a light weight, set the safeties and have a spotter.
Lie on a flat bench and take a grip wider than a normal bench press. Unrack the bar over your upper chest.
Lower the bar slowly with elbows flared out, stopping just above your upper chest or collarbone.
Press it back up to straight arms, keeping full control throughout.

barbell-hack-squat.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Forearms, Hamstrings
steps: Stand in front of a barbell on the floor with your heels close to it. Squat down and grip it behind you, hands shoulder width apart.
Keep your chest up, back flat and arms straight. Brace your stomach.
Stand up by driving through your feet, sliding the bar up the back of your legs.
Lower it back down by squatting, keeping your chest up. Raising your heels on small plates can help if your ankles are tight.
Sit on the floor with your upper back against a sturdy bench and a padded barbell over your hips. Plant your feet about hip width apart.
Hold the bar in place, tuck your chin slightly and brace your stomach.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your torso is parallel to the floor and your shins are vertical.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top without arching your lower back, then lower under control.
Set a bench to a moderate incline in a rack. Lie back with your feet flat and grip slightly wider than your shoulders. Use a spotter or safeties.
Pull your shoulder blades back and down, brace, and unrack the bar over your shoulders.
Lower it slowly to your upper chest, just below your collarbone, with elbows slightly tucked.
Press it back up until your arms are straight, then rack it once you have finished.
Lie on an incline bench holding a light barbell above your chest with straight arms, hands shoulder width apart.
Keeping your arms locked, let your shoulder blades sink back towards the bench.
Push the bar up by reaching your shoulders towards the ceiling, lifting your shoulder blades off the bench. Your elbows stay straight.
Lower back slowly. The movement is small and comes only from your shoulder blades.

barbell-lunge.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Set a barbell across your upper back in a rack and step out. Stand tall with feet hip width apart and brace your stomach.
Take a long step forward and lower your back knee towards the floor, keeping your torso upright.
Stop just before your back knee touches down, with your front knee over your foot.
Push through your front heel to return to standing, then switch legs. Use a lighter load until your balance is solid.

barbell-rear-delt-row.muscles: Primary: Shoulders · Secondary: Biceps, Lats, Mid back
steps: Hold a barbell with an overhand grip a bit wider than shoulder width. Hinge forward with a flat back until your torso is fairly low.
Let the bar hang at arm's length and brace your stomach.
Row the bar towards your upper chest with your elbows flared out wide, squeezing the back of your shoulders.
Lower slowly to straight arms. Keep the weight lighter than a normal row so the rear shoulders do the work.

barbell-rollout-from-bench.muscles: Primary: Abs · Secondary: Glutes, Hamstrings, Lats, Shoulders
steps: Load a barbell with round plates. Kneel on a bench, or place your knees at its edge, with the bar on the floor in front of you.
Grip the bar with straight arms and brace your stomach, tucking your pelvis slightly.
Roll the bar forward, lowering your body towards the floor while keeping your lower back flat.
Pull the bar back in using your abs. Only go as far as you can control; this is harder than a floor rollout.
Sit on a bench with the balls of your feet on a raised block or plate and a padded barbell resting across your lower thighs.
Hold the bar in place with your hands and let your heels drop to feel a stretch in your calves.
Push up onto the balls of your feet as high as you can, lifting the bar.
Pause at the top, then lower your heels slowly back down.
Take the bar from a rack at shoulder height with hands just outside your shoulders. Rest it on the front of your shoulders.
Stand tall, squeeze your glutes and brace your stomach so your lower back does not arch.
Press the bar straight up, moving your head back slightly to let it pass, then bring your head through once it clears.
Lock out overhead, then lower it back to your shoulders under control.
Stand tall holding a barbell at arm's length in front of your thighs, hands about shoulder width apart.
Keep your arms straight and your chin level.
Lift your shoulders straight up towards your ears as high as you can.
Hold briefly at the top, then lower slowly. Avoid rolling your shoulders.

barbell-shrug-behind-the-back.muscles: Primary: Traps · Secondary: Forearms, Mid back
steps: Hold a barbell behind your thighs with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder width apart. Taking it from a rack at that height helps.
Stand tall with arms straight and your stomach braced.
Lift your shoulders straight up towards your ears, feeling your upper back and traps squeeze.
Lower slowly to the start without bending your elbows.
Rest a light barbell across your upper back and stand tall with feet hip width apart.
Keep your hips still and bend directly sideways, letting one shoulder drop towards your hip.
Stop at a comfortable stretch, then use your side muscles to pull yourself back to upright.
Alternate sides. Move slowly and avoid twisting or leaning forward.

barbell-side-split-squat.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Hamstrings, Lower back
steps: Set a barbell across your upper back and stand with your feet much wider than your shoulders, toes pointing forward or slightly out.
Brace your stomach and shift your weight to one side, bending that knee while the other leg stays straight.
Sit your hips back and down until your thigh is roughly parallel, keeping your chest up and knee over your toes.
Push back up to the centre and repeat on the other side. Keep the load light at first.

barbell-squat.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back
steps: Set the bar at mid-chest height in a rack with the safety pins just below your lowest point. Rest it across your upper back.
Step back with feet about shoulder width apart and toes slightly out. Take a big breath and brace.
Squat down by bending hips and knees together, keeping your chest up and knees in line with your toes.
Drive back up through your whole foot to stand tall, re-bracing before the next rep.

barbell-squat-to-a-bench.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back
steps: Place a bench behind you at a height that puts your thighs about parallel when you sit. Set the bar across your upper back.
Stand with feet about shoulder width apart, brace your stomach and keep your chest up.
Squat down with control until you lightly touch the bench. Do not drop onto it or relax.
Drive through your feet to stand back up. Use the rack's safeties as well.

barbell-step-ups.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Quads
steps: Stand facing a sturdy box or bench with a barbell across your upper back. Choose a height where your knee is roughly level with your hip.
Place one whole foot on the box and brace your stomach.
Push through that heel to step up until you are standing tall on the box, bringing the other foot up to meet it.
Step down with control and repeat. Start light because balance is the limiting factor here.

barbell-walking-lunge.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Set a barbell across your upper back and make sure you have a clear path ahead.
Take a long step forward and lower your back knee towards the floor, keeping your chest up.
Push through your front heel and bring your back foot forward into the next step.
Keep moving forward, alternating legs, with control. Use a lighter load than you would for a static lunge.
Hold one end of the rope in each hand and step back until there is a little slack. Stand in a partial squat with a flat back.
Brace your stomach and keep your elbows soft.
Move your arms up and down quickly, either together or alternating, to send waves along the rope.
Keep breathing steadily and keep your stance stable. Keep the waves reaching the anchor end.

bear-crawl-sled-drags.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Attach a sled to a harness or straps around your waist or shoulders.
Get onto your hands and feet with your knees just off the floor and your back flat.
Crawl forward by moving opposite hand and foot together, dragging the sled behind you.
Keep your hips low and level and take short, controlled steps. Start with a light sled.
Sit on the edge of a bench with your hands next to your hips, fingers pointing forward. Walk your feet out and slide your hips off.
Keep your back close to the bench and your shoulders pulled down.
Bend your elbows to lower your body until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor, or less if your shoulders feel pinched.
Press through your palms to straighten your arms. Bend your knees to make it easier.

bench-jump.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Stand beside a low, sturdy bench with your feet together. Learn this with a small bench and easy jumps first.
Dip into a quarter squat and swing your arms back.
Jump sideways over the bench, landing softly on the balls of your feet with knees bent.
Rebound straight back over the other way, keeping each landing quiet and controlled.

bench-press-powerlifting.muscles: Primary: Triceps · Secondary: Chest, Forearms, Lats, Shoulders
steps: Lie on the bench, pull your shoulder blades together and down, and set a slight arch with your feet planted. Set safeties or use a spotter.
Grip the bar at the width you compete or train with, unrack it and settle it over your shoulders. Breathe in and brace.
Lower the bar to your lower chest with elbows slightly tucked, and pause briefly on your chest.
Drive it back up by pushing your feet into the floor, finishing with arms locked. Keep your glutes on the bench.
Attach bands from the bar to the bottom of the rack or bench legs. Set the safeties.
Lie on the bench, pull your shoulder blades back and grip slightly wider than your shoulders.
Unrack and lower the bar under control to your lower chest; the bands will lighten as you descend.
Press up forcefully, keeping the bar path steady as the band tension increases towards lockout.

bench-press-with-chains.muscles: Primary: Triceps · Secondary: Chest, Lats, Shoulders
steps: Hang chains from each end of the bar so some links rest on the floor at the bottom. Set the safeties or use a spotter.
Lie on the bench, set your shoulder blades and grip slightly wider than your shoulders.
Unrack and lower the bar to your chest under control; more chain gathers on the floor as it drops.
Press back up to lockout, staying tight as the chains lift and the load increases.

bench-sprint.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Stand facing a low, sturdy bench or step with one foot on top of it.
Push off the top foot and switch feet quickly in the air, landing with the other foot on the bench.
Pump your arms as if sprinting and stay light on the balls of your feet.
Keep switching at a steady pace. Stop if your foot placement gets careless.

bent-arm-barbell-pullover.muscles: Primary: Lats · Secondary: Chest, Lats, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Lie on a flat bench holding a barbell with a narrow grip above your chest, elbows bent.
Keep your elbows bent at a fixed angle and lower the bar back over your head towards the floor.
Go until you feel a stretch through your lats and chest, without forcing your shoulders.
Pull the bar back over your chest using your back muscles, keeping your elbows at the same angle.

bent-arm-dumbbell-pullover.muscles: Primary: Chest · Secondary: Lats, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Lie across or along a flat bench holding one dumbbell with both hands above your chest, elbows slightly bent.
Keep your hips low and stomach braced.
Lower the dumbbell back over your head in an arc until you feel a stretch through your chest and lats.
Pull it back over your chest along the same arc, keeping the elbow bend unchanged.
Lie on your back with knees bent and feet lifted, arms flat by your sides.
Press your palms into the floor and brace your stomach.
Curl your hips up off the floor, bringing your knees towards your chest.
Lower your hips slowly back down without letting your feet drop.

bent-over-barbell-row.muscles: Primary: Mid back · Secondary: Biceps, Lats, Shoulders
steps: Hold a barbell with an overhand grip just wider than shoulder width. Hinge forward with a flat back until your torso is close to parallel.
Soften your knees and brace hard to protect your lower back.
Pull the bar towards your lower ribs, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower it slowly to straight arms without letting your back round.
Set an incline bench and stand behind it. Hinge forward and rest your forehead on the top of the pad.
Hold light dumbbells hanging below your shoulders, palms facing each other.
Raise the dumbbells out to the sides with a slight bend in your elbows until your arms are about level with your torso.
Lower slowly. The head support stops you from using body swing to lift the weight.

bent-over-low-pulley-side-lateral.muscles: Primary: Shoulders · Secondary: Lower back, Mid back, Traps
steps: Stand beside a low cable pulley and hold the handle with the far hand. Hinge forward with a flat back.
Let the handle hang under your chest with a slight bend in your elbow.
Raise your arm out to the side until it is about level with your torso, squeezing the back of your shoulder.
Lower slowly and switch sides once you have finished.

bent-over-one-arm-long-bar-row.muscles: Primary: Mid back · Secondary: Biceps, Lats, Lower back, Traps
steps: Wedge one end of a barbell into a corner or landmine. Load the other end and stand beside it.
Hinge forward with a flat back and grip the bar just behind the plates with one hand.
Row the bar towards your hip, keeping your elbow close to your side and your torso still.
Lower it slowly to a straight arm, then switch sides.

bent-over-two-arm-long-bar-row.muscles: Primary: Mid back · Secondary: Biceps, Lats
steps: Wedge one end of a barbell into a corner or landmine and load the other end. Straddle the bar facing the plates.
Hinge forward with a flat back and grip the bar with both hands just behind the plates, or use a handle.
Row the bar towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower it under control to straight arms, keeping your back flat.

bent-over-two-dumbbell-row.muscles: Primary: Mid back · Secondary: Biceps, Lats, Shoulders
steps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and hinge forward with a flat back until your torso is fairly low.
Let the dumbbells hang below your shoulders, palms facing back.
Row the dumbbells up to your sides, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower them slowly to straight arms, keeping your back still.

bent-over-two-dumbbell-row-with-palms-in.muscles: Primary: Mid back · Secondary: Biceps, Lats
steps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and hinge forward with a flat back until your torso is fairly low.
Let the dumbbells hang below your shoulders with your palms facing each other.
Row them up to your ribs, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Lower slowly to straight arms without letting your back round.

bent-press.muscles: Primary: Abs · Secondary: Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back, Quads, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Clean a light kettlebell to your shoulder and turn your feet slightly away from it. This is a skill lift, so learn it very light.
Push your hip out towards the loaded side and lean your torso away and down, keeping the forearm vertical.
As you bend under it, the arm straightens and the kettlebell stays in place.
Once your arm is locked, stand back up with the bell overhead. Lower it to your shoulder with control.

board-press.muscles: Primary: Triceps · Secondary: Chest, Forearms, Lats, Shoulders
steps: Set up a bench press with safeties or a spotter. A partner holds boards on your chest, or you secure them there.
Unrack the bar with your normal grip, keep your shoulder blades back and brace.
Lower the bar to the boards, pause briefly, and keep your body tight.
Press back up to lockout. The shorter range lets you work on the top of the press.
Start in a forearm plank with your elbows under your shoulders and body in a straight line.
Brace your stomach and squeeze your glutes.
Press your palms into the floor to straighten your arms and lift your forearms, one arm or both together, into a high plank.
Lower back onto your forearms with control. Keep your hips level throughout.
Hold a bar at about waist height, such as in a rack or on a sturdy bench. Walk your feet back into a leaning plank.
Keep your body straight and your elbows pointing down.
Bend your elbows to lower your head towards and under the bar.
Press through your hands to straighten your arms. Move your feet closer to the bar to make it easier.

bodyweight-flyes.muscles: Primary: Chest · Secondary: Abs, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Place two EZ bars on the floor parallel to each other. Kneel and place one hand on each bar in a push-up position.
Brace your stomach and keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly let the bars roll apart, lowering your chest towards the floor only as far as you can control.
Squeeze your hands back together to roll the bars in and lift yourself up. Start from your knees.

bodyweight-mid-row.muscles: Primary: Mid back · Secondary: Biceps, Lats
steps: Set a bar or suspension handles at about waist height. Hang under it with arms straight and your heels on the floor.
Keep your body in a straight line from shoulders to heels and squeeze your glutes.
Pull your chest towards the bar by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower yourself slowly to straight arms. Bend your knees or raise the bar to make it easier.
Stand with feet about shoulder width apart, toes slightly out. Hold your arms in front of you for balance.
Brace your stomach and keep your chest up.
Sit your hips back and down, bending your knees in line with your toes, as low as you can with a flat back.
Push through your whole foot to stand back up.

bodyweight-walking-lunge.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Stand tall with feet hip width apart and a clear space in front of you.
Take a long step forward and lower your back knee towards the floor, keeping your chest up.
Push through your front heel and swing your back foot forward into the next step.
Keep alternating legs, moving forward with control.
Place a balance dome in front of a low cable pulley and lie back on it, dome side up, holding the handle behind your head.
Plant your feet wide for stability and brace your stomach.
Crunch your ribs up towards your hips, then lower back to a gentle stretch over the ball.
Add side bends by crunching slightly towards one side and then the other. Keep the weight light.
Stand holding a light kettlebell by the handle, hanging between your legs. Hinge slightly at the hips.
Drive your hips forward and pull the bell up close to your body.
Catch it at shoulder height upside down, base pointing up, by squeezing the handle hard with your elbow tucked.
Hold it steady briefly, then lower it back to the hang with control. Keep your face out of its path in case it tips.
Lie on your back with your legs raised straight up and arms by your sides, palms down.
Brace your stomach and press your lower back into the floor.
Lift your hips off the floor, pushing your feet towards the ceiling.
Lower your hips back down slowly without swinging your legs.

box-jump-multiple-response.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Abductors, Adductors, Calves, Glutes, Quads
steps: Set up a row of low, stable boxes or one box with space around it. Start with a small height while learning.
Stand facing the box, dip into a quarter squat and swing your arms back.
Jump onto the box, landing softly with bent knees, then step or hop down and immediately jump onto the next.
Keep a steady rhythm and stop when your landings lose control.

box-skip.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Abductors, Adductors, Calves, Glutes, Quads
steps: Stand facing a low, stable box with enough space around you.
Skip towards the box, driving one knee up and pushing off the other foot.
Land the push-off foot on top of the box, then continue the skip and land on the other side or step back down.
Keep it light and rhythmic. Learn with a very low box first.

box-squat.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Adductors, Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back
steps: Place a sturdy box behind you at a height that puts your thighs about parallel. Set the bar across your upper back and set the safeties.
Stand with a wide stance, toes slightly out, and brace hard.
Sit your hips back and down until you are seated on the box, keeping your shins fairly vertical and back flat.
Stay braced, then drive your feet into the floor and stand up without rocking.

box-squat-with-bands.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Abductors, Adductors, Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back
steps: Attach bands from the bar to the bottom of the rack. Place a box behind you and set the safeties.
Take the bar across your upper back, step back into a wide stance and brace.
Sit back onto the box under control; the band tension eases as you go down.
Drive up forcefully, keeping your chest up as the bands get tighter towards the top.

box-squat-with-chains.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Abductors, Adductors, Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back
steps: Hang chains from each end of the bar so some links rest on the floor at the bottom. Place a box behind you and set the safeties.
Take the bar across your upper back, step back into a wide stance and brace.
Sit back onto the box under control, keeping your back flat.
Stand up forcefully, staying tight as the chains lift and the load increases.
Take a light barbell from a rack at shoulder height and rest it on the front of your shoulders. Stand tall and brace.
Press the bar up just past the top of your head, without locking out.
Guide it back to rest behind your neck on your upper back, then press it back over your head to the front.
Keep the weight light because the behind-the-neck position needs good shoulder mobility.
Start in a forearm plank with your elbows under your shoulders and body straight.
Brace your stomach and lift your hips up high, forming an upside-down V.
Pause briefly, then lower back into a straight plank without letting your hips sag.
Keep moving slowly and breathe steadily.
Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, close to your glutes. Rest your arms by your sides.
Brace your stomach and press your heels into the floor.
Lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees, squeezing your glutes.
Hold briefly, then lower your hips back down slowly.
Set the seat so the handles or pads are at chest height. Sit with your back against the pad.
Grip the handles or place your forearms against the pads with a slight bend in your elbows.
Bring your arms together in front of your chest, squeezing your chest muscles.
Let your arms open slowly until you feel a stretch, without letting your shoulders roll forward.
Set the cables at chest height and stand in the middle holding one handle in each hand. Step forward into a split stance.
Hold the handles by your chest with elbows bent and brace your stomach.
Press the handles forward until your arms are nearly straight, bringing your hands close together.
Return them slowly to your chest, feeling a stretch across your chest.
Set both pulleys high and hold a handle in each hand. Step forward into a split stance and lean slightly forward.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and your arms wide.
Pull the handles down and together in front of your hips or chest, squeezing your chest.
Let your arms open back out slowly until you feel a stretch.
Attach a rope to a high pulley. Kneel facing the stack and hold the rope by your head.
Keep your hips still and brace your stomach.
Crunch your ribs down towards your hips, rounding your upper back.
Pause, then let your torso rise slowly back up while keeping tension on the cable.

cable-deadlifts.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Forearms, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back
steps: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and stand facing the stack, feet hip width apart.
Hinge down with a flat back and grip the bar.
Drive through your legs and hips to stand up tall, keeping the bar close to your body.
Lower it back down by hinging at the hips, keeping your back flat.
Attach a rope to a low pulley and stand facing it, holding one end in each hand with palms facing each other.
Keep your elbows by your sides and stand tall.
Curl the rope up towards your shoulders, keeping your palms facing inward.
Lower it slowly to straight arms without letting your elbows move forward.
Attach an ankle strap to a low pulley. Stand side-on to the stack with the strap on your inside ankle.
Hold the machine for balance and let the strapped leg drift out towards the pulley.
Pull that leg in across the front of your standing leg, keeping it fairly straight.
Let it return slowly. Turn around to work the other side.
Place an incline bench in front of a high pulley, facing away from it. Lie back and hold a straight bar attached to the cable above your head.
Keep your arms straight with a slight bend in your elbows.
Pull the bar down in an arc towards your thighs, using your lats.
Let it return slowly to the start above your head.
Place an incline bench in front of a low pulley, with the pulley behind the top of the bench. Lie back and hold a bar or rope above your head.
Point your elbows up and keep your upper arms still.
Straighten your arms to extend the bar forward and up.
Bend your elbows slowly to lower the bar back behind your head.
Set a handle at elbow height. Stand side-on to the stack with the handle in the hand nearer to it.
Bend your elbow to 90 degrees and tuck it into your side. A small rolled towel under the arm can help.
Rotate your forearm across your stomach, keeping your elbow pinned to your side.
Return slowly. Use a light weight and switch sides.
Set both pulleys high. Stand in the middle holding the handles with arms out wide.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and brace your stomach.
Pull your arms down and in towards your hips in a wide arc.
Let your arms rise back out to the sides slowly.
Attach a rope to a low or mid pulley. Stand side-on to it, holding the rope with both hands.
Brace your stomach and pivot your back foot.
Rotate your torso and pull the rope across and up over your shoulder, as if throwing someone.
Return slowly to the start. Keep the weight moderate and switch sides.
Lie on a bench or the floor with your head near a low pulley. Hold a straight bar or rope above your chest.
Point your elbows up and keep your upper arms still.
Bend your elbows to lower the bar back towards your forehead.
Straighten your arms to press it back up.
Attach a handle to a high pulley. Stand facing the stack and hold it with one hand, palm facing down or in.
Tuck your elbow into your side and keep your upper arm still.
Push the handle down until your arm is straight.
Let it rise slowly until your forearm is roughly level, then switch arms once you are done.
Place a preacher bench in front of a low pulley. Sit with your arms over the pad, holding a bar with an underhand grip.
Keep your upper arms flat against the pad.
Curl the bar up towards your shoulders, squeezing your biceps.
Lower it slowly until your arms are almost straight, keeping tension on the cable.
Set both pulleys at about shoulder height. Stand between them and cross your arms, holding the opposite cable in each hand.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and step back to create tension.
Pull your arms out and back in a wide arc until they are in line with your body.
Return slowly. Keep your shoulders down and let the rear shoulders do the work.
Attach an ankle strap to a low pulley. Lie on your back with your feet towards the stack and the strap around your ankles.
Bend your knees and press your lower back into the floor. Hold something behind your head if needed.
Curl your knees towards your chest, lifting your hips slightly off the floor.
Lower slowly back to the start, keeping control of the cable.
Attach a rope to a pulley at about head height. Face away from it, holding the rope behind your head.
Step forward into a split stance and lean slightly forward. Point your elbows forward.
Straighten your arms forward and slightly up until they are locked.
Bend your elbows slowly to return behind your head, keeping your upper arms still.

cable-rope-rear-delt-rows.muscles: Primary: Shoulders · Secondary: Biceps, Mid back
steps: Attach a rope to a pulley at about shoulder height. Hold the ends with an overhand grip.
Step back until your arms are straight, and brace your stomach.
Pull the rope towards your face, flaring your elbows out wide and squeezing the back of your shoulders.
Return slowly to straight arms.
Set a handle at chest height. Stand side-on to the stack, holding it with both hands and arms extended.
Brace your stomach and keep your hips facing forward.
Rotate your torso away from the stack, keeping your arms straight.
Return slowly. Switch sides once you have finished.
Attach a rope to a high pulley and sit on a bench facing away from it, holding the rope by your head.
Plant your feet and brace your stomach.
Crunch your ribs towards your hips, rounding your upper back.
Return slowly, keeping tension on the cable.

cable-seated-lateral-raise.muscles: Primary: Shoulders · Secondary: Mid back, Traps
steps: Sit on a bench between two low pulleys with a handle in each hand, arms by your sides.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and brace your stomach.
Raise your arms out to the sides to about shoulder height.
Lower slowly without shrugging your shoulders.
Sit or stand between two low pulleys with a handle in each hand at shoulder height.
Brace your stomach and keep your ribs down.
Press the handles up overhead until your arms are nearly straight.
Lower them slowly back to your shoulders.
Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and stand close, holding the bar in front of your thighs.
Keep your arms straight and your chin level.
Lift your shoulders straight up towards your ears as high as you can.
Hold briefly, then lower slowly.
Attach a straight bar to a low pulley. Kneel or sit and rest your forearms on a bench or your thighs, palms up.
Let your wrists hang off the edge with the bar in your fingers.
Curl your wrists up as far as possible, squeezing your forearms.
Lower slowly to a stretch.
Stand in a standing calf-raise machine with the pads on your shoulders and feet flat on the platform.
Stand tall with arms relaxed and your knees soft.
Lift your shoulders straight up against the pads as high as you can.
Hold briefly, then lower slowly. Keep your heels down so your calves stay out of it.
Sit in a leg press machine and place the balls of your feet on the bottom edge of the platform, heels hanging off.
Straighten your legs with a slight bend in your knees and release the safeties.
Push the platform away by pointing your toes as far as you can.
Let your heels lower slowly to a full stretch, then press again. Re-engage the safeties when finished.
Sit in the leg press with your back flat on the pad. Put only the balls of your feet on the bottom edge of the platform, heels hanging off.
Press the platform out until your legs are straight but not locked, and leave the safety catches engaged if the machine allows.
Let your heels drop towards you slowly so your calves stretch, keeping your knees still.
Push through the balls of your feet to extend the ankles as far as they go, squeeze briefly, then lower under control.
Stand with the balls of one or both feet on the handle of a dumbbell laid on the floor, or on a plate resting on it, heels on the ground behind.
Hold a wall or rack for balance so the calves do the work, not your sense of balance.
Rise up onto your toes as high as you can, keeping your knees straight but soft.
Pause at the top, then lower your heels slowly back to the floor for a full stretch.
Stand on the middle of a resistance band with the balls of your feet, and hold the ends at your shoulders or loop them over your shoulders.
Stand tall with your knees straight but soft and your weight over the front of your feet.
Push up onto your toes as high as you can against the band's tension.
Hold for a moment at the top, then lower your heels slowly to the floor.

car-deadlift.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Forearms, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back, Traps
steps: Step into the frame so the handles sit beside your legs, feet about hip-width, and grip the handles firmly.
Sit your hips down, chest up and back flat, then take a big breath and brace your stomach hard.
Drive through the whole foot and stand up, keeping your arms straight and hips and shoulders rising together.
Finish tall without leaning back, then lower the frame under control by bending hips and knees. Learn it light first.
Stand tall holding a weight plate by its edges at roughly ten and two o'clock, arms straight out in front at shoulder height.
Brace your stomach and keep your shoulders down away from your ears.
Turn the plate slowly one way as far as is comfortable, as if steering a wheel, keeping your arms straight and level.
Turn back through the centre to the other side, and keep going side to side without letting the plate drop.

carioca-quick-step.muscles: Primary: Adductors · Secondary: Abs, Abductors, Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Quads
steps: Stand side-on to the direction you want to travel, on the balls of your feet with knees slightly bent and arms loose.
Cross your trailing foot quickly in front of your lead foot, then step the lead foot out to the side again.
Next cross the trailing foot behind, then step the lead foot out, letting your hips twist while your shoulders stay facing forwards.
Keep the steps short and fast along the line, then turn around and lead with the other side.

catch-and-overhead-throw.muscles: Primary: Lats · Secondary: Abs, Chest, Shoulders
steps: Stand facing a partner or a solid wall, feet shoulder-width apart, hands up ready to catch a medicine ball above your head.
Catch the ball overhead and let it carry your arms slightly back, keeping your stomach braced and not arching your lower back.
Straight away, snap your arms and trunk forwards and throw the ball back with both hands, releasing above your head.
Reset your stance between throws and start with a light ball until the rhythm feels smooth.
Lie on a flat bench with chain handles (or another loaded handle) held above your chest, arms straight and palms facing each other.
Keep your upper arms still and angled slightly back towards your head.
Bend only at the elbows to lower the handles beside your head until your forearms are about level.
Straighten your elbows to press back to the start, squeezing the backs of your arms.
Hang chains on each end of the bar so some links rest on the floor at the bottom, then lie on the bench with eyes under the bar. Use safeties or a spotter.
Plant your feet, pull your shoulder blades together and grip the bar just outside shoulder-width. Unrack it over your chest.
Lower the bar under control to your lower chest; the load lightens as the chains pile onto the floor.
Press back up to straight arms as the chains lift and the load builds. Rack the bar when done.

chair-squat.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Stand in front of a sturdy chair or seat with feet about shoulder-width apart, toes turned slightly out. Hold a handle for support if needed.
Push your hips back and bend your knees, keeping your chest up and knees tracking over your toes.
Sit back until you lightly touch the seat without dropping onto it.
Drive through your whole foot to stand back up tall, squeezing your glutes at the top.

chest-push-from-3-point-stance.muscles: Primary: Chest · Secondary: Abs, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Get into a three-point stance: feet staggered, hips low, one hand on the ground and the other holding a medicine ball against your chest.
Explode forwards off both feet, bringing both hands onto the ball as your body rises.
Push the ball hard straight out from your chest, extending your arms fully as you drive forwards.
Follow the throw with a few steps to slow down, then reset. Start with a light ball.

chest-push-multiple-response.muscles: Primary: Chest · Secondary: Abs, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Stand or kneel facing a partner or solid wall, holding a medicine ball at your chest with elbows out.
Push the ball away fast by straightening your arms, finishing with thumbs pointing down.
Catch the return with soft hands, let it come back to your chest, then push it away again straight away.
Keep your stomach braced and the rhythm quick, and use a light ball so you can catch it safely.

chest-push-single-response.muscles: Primary: Chest · Secondary: Abs, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Stand or kneel tall facing an open space, a partner or a wall, with a medicine ball held at your chest and elbows out.
Brace your stomach and load up by drawing the ball in slightly.
Throw the ball as hard as you can straight out from your chest, fully extending your arms.
Let the ball go, reset your position fully, and treat each throw as one maximal effort.

chest-push-with-run-release.muscles: Primary: Chest · Secondary: Abs, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Stand in an athletic stance with a medicine ball at your chest, knees bent and weight on the balls of your feet.
Lean forwards and push the ball out hard from your chest as you start to fall into a run.
Let your arms extend fully on the release, then sprint a few strides after the ball.
Use a clear, open space and a light ball, then walk back and reset before the next one.

chin-up.muscles: Primary: Lats · Secondary: Biceps, Forearms, Mid back
steps: Grip the bar with palms facing you, hands about shoulder-width apart, and hang with straight arms.
Pull your shoulders down and back slightly, and brace your stomach so your legs don't swing.
Pull yourself up by driving your elbows down towards your ribs until your chin clears the bar.
Lower yourself slowly all the way back to straight arms before the next pull.

circus-bell.muscles: Primary: Shoulders · Secondary: Forearms, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back, Traps, Triceps
steps: Stand over the circus dumbbell with feet hip-width apart. Grip the handle with your working hand; your free hand can help steady the bell.
With a flat back and braced stomach, lift and clean the bell to your shoulder, using your legs and hips; the free hand may assist.
Settle it on the shoulder, dip slightly at the knees, then drive up and press the bell overhead to a locked arm.
Hold it steady overhead, then lower it to the shoulder and back to the floor with control. Practise light and in a clear space.

clean.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Calves, Forearms, Glutes, Lower back, Quads, Shoulders, Traps
steps: Stand with the bar over your mid-foot, feet hip-width apart. Grip just outside your knees with a flat back, chest up and shoulders over the bar.
Push the floor away to lift the bar, keeping it close to your legs, until it passes your knees.
Drive your hips forwards and extend hard through ankles, knees and hips, then shrug and pull yourself under the bar.
Catch it on the front of your shoulders with elbows high in a squat, then stand up. Learn with light weights or a coach.

clean-deadlift.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Forearms, Glutes, Lower back, Mid back, Quads, Traps
steps: Set up as for a clean: bar over mid-foot, hip-width stance, grip just outside your knees, back flat and chest up.
Take a breath and brace, then push the floor away so your hips and shoulders rise together.
Keep the bar close, sweeping it back towards you, with shoulders over the bar as it passes your knees.
Stand fully tall at the top, then lower the bar along the same path under control.

clean-pull.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Forearms, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back, Traps
steps: Set up as for a clean: bar over mid-foot, hands just outside your knees, back flat, chest up and shoulders slightly in front of the bar.
Brace and push the floor away, keeping the bar close as it rises past your knees.
Once it reaches mid-thigh, extend ankles, knees and hips explosively and finish with a strong shrug, arms still straight.
Let the bar come back down to your thighs, then lower it to the floor with a flat back. Learn it light first.
Stand tall holding the bar at your thighs with a clean-width grip, feet hip-width apart.
Bend slightly at the hips and knees so the bar sits at mid-thigh, back flat and shoulders just over the bar.
Drive up through your legs and shrug your shoulders towards your ears in one fast movement, keeping your arms straight.
Lower the shoulders and return the bar to your thighs under control, then reset.

clean-and-jerk.muscles: Primary: Shoulders · Secondary: Abs, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back, Quads, Traps, Triceps
steps: Clean the bar from the floor to your shoulders: pull it close, extend hips hard, drop under and catch it on your shoulders, then stand up.
Reset your grip and breathe. Brace your stomach with elbows slightly in front of the bar.
Dip straight down a few inches, then drive up hard and push yourself under the bar, splitting your feet as your arms lock out overhead.
Step the front foot back and the back foot forward to stand still with the bar overhead. Learn this with light loads and a coach.

clean-and-press.muscles: Primary: Shoulders · Secondary: Abs, Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back, Mid back, Quads, Shoulders, Traps, Triceps
steps: Stand with the bar over mid-foot, grip just outside your knees, back flat and chest up.
Pull the bar up close to your body, extend your hips hard and catch it on the front of your shoulders, knees soft.
Stand tall, brace your stomach and squeeze your glutes, then press the bar straight overhead, moving your head back out of its path.
Lower it to your shoulders, then to your thighs and the floor under control. Start light while learning the clean.

clean-from-blocks.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Shoulders, Traps
steps: Set the bar on blocks at about knee height or just above. Stand close with a clean grip, back flat and shoulders slightly over the bar.
Brace, then extend ankles, knees and hips explosively, keeping the bar close to your thighs.
Shrug and pull yourself under, catching the bar on the front of your shoulders with elbows high in a squat.
Stand up tall, then return the bar to the blocks. Learn with light weights first.
Start in a push-up position: hands a little wider than shoulders, body in a straight line from head to heels.
Do one push-up, lowering your chest under control and pressing back up.
Walk your hands a small step round to one side, as if moving round a clock face, with your feet as the centre.
Push up again at each new spot, working round and then back the other way. Keep your stomach tight throughout.
Lie on the bench with eyes under the bar and grip it about shoulder-width or slightly narrower. Set safeties or have a spotter.
Plant your feet, draw your shoulder blades back, and unrack the bar over your chest.
Lower it to your lower chest, keeping your elbows tucked close to your sides.
Press back up to straight arms, driving with your triceps, then rack when done.
Lie on a flat bench holding two dumbbells above your chest, palms facing each other and the dumbbells touching.
Keep the dumbbells pressed together and your elbows close to your body.
Lower them slowly to the middle of your chest.
Press back up to straight arms, keeping them together and squeezing the backs of your arms.
Attach a band to the EZ bar and anchor or stand on it so it pulls down. Hold the bar on the inner angled grips, palms up.
Stand tall with elbows at your sides and knees soft.
Curl the bar up towards your shoulders without swinging; the band gets harder towards the top.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly against the band's pull to straight arms.
Lie on a flat bench holding an EZ bar on the inner grips, arms straight above your chest.
Plant your feet and keep your shoulder blades drawn back.
Lower the bar to your lower chest with your elbows tucked close to your sides.
Press back up to straight arms, feeling it in the backs of your arms.
Stand tall holding the EZ bar on its inner angled grips, palms facing up and arms straight.
Pin your elbows to your sides and keep your torso still.
Curl the bar up towards your shoulders, moving only at the elbows.
Squeeze briefly, then lower slowly back to straight arms.

close-grip-front-lat-pulldown.muscles: Primary: Lats · Secondary: Biceps, Mid back, Shoulders
steps: Sit at the pulldown with thighs under the pads. Take a close grip on the bar or a narrow handle.
Lean back slightly, chest up, arms straight and shoulders pulled down away from your ears.
Pull the handle down to your upper chest, driving your elbows down and back.
Pause, then let it rise slowly until your arms are straight again.

close-grip-push-up-off-of-a-dumbbell.muscles: Primary: Triceps · Secondary: Abs, Chest, Shoulders
steps: Stand a dumbbell on its end or lay it on its side so it won't roll, and place both hands on it close together.
Walk your feet back into a push-up position with a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your chest towards the dumbbell, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Press back up to straight arms, keeping your stomach tight and hips level.
Stand tall holding a barbell with palms up and hands a little closer than shoulder-width.
Keep your elbows at your sides and your knees soft.
Curl the bar up towards your shoulders without leaning back or swinging.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly to straight arms.
Lie on your back with legs straight and arms stretched out on the floor behind your head.
Brace your stomach and press your lower back gently towards the floor.
At the same time, bring your knees towards your chest and sweep your arms over to meet them as your upper back lifts.
Uncurl slowly until you are lying long again without letting your feet or arms crash down.

conans-wheel.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Abs, Biceps, Calves, Forearms, Lower back, Shoulders, Traps
steps: Set the loaded arm at a height where you can hug it in the crook of your elbows, close to your chest.
Squat down, hug the bar tightly, brace your stomach and stand up with it, back flat.
Walk forwards round the circle in short, steady steps, keeping your chest up and the load tight to your body.
Lower the bar with control by bending at the knees when you stop. Start light and clear the area around the wheel.
Sit on the end of a bench, feet wide, and hold a dumbbell in one hand.
Rest the back of that upper arm against the inside of the same-side thigh, arm hanging straight.
Curl the dumbbell up towards your shoulder, moving only at the elbow.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly to a straight arm. Switch arms.
Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hands lightly behind your head.
Curl your shoulders off the floor and twist to bring one elbow towards the opposite knee, lifting that knee to meet it.
Squeeze through your side, keeping your neck relaxed rather than pulling on your head.
Lower back down under control and repeat to the other side.
Stand tall holding dumbbells at your sides, palms facing your thighs.
Keeping that neutral grip, curl one dumbbell up and across your body towards the opposite shoulder.
Pause near the top, keeping your upper arm close to your body.
Lower it slowly back to your side, then curl the other arm.
Anchor a band behind you at chest height, or wrap it around a post, and hold one end in each hand.
Step forwards until there's tension, arms out to your sides with a slight bend in the elbows.
In a wide hugging arc, bring your hands to meet in front of your chest, keeping the elbow bend fixed.
Let your arms open back out slowly until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Stand tall holding a weight in each hand, feet hip-width apart and stomach braced.
Raise both arms straight out to the sides until they are level with your shoulders.
Hold that position with straight arms and your shoulders down, breathing steadily.
When you can no longer keep your arms level, lower the weights under control. Start light.
Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, arms stretched straight up beyond your head, hands together.
Keep your arms in line with your ears throughout.
Curl your shoulders and upper back off the floor by tightening your stomach.
Pause briefly, then lower slowly back down.
Lie on your back with your calves resting on top of an exercise ball, knees and hips bent to about a right angle.
Place your hands lightly beside your head or across your chest.
Curl your shoulders off the floor, bringing your ribs towards your hips, while keeping the ball still.
Lower back down slowly, keeping your stomach engaged.
Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat, and hands lightly behind your head or across your chest.
Tighten your stomach and curl your shoulders and upper back off the floor.
Keep your lower back on the floor and your neck relaxed, looking slightly up.
Lower back down slowly before starting the next one.
Stand holding light dumbbells at your thighs, palms facing you.
Pull them up with elbows leading until your upper arms are level with your shoulders, like an upright row.
Keeping the elbows in place, rotate your forearms up so the dumbbells point to the ceiling.
Press them overhead, then reverse each step to lower. Use light weights; this is about control.
Lie on your back with arms reaching straight up and knees bent at a right angle above your hips.
Press your lower back gently into the floor and brace your stomach.
Slowly lower one arm behind your head and straighten the opposite leg towards the floor, without letting your back arch.
Bring them back to the start and repeat on the other side, breathing out as you reach.

deadlift-with-bands.muscles: Primary: Lower back · Secondary: Forearms, Glutes, Hamstrings, Mid back, Quads, Traps
steps: Anchor bands to the platform or a loaded bar holder and loop them over the bar ends. Stand with the bar over mid-foot.
Grip just outside your legs, push your hips back, flatten your back and take a big breath to brace.
Push the floor away and stand up, keeping the bar close; the band pull increases towards the top.
Lock out with hips and knees straight, then lower the bar under control along your legs.

deadlift-with-chains.muscles: Primary: Lower back · Secondary: Forearms, Glutes, Hamstrings, Mid back, Quads, Traps
steps: Hang chains from each end of the bar so they bunch on the floor at the start. Stand with the bar over mid-foot.
Grip just outside your legs, set a flat back and take a big breath to brace your stomach.
Drive through your feet and stand up, keeping the bar close as the chains lift and add weight.
Finish tall, then lower the bar under control back to the floor.
Hook your legs under the pads of a decline bench and lie back with eyes under the bar. Have a spotter or use safeties.
Grip slightly wider than shoulders, draw your shoulder blades back and unrack the bar over your chest.
Lower it slowly to your lower chest.
Press back up to straight arms, then rack carefully before sitting up.
Lie on a decline bench with legs secured, holding a barbell with a close grip above your chest. A spotter helps here.
Lower the bar to your lower chest with elbows tucked, then press it back up.
From the top, bend only at the elbows to lower the bar towards your forehead, keeping upper arms still.
Extend your elbows to lock out again. Alternate the two parts under control.
Hook your feet under the pads of a decline bench and lie back, hands lightly beside your head or across your chest.
Curl your shoulders and upper back up towards your hips by tightening your stomach.
Stop once your upper back is off the bench, without yanking on your neck.
Lower back slowly until your shoulders almost touch the bench.
Hook your legs under the pads of a decline bench and lie back with a dumbbell held on each side of your lower chest.
Press the dumbbells up until your arms are straight above your chest.
Lower them slowly to the sides of your lower chest, elbows at a comfortable angle.
Press back up. When done, bring them to your chest before sitting up carefully.
Lie on a decline bench with legs secured, dumbbells held above your chest, palms facing each other.
Set a slight bend in your elbows and keep it fixed throughout.
Open your arms out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Bring the dumbbells back together above you in the same arc, squeezing your chest.
Lie on a decline bench with legs secured, holding dumbbells above your chest, palms facing each other.
Keep your upper arms still and angled slightly back towards your head.
Bend at the elbows to lower the dumbbells beside your head.
Straighten your arms to bring them back up, feeling the backs of your arms work.
Lie on a decline bench with legs secured, holding an EZ bar on the inner grips above your chest.
Keep your upper arms still, tilted slightly back towards your head.
Bend at the elbows to lower the bar slowly towards your forehead.
Extend your elbows to press it back up, squeezing your triceps.
Hook your feet under the pads of a decline bench and lie back, hands lightly beside your head.
Curl your upper back off the bench and twist so one shoulder moves towards the opposite knee.
Squeeze through your side, then lower back down under control.
Repeat twisting to the other side, keeping your neck relaxed.
Put your feet on a bench or box behind you and your hands on the floor a little wider than your shoulders.
Hold a straight line from head to heels with your stomach and glutes tight.
Lower your chest towards the floor under control.
Push back up to straight arms without letting your hips sag.
Lie on a decline bench with your head at the high end, holding the bench behind your head.
Bend your knees and lift them so your thighs are upright.
Curl your hips up off the bench, bringing your knees towards your chest by tightening your stomach.
Lower your hips slowly back down without letting your legs swing.
Set a decline bench under the Smith machine so the bar lines up with your lower chest, and set the safety stops.
Lie back with legs secured and grip the bar slightly wider than shoulders, then twist it off the hooks.
Lower the bar slowly to your lower chest.
Press back up to straight arms, and twist the bar back onto the hooks when finished.

deficit-deadlift.muscles: Primary: Lower back · Secondary: Forearms, Glutes, Hamstrings, Mid back, Quads, Traps
steps: Stand on a stable plate or low platform with the bar over mid-foot. The extra height increases the range, so use lighter loads.
Bend down and grip just outside your legs, hips low, back flat and chest up. Breathe in and brace.
Push the floor away and stand up, keeping the bar close to your legs.
Lock out tall, then lower the bar under control back to the floor.

depth-jump-leap.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Abductors, Adductors, Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Stand on the edge of a low box with toes near the edge. Start low and keep plenty of clear space in front.
Step off, don't jump off, and land on both feet with knees bent and soft.
As soon as you land, spring forwards and upwards as far as you can, swinging your arms.
Land softly on both feet with knees over toes, then walk back and reset.
Adjust the seat so the handles sit just below your shoulders when you start. Sit with your back against the pad.
Grip the handles with elbows bent and tucked close to your sides.
Press the handles down until your arms are straight, without shrugging your shoulders.
Let the handles rise slowly back up to the start.
Grip parallel bars and lift yourself up to straight arms, then lean your torso forward slightly with legs bent behind you.
Let your elbows flare a little as you lower yourself slowly.
Go down until you feel a stretch across your chest, usually with upper arms about level. Stay within a comfortable range.
Press back up to straight arms, keeping the forward lean.
Grip parallel bars and push up to straight arms, keeping your body as upright as you can.
Keep your elbows pointing back and close to your sides.
Lower yourself slowly until your upper arms are roughly level with the bars, or a little higher if your shoulders prefer.
Press back up to straight arms, feeling it in the backs of your arms.
Stand with the balls of your feet on a step or block, then hinge forward at the hips and support your upper body on a bench or rail.
Keep a flat back and straight knees; the load sits over your hips on a machine pad or weight belt.
Rise up onto your toes as high as you can.
Pause, then lower your heels slowly below the step for a full stretch.

double-kettlebell-alternating-hang-clean.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Biceps, Calves, Forearms, Glutes, Lower back, Quads, Traps
steps: Hold a kettlebell in each hand, arms hanging, then hinge so the bells sit just above your knees with a flat back.
Drive your hips forward to clean one bell to the rack position at your shoulder, letting it roll round your wrist rather than flip.
Lower that bell back to the hang as you clean the other one up.
Keep alternating smoothly with a braced stomach. Learn it with light bells first.

double-kettlebell-jerk.muscles: Primary: Shoulders · Secondary: Calves, Quads, Triceps
steps: Hold two kettlebells in the rack position at your shoulders, elbows tucked, feet about hip-width.
Dip a few inches by bending your knees, then drive up hard to launch the bells upwards.
Drop into a second quick dip as your arms lock out overhead, then stand up straight with the bells locked above you.
Bring them back to the rack with control, absorbing through your knees. Learn it light with plenty of room.

double-kettlebell-push-press.muscles: Primary: Shoulders · Secondary: Calves, Quads, Triceps
steps: Hold two kettlebells in the rack position at your shoulders, feet about hip-width, stomach braced.
Dip a few inches by bending your knees, keeping your chest up.
Drive up through your legs and use that momentum to press both bells overhead to locked arms.
Lower them back to the rack under control, bending your knees slightly to cushion the catch.

double-kettlebell-snatch.muscles: Primary: Shoulders · Secondary: Glutes, Hamstrings, Quads
steps: Stand with two kettlebells between your feet, hinge down with a flat back and grip both handles.
Hike them back between your legs, then drive your hips forward hard so the bells float up close to your body.
As they rise, punch your hands through so the bells turn over softly onto your forearms, arms locked overhead.
Drop them back down in a controlled arc into the next swing. Learn it light before going heavy.

double-kettlebell-windmill.muscles: Primary: Abs · Secondary: Glutes, Hamstrings, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Press one kettlebell overhead and hold the other in the opposite hand, hanging down. Turn your feet slightly away from the top bell.
Keep your eyes on the top bell and your arm locked straight up.
Push your hip out to the side of the top bell and hinge down, sliding the lower bell towards your front foot.
Go only as far as you can with a flat back, then stand back up by driving your hips through. Start light.

double-leg-butt-kick.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Abductors, Adductors, Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees slightly bent and arms ready to swing.
Jump straight up, swinging your arms, and kick both heels up towards your backside.
Bring your feet back down underneath you before you land.
Land softly on the balls of your feet with knees bent, reset, and go again.
Lie face down with your hips over an exercise ball and your hands on the floor in front of you.
Walk your hands out slightly so the ball supports your hips and thighs.
Squeeze your glutes and lift your straight legs until your body forms a line from head to heels.
Hold the position steadily, breathing normally, then lower your feet to the floor.
Stand tall holding a barbell with palms up, hands about shoulder-width, bar against your thighs.
Curl the bar up while pulling your elbows back, so the bar slides up the front of your body.
Stop when the bar is at your lower chest, with your elbows behind you.
