Lower it back down along your body under control.
Set two low boxes or plates just wider than your shoulders and start in a push-up position with hands on them.
Lift your hands off and drop them to the floor between the boxes, landing with soft, bent elbows.
As soon as your hands land, push explosively so your hands leave the floor and return to the boxes.
Keep your body in a straight line throughout. Start with very low boxes.
Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing forwards.
Keep your elbows at your sides and your torso still.
Curl one dumbbell up towards your shoulder, then lower it slowly.
Repeat with the other arm, alternating without swinging.
Sit on a flat bench with dumbbells on your thighs, then lie back and bring them to the sides of your chest.
Plant your feet and draw your shoulder blades back and down.
Press the dumbbells up until your arms are straight above your chest.
Lower them slowly to the sides of your chest, elbows at a comfortable angle, and press again.
Lie on a flat bench holding dumbbells at the sides of your chest, palms facing each other.
Plant your feet and keep your shoulder blades set back.
Press the dumbbells up until your arms are straight, keeping palms facing in.
Lower them slowly back to your chest with elbows close to your sides.
Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing forwards.
Keep your elbows pinned to your sides.
Curl both dumbbells up towards your shoulders without swinging your body.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly to straight arms.

dumbbell-clean.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Calves, Forearms, Glutes, Lower back, Quads, Shoulders, Traps
steps: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, feet hip-width apart.
Hinge at the hips with a flat back so the dumbbells reach just above your knees.
Drive your hips forward and extend your legs explosively, pulling the dumbbells up close to your body.
Drop slightly and catch them on your shoulders, then stand tall. Start light while you learn it.
Lie on the floor with knees bent, holding dumbbells above your chest.
Lower them slowly until the backs of your upper arms lightly touch the floor.
Pause briefly without relaxing your arms.
Press back up to straight arms, driving through your triceps.
Lie on a flat bench holding dumbbells above your chest, palms facing each other.
Bend your elbows slightly and keep that bend fixed throughout.
Open your arms out wide in an arc until you feel a stretch across your chest, stopping around shoulder level.
Bring the dumbbells back together along the same arc, squeezing your chest.

dumbbell-incline-row.muscles: Primary: Mid back · Secondary: Biceps, Forearms, Lats, Shoulders
steps: Set a bench to a low incline and lie face down on it, holding a dumbbell in each hand with arms hanging.
Keep your chest on the pad and your neck in line with your back.
Row the dumbbells up towards your lower ribs, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower them slowly until your arms are straight again.
Lie on an incline bench holding dumbbells straight above your shoulders, arms locked.
Keeping your arms straight, reach the dumbbells towards the ceiling so your shoulder blades lift off the bench.
Pause briefly at the top of the reach.
Let your shoulder blades sink back to the bench slowly, keeping your arms straight.

dumbbell-lunges.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Take a long step forwards and lower your back knee towards the floor, keeping your front knee over your foot.
Stop just before your back knee touches, with your torso upright.
Push through your front foot to return to standing, then switch legs.
Lie on your side on a flat bench, holding a dumbbell in your top hand with arm hanging down in front of you.
Keep a slight bend in your elbow.
Raise the dumbbell up and back until your arm is roughly level with your shoulder, leading with the elbow.
Lower it slowly back down. Switch sides when done.
Lie on a bench or the floor with your upper arm supported and forearm pointing up, holding one end of a dumbbell with the weight above your hand.
Start with your palm facing in or slightly up.
Rotate your forearm so your palm turns downward, controlling the weight as it tips.
Rotate slowly back to the start. Use a light weight; this is a small joint.
Lie face down on a flat or slightly inclined bench, holding dumbbells with arms hanging.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and your chest on the pad.
Raise the dumbbells out to your sides until your arms are roughly level with your shoulders.
Lower them slowly, keeping the movement controlled.
Lie on a bench or the floor with your upper arm supported and forearm pointing up, holding one end of a dumbbell.
Start with your palm facing down or slightly in.
Rotate your forearm so your palm turns upward, keeping your elbow still.
Return slowly to the start. Use a light weight.
Stand or sit tall with a dumbbell held at one shoulder, palm facing forwards or in.
Brace your stomach and squeeze your glutes to stop yourself leaning.
Press the dumbbell straight up until your arm is locked out overhead.
Lower it slowly back to your shoulder. Switch arms.
Stand or sit tall holding a dumbbell in one hand, arm straight overhead.
Keep your upper arm close to your head and still.
Bend at the elbow to lower the dumbbell behind your head.
Straighten your arm back to the top. Switch arms.
Stand tall with a dumbbell in one hand in front of your thigh, palm facing you.
Lead with your elbow and pull the dumbbell up along your body.
Stop when your elbow is about level with your shoulder, or lower if that feels uncomfortable.
Lower it slowly back to your thigh. Switch arms.
Set a bench to an incline and lie face down on it, holding dumbbells with arms hanging straight down.
Keep your upper arms still and pointing to the floor.
Curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly to straight arms.
Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs, palms facing you.
Lead with your elbows and raise the dumbbells up close to your body.
Stop around chest height, with elbows no higher than your shoulders.
Lower them slowly back to your thighs.

dumbbell-rear-lunge.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Stand tall holding dumbbells at your sides.
Step one foot back and lower your back knee towards the floor.
Keep your front knee over your foot and your torso upright.
Push through your front foot to step back up to standing, then switch legs.
Stand tall with dumbbells at your sides, thumbs pointing forwards.
Raise your arms up and slightly forwards, at about a 30-degree angle from your sides.
Stop at shoulder height, keeping your shoulders down away from your ears.
Lower slowly back down. Use light weights.

dumbbell-seated-box-jump.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Sit on a low bench or box facing a second box, holding light dumbbells at your sides.
Keep your feet flat on the floor and your chest up.
Stand up explosively and jump straight onto the box in front, landing softly with bent knees.
Step down carefully, never jump down, and sit back down to reset. Start with a low box.
Sit on a bench with the ball of one foot on a step or plate, and rest a dumbbell on that thigh near the knee.
Hold the dumbbell steady with your hand.
Raise your heel as high as you can, pushing through the ball of your foot.
Lower your heel slowly for a full stretch. Switch legs.
Sit or stand tall with dumbbells at shoulder height, palms facing forwards.
Brace your stomach and keep your back neutral.
Press the dumbbells up until your arms are straight overhead.
Lower them slowly back to your shoulders.
Stand tall with dumbbells at your sides, arms straight.
Shrug your shoulders straight up towards your ears.
Hold briefly at the top without rolling your shoulders.
Lower them slowly back down.
Stand tall with a dumbbell in one hand at your side and your other hand on your hip or head.
Keep your feet planted and hips still.
Bend sideways towards the dumbbell, lowering it along your leg.
Use the opposite side of your waist to pull yourself back upright. Switch sides.

dumbbell-squat.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding dumbbells at your sides or at your shoulders.
Brace your stomach and keep your chest up.
Bend at the hips and knees to sit down, knees tracking over your toes, as low as you can with a flat back.
Drive through your whole foot to stand back up tall.

dumbbell-squat-to-a-bench.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back
steps: Stand in front of a bench with feet shoulder-width apart, holding dumbbells at your sides.
Push your hips back and bend your knees, keeping your chest up.
Lower until you lightly touch the bench without sitting down fully.
Drive through your feet to stand back up.

dumbbell-step-ups.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Stand facing a sturdy box or bench, holding dumbbells at your sides.
Place one whole foot firmly on the box.
Drive through that foot to step up until you're standing tall on the box, without pushing off hard with the back leg.
Step back down with control, then repeat or switch legs.
Lie on a flat bench holding dumbbells above your chest, palms facing towards your feet.
Keep your upper arms still and pointing up.
Bend at the elbows to lower the dumbbells towards the sides of your head.
Straighten your arms to press them back up.
Stand tall holding an EZ bar on its outer angled grips, palms facing up.
Keep your elbows at your sides.
Curl the bar up towards your shoulders without swinging.
Lower it slowly back to straight arms.
Lie on a flat bench holding an EZ bar on its inner grips, arms straight above your chest.
Keep your upper arms still and angled slightly back.
Bend at the elbows to lower the bar towards your forehead.
Straighten your arms to press back up.
Lie on your back with hands lightly behind your head and both knees lifted and bent.
Press your lower back gently into the floor and curl your shoulders up.
Twist to bring one elbow towards the opposite knee while straightening the other leg out low.
Switch sides in a smooth, controlled motion, keeping your neck relaxed.
Stand on a low step with a barbell on your upper back. Set it up in a rack with safety pins.
Step one foot back off the step and lower your back knee towards the floor.
Keep your front knee over your foot and your torso upright.
Push through your front foot to return to standing on the step, then switch legs.

elevated-cable-rows.muscles: Primary: Lats · Secondary: Mid back, Traps
steps: Sit at a cable machine with the pulley set above chest height, holding the handle with arms straight.
Lean back slightly with your chest up.
Pull the handle down towards your upper stomach, driving your elbows back.
Let it return slowly to straight arms.
Sit on an exercise ball, then walk your feet forwards until your lower back rests on the ball.
Place your hands lightly behind your head or across your chest.
Curl your upper body up, bringing your ribs towards your hips.
Lower back over the ball slowly.
Start in a push-up position with your shins on an exercise ball.
Keep your back flat and stomach tight.
Pull the ball towards your chest by bending your knees.
Push it back out slowly to straight legs.
Lie on the floor with knees bent and a kettlebell held above one shoulder, arm straight and wrist firm.
Lower it slowly until the back of your upper arm lightly touches the floor.
Press back up, then reach the bell a little further towards the ceiling so your shoulder blade lifts off the floor.
Let the shoulder settle back down before the next lowering. Switch arms, and roll onto your side to put the bell down.
Lie on your side with a dumbbell in your top hand, elbow bent to 90 degrees and resting on your side.
Keep your elbow tucked against your ribs.
Rotate your forearm up towards the ceiling.
Lower it slowly back down. Use a light weight.
Stand with a band anchored at elbow height, held in the hand furthest from the anchor.
Bend your elbow to 90 degrees and tuck it against your side.
Rotate your forearm outward away from your body.
Return slowly to the start.
Stand side-on to a cable at elbow height, holding the handle with the far hand.
Bend your elbow to 90 degrees and tuck it against your side.
Rotate your forearm outward away from the machine.
Return slowly to the start.
Set a rope on a cable at head height and grip it with palms facing in.
Step back so your arms are straight and there's tension.
Pull the rope towards your face, splitting your hands apart and driving your elbows back.
Let it return slowly to straight arms.

farmers-walk.muscles: Primary: Forearms · Secondary: Abs, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back, Quads, Traps
steps: Stand between two heavy weights, bend down with a flat back and grip the handles.
Stand up tall with your chest up and stomach braced.
Walk forwards with short, controlled steps.
Put the weights down carefully by bending your knees.

fast-skipping.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Abductors, Adductors, Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Stand tall on a flat, clear stretch of ground, weight on the balls of your feet.
Skip forwards with a quick hop-step, driving one knee up to about hip height while the opposite arm swings forwards.
Keep your contacts short and springy, staying tall rather than leaning back.
Switch legs every skip and keep the rhythm fast, then slow to a walk at the end.
Sit on a bench holding a barbell with palms up, forearms resting on your thighs and wrists just past your knees.
Open your fingers slowly and let the bar roll down to your fingertips, keeping hold of it.
Close your fingers to roll the bar back into your palms, then curl your wrists up slightly.
Use a light load; your grip is doing all the work.
Set a flat bench between two low cable pulleys and lie on it holding a handle in each hand.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Bring the handles together above your chest in a wide arc.
Let them open back out slowly until you feel a stretch.
Sit on the end of a flat bench, lean back slightly and hold the sides behind your hips, legs extended out in front.
Brace your stomach and keep your feet just off the floor.
Pull your knees in towards your chest while bringing your torso slightly forwards.
Push your legs back out slowly to straight, without letting your feet touch down.
Lie on a flat bench holding the edges behind your head, legs straight.
Raise your legs until they're vertical.
Lower them slowly without letting your lower back arch.
Stop just before they touch the bench.
Sit on an incline bench with dumbbells hanging at your sides, palms facing forwards.
Keep your upper arms still.
Curl the dumbbells up, curling your wrists slightly at the top.
Lower them slowly to straight arms.
Kneel on a pad with your ankles held down firmly by a partner or a secure anchor.
Squeeze your glutes and keep a straight line from knees to head, hands ready in front of your chest.
Lower yourself forwards as slowly as you can, resisting with the backs of your thighs.
Catch yourself with your hands, give a small push, and pull back up with your hamstrings to kneeling.
Lie on the floor inside a rack with the bar set just below arm's reach and safety pins set low. Grip about shoulder-width.
Bend your knees or keep legs straight, brace, and unrack the bar to straight arms above your chest.
Lower it slowly until the backs of your upper arms rest on the floor, elbows tucked at about 45 degrees.
Pause briefly without relaxing, then press back up to straight arms.
Hang an equal length of chain over each end of the bar so the links pile on the floor when the bar is low.
Lie on the floor under the bar in a rack with knees bent, and unrack it over your chest with a grip just inside shoulder width.
Lower under control until your upper arms touch the floor, keeping elbows tucked at roughly 45 degrees.
Pause briefly, then press back to straight arms. The load rises as more chain lifts off the floor, so drive hard through the top.
Lie on your back with legs straight and hands under your hips or flat by your sides.
Press your lower back gently into the floor and lift both heels a few centimetres off the ground.
Kick your legs up and down in small, quick alternating movements, keeping knees soft but mostly straight.
Keep breathing steadily. Lower both heels to rest if your back starts to arch off the floor.

forward-drag-with-press.muscles: Primary: Chest · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Quads, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Attach the sled straps to handles and hold one in each hand at chest height, facing away from the sled with slack taken out.
Walk forward with short, strong steps, leaning slightly into the drag.
As you step, press both handles straight out in front of you until your arms are extended, then bring them back to your chest.
Keep your ribs down and your trunk braced so the press comes from your chest and arms, not from arching your back.

frankenstein-squat.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Abs, Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Set a barbell on the front of your shoulders from a rack, then let go and hold both arms straight out in front of you.
Stand with feet about shoulder width apart and keep your chest tall so the bar stays balanced on your shoulders.
Squat down by bending hips and knees together, keeping elbows high and torso upright.
Stand back up through the whole foot. Use a light bar and set the rack safeties, since you are not gripping it.

freehand-jump-squat.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Stand with feet about hip to shoulder width apart and hands behind your head or at your chest.
Sit down into a quarter to half squat, keeping your chest up and knees tracking over your toes.
Drive through the floor and jump straight up as high as you can.
Land softly on the balls of your feet, sink back into the squat to absorb the landing, and reset before the next jump.
Lie on your back, put the soles of your feet together and let your knees drop out to the sides.
Reach your arms overhead or cross them over your chest.
Curl your head, shoulders and back up off the floor, reaching your hands towards your feet.
Roll back down one section of spine at a time, keeping the movement slow and controlled.

front-barbell-squat.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Rest the bar on the front of your shoulders against your throat, elbows pointing forward and high. Set the rack safeties.
Step back, stand with feet about shoulder width, take a breath and brace your trunk.
Squat down between your heels, keeping your torso upright and elbows up so the bar does not roll forward.
Drive back up through your whole foot, leading with the elbows and chest, and breathe out at the top.

front-barbell-squat-to-a-bench.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Place a bench or box behind you at a height that puts your thighs around parallel. Set the rack safeties.
Take the bar in the front rack, elbows high, step back and stand with feet about shoulder width. Brace.
Sit back and down under control until you lightly touch the bench, without relaxing onto it.
Keep your chest tall and drive straight back up to standing.

front-box-jump.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Abductors, Adductors, Calves, Glutes, Quads
steps: Stand facing a sturdy box about a short step away, feet hip width apart. Start with a low box.
Swing your arms back as you dip into a quarter squat.
Swing your arms forward and jump up onto the box, landing softly with both feet flat and knees bent.
Stand up tall on the box, then step down one foot at a time rather than jumping off.
Attach a handle to a low pulley and stand facing away from it, holding the handle in one hand beside your thigh.
Stand tall with a soft bend in the elbow and your shoulder blade set down and back.
Raise your arm straight forward until your hand reaches about shoulder height.
Lower slowly back to your thigh, keeping tension on the cable, and finish all reps before switching sides.

front-cone-hops-or-hurdle-hops.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Abductors, Adductors, Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Set out a row of low cones or mini hurdles a stride apart and stand behind the first one, feet hip width.
Dip slightly, swing your arms and hop forward over the first cone with both feet together.
Land softly on the balls of your feet and spring straight into the next hop with as little ground time as possible.
Keep your knees tracking over your toes. Start with low cones and add height only once landings feel quiet.
Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs, palms facing you.
Brace your trunk and keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Lift one dumbbell straight forward to about shoulder height without leaning back.
Lower it slowly, then raise the other arm. You should feel this in the front of your shoulder.
Set a bench to a low incline and sit back against it, a dumbbell in each hand hanging by your sides.
Keep your back and head on the pad and a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise both dumbbells forward and up until your arms point at the ceiling or just short of it.
Lower slowly back down alongside the bench. Use light weights; the start of the lift is the hardest part.
Stand tall holding a weight plate with both hands at the sides, resting against your thighs.
Brace your trunk and keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise the plate straight forward to eye level, keeping your torso still.
Lower it slowly back to your thighs without letting it swing.

front-raise-and-pullover.muscles: Primary: Chest · Secondary: Lats, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Lie flat on a bench holding a light barbell with a shoulder-width grip, arms straight and the bar resting on your thighs.
Keeping a slight bend in your elbows, raise the bar in an arc up over your chest.
Continue the arc behind your head until you feel a stretch through your chest and lats, keeping your lower back on the bench.
Pull the bar back over your chest and down to your thighs along the same path.

front-squat-clean-grip.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Abs, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Take the bar from a rack with your hands just outside shoulder width and let it sit on your shoulders, fingertips under the bar, elbows high.
Step back, set your feet about shoulder width, take a breath and brace.
Squat down with an upright torso, keeping your elbows lifted so the bar stays on your shoulders.
Drive up through your whole foot to standing. Set the safeties in case you need to dump the bar.
Clean two kettlebells to the rack position, handles in your hands and bells resting on your forearms at chest height.
Stand with feet about shoulder width, elbows tucked, and brace your trunk.
Squat down between your knees, keeping your chest up and the bells tight to your body.
Push back up to standing and breathe out at the top.
Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs, palms facing you.
Brace your trunk and keep your elbows slightly bent.
Raise both dumbbells together straight forward to shoulder height, without leaning back.
Lower them slowly to your thighs and reset before the next rep.

full-range-of-motion-lat-pulldown.muscles: Primary: Lats · Secondary: Biceps, Mid back, Shoulders
steps: Sit at the pulldown with your thighs under the pad and take the bar with a grip a little wider than your shoulders.
Let your arms go fully straight and allow your shoulders to rise towards your ears for a full stretch.
Pull your shoulder blades down first, then drive your elbows down to bring the bar to your upper chest.
Return slowly all the way to the stretched position before the next rep.

gironda-sternum-chins.muscles: Primary: Lats · Secondary: Biceps, Mid back
steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with a shoulder-width underhand or overhand grip.
Pull yourself up while leaning your head and shoulders back, arching your upper back.
Aim to bring your lower chest to the bar, squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top.
Lower slowly back to a full hang. This is demanding, so use assistance until you can reach the bar with control.
Set the machine so your knees sit just behind the pad and your ankles are locked under the rollers.
Start upright on your knees with a straight line from knees to head and your glutes squeezed.
Lower your body forward slowly by straightening at the knee, keeping your hips extended.
Pull yourself back up using your hamstrings. Push off lightly with your hands at the bottom if you need help.
Kneel on all fours, placing your hands below your shoulders and your knees below your hips.
Brace your trunk so your back stays flat.
Keeping one knee bent, drive that heel back and up until your thigh is in line with your body.
Squeeze your glute at the top, lower slowly, and finish all reps before switching legs.

goblet-squat.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Shoulders
steps: Hold a kettlebell by the horns close to your chest, elbows pointing down.
Stand with feet slightly wider than your hips, toes turned out a little.
Squat down between your knees, keeping your chest tall and the bell close.
Push through your whole foot to stand back up, squeezing your glutes at the top.

good-morning.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Abs, Glutes, Lower back
steps: Set a barbell across your upper back as for a back squat, and stand with feet about hip width.
Take a breath, brace your trunk and unlock your knees slightly.
Push your hips back and let your torso tilt forward with a flat back until you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings.
Drive your hips forward to return to standing. Start light; the load sits far from your hips.

good-morning-off-pins.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Abs, Glutes, Lower back
steps: Set the rack pins so the bar sits at about your upper-back height when you are hinged forward.
Get under the bar in the hinged position, bar across your upper back, back flat and knees slightly bent.
Brace hard, then drive your hips forward to lift the bar off the pins and stand up tall.
Hinge back down under control and let the bar settle on the pins before the next rep.
Hang from a pull-up bar with an underhand grip and pull up to the top of a chin-up.
Hold that position with elbows bent and chin over or near the bar.
Curl your knees up towards your chest, then lower them slowly without swinging.
Lower yourself to a hang with control. Keep both parts slow so momentum does not take over.

hack-squat.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Stand on the platform with your back and shoulders against the pads, feet about shoulder width.
Release the safety handles and brace your trunk.
Lower by bending your knees and hips until your thighs are about parallel, keeping your back on the pad.
Press through your whole foot back to the top without locking your knees hard. Re-engage the safeties at the end.
Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, arms by your sides and palms facing each other.
Keep your elbows tucked close to your ribs.
Curl the dumbbells up while keeping your palms facing in, until your forearms are nearly vertical.
Lower slowly to straight arms without swinging your body.
Set a bench to a moderate incline and sit back with a dumbbell in each hand at chest level, palms facing each other.
Plant your feet, set your shoulder blades back and down, and keep your elbows fairly close to your body.
Press the dumbbells up until your arms are straight above your upper chest.
Lower them slowly back to the sides of your chest, keeping the neutral grip throughout.
Kick up into a handstand against a wall, hands a little wider than shoulders and fingers spread.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your trunk so your body stays in a straight line.
Bend your elbows to lower your head slowly towards a padded surface on the floor.
Press back up to straight arms. Build up with pike push-ups first if you cannot yet control the descent.

hang-clean.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Forearms, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back, Shoulders, Traps
steps: Stand holding the bar with a grip just outside your thighs, then hinge slightly so it hangs just above your knees. Learn with a light bar.
Keeping your back flat and the bar close, jump by driving your hips and legs straight while shrugging.
Pull yourself under the bar, whipping your elbows forward to catch it on the front of your shoulders in a partial squat.
Stand up tall with the bar in the front rack, then lower it back to your thighs with control.

hang-clean-below-the-knees.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Forearms, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back, Shoulders, Traps
steps: Lift the bar to standing, then hinge until it hangs just below your knees, shoulders over the bar and back flat. Learn with light loads.
Pull the bar up close to your thighs, then extend your hips and knees explosively and shrug.
Drop under the bar and catch it on your shoulders with elbows high, in a squat.
Stand up tall, then return the bar to the hang position under control.

hang-snatch.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Abs, Calves, Forearms, Glutes, Lower back, Quads, Shoulders, Traps
steps: Take a wide snatch grip and stand tall, then hinge so the bar hangs around mid-thigh. Learn with an empty bar or a stick.
Keeping the bar close, extend your hips and knees explosively and shrug.
Pull yourself under the bar and punch it overhead, catching it on locked arms in a squat.
Stand up with the bar overhead, then lower it to your hips with control. Use bumper plates so you can drop it safely.

hang-snatch-below-knees.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Abs, Calves, Forearms, Glutes, Lower back, Quads, Shoulders, Traps
steps: With a wide snatch grip, hinge until the bar hangs just below your knees, shoulders over the bar and back flat. Learn with light loads.
Bring the bar up along your thighs, then drive your hips and knees straight explosively.
Pull under and punch the bar overhead, catching it with locked arms in a squat.
Stand up with the bar stable overhead before lowering it under control or dropping it on bumpers.

hanging-bar-good-morning.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Abs, Glutes, Lower back
steps: Hang the bar from chains or straps in a rack so it sits at your upper back when you are hinged forward.
Duck under, set the bar across your upper back, hinge with a flat back and knees slightly bent. Brace.
Drive your hips forward and stand up tall, lifting the bar off its supports.
Hinge back down slowly until the bar settles, and reset your brace before the next rep.
Hang from a pull-up bar with a shoulder-width grip and your shoulders gently engaged.
Keep your legs straight or slightly bent and still before you start, so you are not swinging.
Raise your legs in front of you to at least hip height by tilting your pelvis up.
Lower them slowly back down, stopping any swing before the next rep.
Hang from a pull-up bar with a shoulder-width grip and your legs together and straight.
Brace your trunk and keep your arms straight but active.
Lift your straight legs all the way up towards the bar, curling your pelvis to fold into a pike.
Lower slowly with control. Bend your knees if you cannot yet reach the bar with straight legs.

heaving-snatch-balance.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Abs, Forearms, Glutes, Hamstrings, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Set the bar on your upper back from a rack and take a wide snatch grip. Stand with feet in your squat stance. Learn with an empty bar.
Dip slightly at the knees, then drive up to launch the bar off your back.
Push yourself down under the bar, locking your arms overhead as you drop into a full squat.
Hold steady at the bottom, then stand up with the bar overhead. Use bumper plates and clear space to bail forward or back.

heavy-bag-thrust.muscles: Primary: Chest · Secondary: Abs, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Stand in a staggered stance facing a hanging heavy bag, hands on the bag at chest height.
Brace your trunk and keep your elbows bent close to your sides.
Push the bag away explosively by driving through your legs and extending your arms.
As the bag swings back, catch it with bent arms, absorb it, and push again.
Stand between two high pulleys holding a handle in each hand, arms stretched out to the sides at shoulder height, palms up.
Keep your upper arms level and still throughout.
Curl the handles towards the sides of your head by bending your elbows.
Straighten your arms slowly back out to the sides.
Anchor a band low in front of you and loop it around one ankle. Hold a support for balance.
Stand tall with a slight bend in your standing knee and your trunk braced.
Drive the banded leg straight back behind you, squeezing your glute, without arching your lower back.
Let the leg return slowly to the start and finish all reps before switching sides.
Anchor a band low behind you and loop it around one ankle. Hold a support for balance.
Stand tall with your standing leg slightly bent and your trunk braced.
Lift the banded knee forward and up towards hip height.
Lower it slowly back to the start, keeping your body upright, then switch sides.
Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat, and a band stretched across your hips with each end held down or anchored.
Press your lower back gently towards the floor and brace.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower your hips slowly back to the floor.

hurdle-hops.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Abductors, Adductors, Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Set out a row of low hurdles a stride apart and stand behind the first one, feet hip width.
Swing your arms and jump over the hurdle with both feet, tucking your knees up.
Land softly on the balls of your feet and go straight into the next jump.
Keep landings quiet and knees tracking over toes. Begin with low hurdles and raise them gradually.

hyperextensions-back-extensions.muscles: Primary: Lower back · Secondary: Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Set the pad so it sits just below your hip bones, and hook your heels under the foot rollers.
Cross your arms on your chest and let your torso hang forward with a flat back.
Raise your torso until your body is in a straight line, squeezing your glutes and lower back.
Stop at straight rather than arching past it, then lower slowly.

hyperextensions-with-no-hyperextension-b.muscles: Primary: Lower back · Secondary: Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Lie face down across a flat bench with your hips at the end, and have a partner hold your ankles or hook them under a secure support.
Let your torso hang down off the end with a flat back, arms crossed on your chest.
Raise your torso until your body forms a straight line.
Lower slowly back down. Make sure the bench is stable and your legs are held firmly before you start.
Lie on an incline bench holding a barbell or EZ bar above your head with a narrow grip, arms straight.
Keep your upper arms still and angled slightly back.
Bend your elbows to lower the bar slowly behind your head.
Straighten your arms to return to the start. Keep your elbows pointing forward, not flaring out.

incline-bench-pull.muscles: Primary: Mid back · Secondary: Lats, Shoulders
steps: Lie face down on an incline bench with a barbell hanging below you, gripped just wider than shoulders.
Keep your chest on the pad and your neck in line with your spine.
Row the bar up towards the bench by driving your elbows up and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower the bar slowly until your arms are straight.
Place an incline bench between two low pulleys and lie back holding a handle in each hand at chest level.
Plant your feet and set your shoulder blades back and down.
Press the handles up and slightly together over your upper chest until your arms are straight.
Lower them slowly back to chest level, keeping tension on the cables.
Place an incline bench between two low pulleys and lie back holding a handle in each hand above your chest.
Keep a soft, fixed bend in your elbows.
Open your arms wide in an arc until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Bring the handles back together over your upper chest, as if hugging a large barrel.
Take a dumbbell in each hand and lean back against an incline bench, holding them at chest level with palms facing each other.
Plant your feet and pull your shoulder blades back and down.
Press the dumbbells up over your upper chest until your arms are straight.
Lower slowly to the sides of your chest, keeping your elbows close and palms facing in.
Take a dumbbell in each hand and lean back against an incline bench, arms hanging straight down, palms forward.
Keep your upper arms still and your shoulders against the pad.
Curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders.
Lower slowly to fully straight arms. You will feel a stretch in the biceps at the bottom.
Sit back on an incline bench with dumbbells held above your upper chest, palms facing each other.
Keep a slight, fixed bend in your elbows.
Lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Bring them back up along the same arc until they meet above your chest.
Sit back on an incline bench with dumbbells held above your upper chest, palms facing each other.
With a slight bend in your elbows, lower the dumbbells out to the sides until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Bring them back up in an arc, rotating your wrists as they rise so your little fingers turn in to face each other at the top.
Squeeze your chest briefly, then reverse the rotation as you lower.
Take a dumbbell in each hand and lean back against an incline bench, holding them at shoulder level, palms facing forward.
Plant your feet and set your shoulder blades back and down.
Press the dumbbells up over your upper chest until your arms are straight.
Lower them slowly back to the sides of your chest.
Take a dumbbell in each hand and lean back against an incline bench, letting them hang straight down, palms facing in.
Keep your upper arms still and your back against the pad.
Curl the dumbbells up while keeping your palms facing each other.
Lower slowly to straight arms.
Take a dumbbell in each hand and lean back against an incline bench, arms hanging down, palms facing forward.
Turn your arms slightly outwards so the dumbbells sit a little away from your sides.
Curl the dumbbells up and out towards the outside of your shoulders, keeping your upper arms still.
Lower slowly back to straight arms.
Place your hands on a bench or box slightly wider than your shoulders and step your feet back into a straight line.
Brace your trunk and squeeze your glutes so your hips do not sag.
Lower your chest towards the edge of the bench, elbows at about 45 degrees to your body.
Push back up to straight arms. The higher the surface, the easier the push-up.
Place your hands close together on a bench or box and walk your feet back into a straight line.
Brace your trunk and keep your body rigid.
Lower your chest to the edge of the bench, keeping your elbows tucked close to your sides.
Press back up to straight arms, focusing on your triceps.
Get into an incline push-up with your hands on two low, stable boxes and feet behind you.
Drop your hands off the boxes to the floor between them, landing with bent elbows to absorb the fall.
Immediately push up explosively so your hands leave the floor, and bring them back onto the boxes.
Keep your body straight throughout. Learn it with low boxes and only progress once landings feel controlled.

incline-push-up-medium.muscles: Primary: Chest · Secondary: Abs, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Place your hands on a bench or box at shoulder width and step your feet back into a straight line.
Brace your trunk and squeeze your glutes.
Lower your chest towards the bench, keeping your elbows at a moderate angle to your body.
Push back up to straight arms without letting your hips drop.

incline-push-up-reverse-grip.muscles: Primary: Chest · Secondary: Abs, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Place your hands on a bench at shoulder width with your fingers pointing back towards your feet.
Walk your feet back until your body forms a straight line, and brace your trunk.
Lower your chest towards the bench, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Push back up to straight arms. Go gently at first; this grip puts extra stretch on the wrists.

incline-push-up-wide.muscles: Primary: Chest · Secondary: Abs, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Place your hands on a bench or box well wider than your shoulders and step your feet back into a straight line.
Brace your trunk and keep your body rigid.
Lower your chest towards the bench, letting your elbows move out to the sides.
Push back up to straight arms, feeling the work across your chest.
Anchor a band at elbow height and stand side-on to it, holding the band in the hand nearest the anchor.
Bend your elbow to 90 degrees and keep it pinned to your side, forearm pointing out towards the anchor.
Rotate your forearm in across your stomach, keeping your elbow in place.
Let it return slowly out to the start, then switch sides.
Set a bar in a rack or Smith machine at about waist height and lie underneath, gripping it slightly wider than your shoulders.
Walk your feet out so your body forms a straight line from heels to head, arms straight.
Pull your chest up to the bar by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower slowly to straight arms. Bend your knees to make it easier.

inverted-row-with-straps.muscles: Primary: Mid back · Secondary: Biceps, Lats
steps: Adjust suspension straps so the handles hang about waist height, and hold one in each hand.
Lean back and walk your feet forward until your body is straight and angled, arms extended.
Pull your chest towards the handles, keeping your elbows close and your body rigid.
Lower slowly back to straight arms. The more horizontal you are, the harder it gets.
Stand tall holding a light dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing in.
Brace your trunk and keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise both arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height, making a T shape.
Hold briefly, then lower slowly back to your sides. Use light weights; the load is far from the shoulder.
Stand or sit tall and press your palms together in front of your chest, elbows out to the sides.
Push your hands into each other as hard as you comfortably can.
Hold the squeeze while breathing steadily; do not hold your breath.
Relax your hands and rest before the next hold.
Sit or stand tall with your head level and chin slightly tucked.
Place your palm on your forehead and press your head gently forward into your hand, without letting it move.
Hold for a few seconds while breathing normally, then relax.
Move your hands to the back of your head and press gently backwards into them. Build pressure gradually and stop if anything hurts.
Sit or stand tall with your head level and eyes forward.
Place one palm against the side of your head, just above the ear.
Press your head sideways into your hand without letting it move, holding for a few seconds.
Relax, then repeat on the other side. Use gentle pressure and build up gradually.

isometric-wipers.muscles: Primary: Chest · Secondary: Abs, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Get into a push-up position with your hands wider than your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Shift your weight towards one hand, bending that elbow to lower your chest towards it while the other arm stays straighter.
Hold briefly, then push across to the other side, keeping your hips level.
Keep your trunk braced the whole time and breathe steadily.
Lie on a flat bench and unrack a barbell over your chest with a grip about shoulder width. Use safeties or a spotter.
Keep your elbows pointing towards your feet rather than flaring out.
Lower the bar by bending your elbows and letting it drift down towards your upper chest or chin, part way between a press and a skull crusher.
Press the bar back up to straight arms by extending your elbows.
Lie flat on your back with your arms stretched overhead and legs straight.
Brace your trunk and press your lower back towards the floor.
Lift your arms and legs together, reaching your hands towards your shins so your body folds into a V.
Lower both halves back down slowly. Bend your knees if you cannot yet control the straight-leg version.
Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, arms reaching forward.
Gently press your heels down and back into the floor to switch on your hamstrings, which quietens the hip flexors.
Keep that heel pressure and slowly curl up, one section of your spine at a time.
Roll back down just as slowly. The range is small; keep the tension rather than chasing height.

jefferson-squats.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back, Traps
steps: Stand straddling a barbell on the floor, feet wide and turned slightly out, the bar running between your legs.
Squat down and grip the bar with one hand in front of your body and the other behind, keeping your back flat.
Brace and stand up by driving through your feet, keeping your torso upright.
Lower the bar back to the floor with control. Swap which foot and hand are in front between sets.

jerk-balance.muscles: Primary: Shoulders · Secondary: Glutes, Hamstrings, Quads, Triceps
steps: Hold a light bar in the front rack and stand in a short split, back foot in its jerk position and front foot about half a step forward.
Dip by bending your knees with your torso upright.
Drive up, then push yourself under the bar as you step the front foot forward into a full split, locking your arms overhead.
Stabilise, then bring your feet back together with the bar overhead. Learn it with an empty bar.
Take a bar in the front rack from a rack, elbows slightly forward, and stand with feet about hip width. Set safeties.
Brace your trunk and keep your weight across your whole foot.
Dip straight down by bending only at the knees a short way, keeping your torso vertical.
Drive straight back up to standing. Keep the dip short and the bar path vertical.

keg-load.muscles: Primary: Lower back · Secondary: Abs, Biceps, Calves, Forearms, Glutes, Hamstrings, Mid back, Quads, Shoulders, Traps
steps: Stand close to the keg with the loading platform in front of you. Learn with a light or partly filled keg.
Hinge down, grip the keg securely around its sides or bottom edge, flat back, and brace hard.
Stand up with it, lapping it against your thighs if needed, then drive your hips forward to lift it onto the platform.
Walk back and lift the keg down with control using your legs, keeping it close to your body.
Hold a kettlebell in the rack position at your shoulder, palm facing you and the bell resting on your forearm.
Stand tall and brace your trunk and glutes.
Press the bell up overhead, rotating your hand as it rises so your palm faces forward at the top.
Reverse the rotation as you lower back to the rack. Finish all reps, then switch sides.

kettlebell-dead-clean.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Lower back, Quads, Traps
steps: Stand with a kettlebell on the floor between your feet, hinge down and grip the handle with a flat back.
Drive through your legs and hips to lift the bell, keeping it close to your body.
As it rises, pull your elbow down and let the bell roll around your hand to rest on your forearm at your shoulder.
Lower it back to the floor under control, hinging with a flat back.
Stand with feet wider than your hips, knees bent and hips back, holding a kettlebell in one hand.
Pass the bell between your legs from front to back, and take it with your other hand reaching round from behind.
Bring it round the outside of that leg to the front, then pass it back through the other way.
Keep your back flat and move smoothly so the bell traces a figure of eight around your legs.

kettlebell-hang-clean.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Lower back, Shoulders, Traps
steps: Stand holding a kettlebell in one hand in front of you, then hinge so it hangs just above your knees.
Snap your hips forward to drive the bell upwards, keeping it close to your body.
Tuck your elbow in so the bell rolls softly round your hand and settles against your forearm at your shoulder.
Let it drop back down to the hang with control, hinging to absorb it.

kettlebell-one-legged-deadlift.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Glutes, Lower back
steps: Stand on one leg holding a kettlebell in the opposite hand, standing knee slightly bent.
Hinge forward at the hip, letting your free leg extend straight behind you as the bell lowers towards the floor.
Keep your back flat and your hips square to the floor.
Drive your hips forward to return to standing. Finish the set, then switch legs.

kettlebell-pass-between-the-legs.muscles: Primary: Abs · Secondary: Glutes, Hamstrings, Shoulders
steps: Stand with feet wider than your hips and knees slightly bent, holding a kettlebell in one hand.
Hinge forward a little and pass the bell between your legs to the other hand behind you.
Bring it round the outside of your leg to the front, then pass it back through.
Keep your back flat and your trunk braced, and move smoothly rather than quickly.
Stand with feet wide, holding one kettlebell by the horns with both hands at chest height.
Brace your trunk and push the bell out in front of you with arms nearly straight.
Swing it in a smooth arc down and across to one side, then back up and over to the other side.
Pivot your feet as you turn, and keep your back flat and the movement controlled.

kettlebell-pistol-squat.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Shoulders
steps: Stand on one leg holding a kettlebell by the horns at your chest, the other leg lifted slightly in front.
Lower slowly into a deep one-legged squat, reaching the free leg forward and using the bell as a counterweight.
Keep your standing heel down and your knee tracking over your toes.
Drive back up to standing. Squat to a box first if you cannot yet control the full depth.
Sit on the floor or a bench holding a kettlebell in the rack position at your shoulder.
Sit tall with your trunk braced and your shoulders down.
Press the bell straight up until your arm is locked out overhead.
Lower it slowly back to the rack. Finish all reps, then switch sides.
Stand tall with two kettlebells in the rack position at your shoulders.
Brace your trunk and squeeze your glutes.
Press one bell overhead to lockout.
As you lower it, press the other bell up so the arms pass each other, alternating in a steady rhythm.

kettlebell-sumo-high-pull.muscles: Primary: Traps · Secondary: Adductors, Glutes, Hamstrings, Quads, Shoulders
steps: Stand with feet wide and toes turned out, a kettlebell on the floor between your feet.
Squat down and grip the handle with both hands, back flat and chest up.
Drive up through your legs and pull the bell up to chest height, leading with your elbows high and out.
Lower it back to the floor under control, keeping your back flat.
Hold two kettlebells in the rack position at your shoulders and stand with feet about shoulder width.
Brace and squat down, keeping your chest up and elbows tucked.
Drive up out of the squat and use that momentum to press the bells overhead to lockout.
Lower the bells back to your shoulders and go straight into the next squat.

kettlebell-turkish-get-up-lunge-style.muscles: Primary: Shoulders · Secondary: Abs, Hamstrings, Quads, Triceps
steps: Lie on your back holding a kettlebell straight up in one hand, same-side knee bent. Keep your eyes on the bell and start light.
Roll onto the opposite elbow, then up to that hand, then lift your hips.
Sweep your straight leg back under you into a half-kneeling position, then stand up out of the lunge.
Reverse each step to lie back down, keeping the bell locked out overhead the whole time.

kettlebell-turkish-get-up-squat-style.muscles: Primary: Shoulders · Secondary: Abs, Calves, Hamstrings, Quads, Triceps
steps: Lie on your back holding a kettlebell straight up in one hand, same-side knee bent. Keep your eyes on the bell and start light.
Roll onto the opposite elbow, then up to that hand, then lift your hips high.
Bring your straight leg through under you so both feet are planted, and sit into a deep squat with the bell overhead.
Stand up from the squat, then reverse every step back to the floor with the arm locked.

kettlebell-windmill.muscles: Primary: Abs · Secondary: Glutes, Hamstrings, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Press a kettlebell overhead in one hand and turn both feet about 45 degrees away from that arm.
Keep your eyes on the bell and the arm locked out.
Push your hip out towards the bell side and hinge down, sliding your free hand down the inside of your leg towards the floor.
Go only as far as your hamstrings allow with a flat back, then drive back up to standing.

kipping-muscle-up.muscles: Primary: Lats · Secondary: Abs, Biceps, Forearms, Mid back, Shoulders, Traps, Triceps
steps: Hang from a bar with a false or strong overhand grip. Only attempt this once you have solid pull-ups and dips.
Build a controlled swing by moving your chest through and then your legs forward.
At the forward swing, pull hard and drive your hips towards the bar, then quickly roll your chest over the top.
Press out of the dip to straight arms above the bar, then lower yourself back to a hang under control.
Support yourself on parallel bars or a dip station with straight arms, or on forearm pads, shoulders pushed down.
Let your legs hang straight below you and hold still.
Raise your knees towards your chest, curling your hips up at the top.
Lower your legs slowly back to hanging without swinging.

knee-tuck-jump.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Abductors, Adductors, Calves, Glutes, Quads
steps: Stand with feet hip width apart and arms by your sides.
Dip into a quarter squat, swing your arms and jump straight up.
At the top, pull both knees up towards your chest, then extend your legs to land.
Land softly on the balls of your feet with bent knees, and reset before the next jump if you need to.
Kneel tall on a mat with your trunk upright and elbows bent to about 90 degrees.
Brace your trunk so your body stays still while your arms move.
Drive your arms in a sprinting action, one hand forward to about chin height as the other elbow swings back past your hip.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and the action fast but controlled.
Attach a rope to a high pulley, kneel facing it, and hold the rope ends beside your head.
Keep your hips still and set slightly back.
Crunch down by curling your ribs towards your hips, rotating so one elbow travels towards the opposite knee.
Return slowly to upright, then crunch again turning to the other side.
Attach a rope or bar to a pulley at about head height, kneel facing away from the machine, and hold it behind your head.
Lean slightly forward with your elbows pointing forward beside your head.
Straighten your arms to push the attachment forward and out in front of you.
Bend your elbows slowly to return behind your head, keeping your upper arms still.

kneeling-high-pulley-row.muscles: Primary: Lats · Secondary: Biceps, Mid back
steps: Attach a bar or rope to a high pulley and kneel facing it, arms stretched up and forward.
Brace your trunk and keep your torso upright or leaning back slightly.
Pull the handle down towards your upper chest, driving your elbows down and back.
Let your arms extend slowly back to the start.

kneeling-jump-squat.muscles: Primary: Glutes · Secondary: Calves, Hamstrings, Quads
steps: Kneel on a mat with a light barbell across your upper back and your feet flat behind you, toes tucked. Learn it unloaded first.
Sit your hips back towards your heels, keeping your chest up and back flat.
Swing your hips forward explosively and jump your feet under you, landing in a squat.
Stand up tall, then kneel back down one knee at a time with control.

kneeling-single-arm-high-pulley-row.muscles: Primary: Lats · Secondary: Biceps, Mid back
steps: Attach a single handle to a high pulley and kneel facing it, holding the handle with one arm stretched up.
Keep your torso upright and your trunk braced.
Pull the handle down towards your side, driving your elbow down and back.
Let your arm extend slowly back up. Finish all reps, then switch sides.

kneeling-squat.muscles: Primary: Glutes · Secondary: Abs, Hamstrings, Lower back
steps: Kneel on a pad inside a rack with a barbell across your upper back, set from the rack at kneeling height. Set safeties.
Sit back until your glutes lightly touch your heels, keeping your back flat and chest up.
Drive your hips forward to rise up onto your knees, squeezing your glutes at the top.
Sit back down slowly and return the bar to the rack when finished.

landmine-180s.muscles: Primary: Abs · Secondary: Glutes, Lower back, Shoulders
steps: Set one end of a barbell in a landmine or corner and hold the other end with both hands at chest height, arms extended.
Stand with feet shoulder width and knees slightly bent.
Rotate your trunk and hips to swing the bar in an arc down towards one hip, pivoting your feet.
Bring it back up through the centre and across to the other hip with control.

landmine-linear-jammer.muscles: Primary: Shoulders · Secondary: Abs, Calves, Chest, Hamstrings, Quads, Triceps
steps: Set one end of a barbell in a landmine and hold the loaded end with both hands at chest height, facing it.
Stand with a staggered or even stance and squat down slightly, trunk braced.
Drive up through your legs and use that momentum to press the bar up and forward until your arms are straight.
Lower the bar back to your chest and sink into the next dip.

lateral-bound.muscles: Primary: Adductors · Secondary: Abductors, Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Quads
steps: Stand on one leg with a slight bend in the knee.
Sink your hips and push off sideways, jumping across to land on the opposite foot.
Land softly with a bent knee and hold the landing briefly for balance.
Push back off to the other side. Keep jumps modest until your landings feel steady.

lateral-box-jump.muscles: Primary: Adductors · Secondary: Abductors, Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Quads
steps: Stand beside a low, sturdy box with feet hip width apart.
Dip into a quarter squat and swing your arms.
Jump sideways up onto the box, landing softly with both feet and knees bent.
Step or hop down to the other side and repeat in the other direction.

lateral-cone-hops.muscles: Primary: Adductors · Secondary: Abductors, Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Quads
steps: Stand beside a cone or small hurdle with feet together.
Dip slightly and hop sideways over the cone with both feet.
Land softly on the balls of your feet and immediately hop back across.
Keep your chest up and knees tracking over your toes, spending as little time on the ground as you can.
Stand on the middle of a band and hold one end in each hand at your sides.
Stand tall with a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise both arms out to the sides until your hands reach shoulder height.
Lower slowly against the band's pull back to your sides.
Lie on the floor holding a kettlebell in the rack position at your chest, elbow on the floor.
Straighten the leg on the kettlebell side and cross the other leg over it, rolling slightly onto that side.
Press the kettlebell straight up until your arm is locked out.
Lower it slowly until your upper arm touches the floor. Finish all reps, then switch sides.
Sit in the machine with your back against the pad and the roller resting on the front of your lower shins.
Line your knees up with the machine's pivot point and hold the side handles.
Straighten your legs until your knees are extended, squeezing your quads.
Lower the weight slowly back down without letting the stack crash.
Stand tall beside a wall or support and hold it lightly for balance.
Brace your trunk and keep your standing knee soft.
Lift one straight leg back behind you, squeezing your glute, without arching your lower back.
Lower it slowly back to the floor and finish all reps before switching sides.

leg-press.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Sit in the machine with your back flat on the pad and feet on the platform about shoulder width.
Push the platform up and release the safety handles.
Lower the platform slowly by bending your knees towards your chest, stopping before your lower back lifts off the pad.
Press back up through your whole foot without locking your knees hard. Re-engage the safeties at the end.
Sit on the floor or a bench edge, lean back slightly and support yourself on your hands.
Extend your legs out in front of you, heels just off the floor.
Pull your knees in towards your chest while bringing your torso slightly forward.
Extend your legs back out slowly, keeping your trunk braced.
Adjust the seat so the handles line up with your mid chest, and sit with your back flat on the pad.
Grip the handles and set your shoulder blades back and down.
Press the handles forward until your arms are straight.
Return slowly until you feel a stretch across your chest, without letting the weight touch down.
Stand on the platform between the handles with feet about hip width.
Hinge and bend your knees to grip the handles, back flat and chest up. Brace.
Drive through your feet to stand up tall, pushing your hips forward at the top.
Lower the handles back down with control, keeping your back flat.
Adjust the seat so the handles line up with your lower chest, and sit with your back on the pad.
Grip the handles and set your shoulder blades back and down.
Press the handles forward and down until your arms are straight.
Return slowly to the stretched position, keeping tension on the machine.
Adjust the seat and thigh pad so you can just reach the handles with your arms stretched up and forward.
Grip the handles and keep your chest tall.
Pull the handles down and back towards your ribs, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Let your arms extend slowly back to the start.
Adjust the seat so the handles line up with your upper chest, and sit with your back flat on the pad.
Grip the handles and set your shoulder blades back and down.
Press the handles up and forward until your arms are straight.
Lower slowly back to the stretched position without letting the weight rest.

leverage-iso-row.muscles: Primary: Lats · Secondary: Biceps, Mid back
steps: Adjust the seat so the handles are at about chest height and sit with your chest against the pad.
Grip the handles with your arms extended forward.
Row the handles back towards your sides, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades.
Let the handles return slowly until your arms are straight. You can work both arms together or one at a time.
Adjust the seat so the handles start at about shoulder height, and sit with your back flat on the pad.
Grip the handles and brace your trunk.
Press the handles overhead until your arms are straight.
Lower them slowly back to shoulder height.
Stand in the machine with the handles at your sides, or under the pads, and grip firmly.
Stand tall with your arms straight and your trunk braced.
Lift your shoulders straight up towards your ears as high as you can.
Hold briefly, then lower your shoulders slowly without rolling them.
Stand at the start line, feet hip width, one foot slightly behind the other.
Bend forward into a crouch with weight over the front foot and the opposite arm forward, back straight.
Drop your hips a little further to load your legs, eyes looking a short way ahead.
Drive off both feet into your first steps, pumping your arms hard and staying low as you accelerate.

linear-acceleration-wall-drill.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Quads
steps: Stand about an arm's length from a wall and lean into it with straight arms, body in one line at roughly 45 degrees.
Rise onto the balls of your feet and lift one knee to hip height, toes pulled up towards your shin.
Drive that foot down and back under your hip as the other knee comes up, switching legs sharply.
Keep your hips high and trunk rigid; the push comes from your hamstrings and glutes, not from bending at the waist.
Do short, crisp bursts of switches, then stand up and reset before the next one.

linear-depth-jump.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Stand on the edge of a low, stable box. Start low; height adds impact, not skill.
Step off (don't jump off) and land on both feet, knees soft and tracking over your toes.
The moment your feet touch, spring forward and up as far as you can, swinging your arms.
Land the jump quietly with bent knees and hips back, then walk back and reset fully before the next rep.

log-lift.muscles: Primary: Shoulders · Secondary: Abs, Chest, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back, Mid back, Quads, Traps, Triceps
steps: Stand close to the log, hinge down and grip the neutral handles with a flat back and braced trunk.
Pull the log up your thighs, roll it into your lap, then drive it up onto your chest with your hips.
Set your elbows high under it, take a fresh breath and brace hard.
Dip slightly at the knees and drive up, pressing the log overhead until your arms lock and your head comes through.
Lower it back to your chest under control, then down to the floor. Learn it with a light log first.

london-bridges.muscles: Primary: Lats · Secondary: Biceps, Forearms, Mid back
steps: Hang a climbing rope or strong strap from a secure overhead point and grip it high with both hands.
Walk your feet forward until your body leans back at an angle, heels on the floor and body straight.
Pull yourself up the rope hand over hand towards an upright position, keeping your chest up and shoulders down.
Walk your hands back down the rope under control to lower yourself to the start angle.
Set both pulleys at the lowest position and take a handle in each hand, standing centred with a small step forward.
Start with arms low and slightly out to the sides, elbows softly bent and palms facing forward.
Sweep your hands up and together in an arc until they meet around chest to chin height, squeezing your upper chest.
Lower back along the same arc with control until you feel a stretch across the chest.
Attach a bar or rope to a low pulley. Face away from the stack and hold it behind your head, elbows pointing up.
Stagger your feet and brace your trunk so your lower back stays neutral.
Keep your upper arms still and straighten your elbows to press the handle up overhead.
Bend your elbows slowly to lower it back behind your head, feeling the stretch in the backs of your arms.

low-pulley-row-to-neck.muscles: Primary: Shoulders · Secondary: Biceps, Mid back, Traps
steps: Sit at a low cable row with a rope or straight bar, knees slightly bent and chest tall.
Start with arms straight in front at shoulder height, torso upright rather than leaning back.
Pull towards your neck with elbows flared out high, squeezing your rear shoulders and upper back.
Pause briefly, then let your arms extend slowly without rounding forward.

lunge-pass-through.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Quads
steps: Stand tall holding a kettlebell in one hand by your side.
Step forward into a lunge, lowering until both knees are bent at about 90 degrees.
At the bottom, pass the kettlebell under your front thigh into your other hand.
Push through your front foot to stand back up, then lunge with the other leg and pass it back.
Keep your chest up and your front knee in line with your toes throughout.

lunge-sprint.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Set up on the machine or sled in a split stance, one foot forward and hands on the handles.
Sink into a lunge so your front knee is bent and your back heel is lifted.
Drive hard through your front foot and quickly switch legs, pushing forward in short, powerful strides.
Stay tall with your hips square; stop the set as soon as the strides lose speed or control.
Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and lie on your back with your feet towards the stack.
Hold the bar with palms up, arms straight along your body and elbows tucked to your sides.
Curl the bar towards your chest, keeping your upper arms on the floor.
Squeeze at the top, then straighten your arms slowly against the cable's pull.

lying-cambered-barbell-row.muscles: Primary: Mid back · Secondary: Biceps, Lats, Traps
steps: Lie face down on a raised flat bench with a cambered bar under you, your chin just past the end.
Grip the bar a little wider than shoulder width, arms hanging straight.
Pull the bar up by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades; the bend lets it travel higher.
Keep your chest on the pad the whole time, then lower the bar slowly to full arm length.
Attach a straight bar to a high pulley and lie on your back on the floor or a bench beneath it.
Take a close, palms-up grip with your arms reaching straight up towards the pulley.
Keep your upper arms fixed and curl the bar down towards your forehead by bending your elbows.
Squeeze your biceps, then slowly straighten your arms back up.
Lie on a flat bench holding a barbell with a close, overhand grip, arms straight above your chest.
Let your arms drift slightly back so the bar is over your forehead, then bend your elbows to lower it behind your head.
Keep your elbows pointing up and in rather than flaring out.
Straighten your elbows to bring the bar back above your forehead. Use a weight you can control near your head.
Lie on a flat bench holding an EZ bar with a close grip, arms straight over your chest.
Bend your elbows and lower the bar towards your chin, letting your elbows travel slightly forward.
Stop just short of your chin with control.
Press the bar back up by straightening your elbows, feeling it in the backs of your arms.
Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand, arms straight above your shoulders, palms facing each other.
Keep your upper arms still and bend your elbows to lower the dumbbells beside your head.
Go down until you feel a good stretch in the backs of your arms.
Straighten your elbows to press the dumbbells back up, without letting them clash.
Lie face down on a flat bench with your head and neck off the end, a folded towel on the back of your head.
Hold a light plate on the towel with both hands. Start very light; the neck does not need much load.
Lower your chin slowly towards your chest, then lift your head back until it lines up with your body.
Move smoothly with no jerking, and stop if you feel any pain or pins and needles.
With a folded towel on your forehead, lie face up on a flat bench so your head extends past the end.
Hold a light plate on the towel with both hands. Begin with very little weight.
Let your head tip back slowly, then lift your chin towards your chest.
Keep every rep slow and controlled, and stop straight away if anything feels sharp or numb.
Lie face down on a high flat bench with your arms hanging straight towards the floor.
Hold a barbell with an underhand, shoulder-width grip.
Curl the bar up towards your forehead, keeping your upper arms pointing down.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly to straight arms.
Lie face down on the machine with the pad just above your heels and your knees just off the bench edge.
Hold the handles and keep your hips pressed into the pad.
Curl your heels towards your glutes as far as you can without lifting your hips.
Lower the weight slowly until your legs are nearly straight, keeping tension on the hamstrings.

lying-machine-squat.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Lie back on the machine with your shoulders under the pads and your feet about shoulder width on the platform.
Release the safety handles and brace your trunk, keeping your back flat on the pad.
Bend your knees and lower as deep as you can while your lower back stays on the pad.
Push through your whole foot to straighten your legs without locking your knees hard. Re-engage the safeties at the end.
Lie on your side on a flat or slightly inclined bench, holding a dumbbell in your top hand.
Start with the dumbbell in front of your hips, elbow slightly bent.
Raise your arm out and up until it points towards the ceiling, leading with your elbow.
Lower slowly back down. Finish your set, then roll over for the other arm.
Lie face down on a flat or low incline bench with a light dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging down.
Keep a soft bend in your elbows and your palms facing each other.
Lift your arms out to the sides until they are level with your body, feeling the backs of your shoulders.
Pause briefly, then lower slowly without swinging.
Lie on your back on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging down beside the bench.
Turn your palms up and keep your upper arms still.
Curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders, feeling a big stretch from the start.
Lower slowly all the way back to straight arms.

lying-t-bar-row.muscles: Primary: Mid back · Secondary: Biceps, Lats
steps: Lie face down on the chest pad of the machine, feet on the platform, and grip the handles.
Lift the weight off the rack so your arms are straight and your chest stays on the pad.
Pull the handles up by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower under control to full arm length, then rack the weight when you finish.
Lie on a flat bench holding an EZ bar with a narrow overhand grip, arms straight over your chest.
Keep your upper arms still and bend your elbows to lower the bar towards your forehead.
Stop a few centimetres above your head, elbows pointing up.
Straighten your arms to press the bar back up, squeezing the backs of your arms.
Adjust the seat so the handles line up with your mid chest, and sit with your back flat on the pad.
Grip the handles, set your shoulder blades back and plant your feet.
Press the handles forward until your arms are straight but not forcefully locked.
Let them come back slowly until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Adjust the seat so your elbows line up with the machine's pivot and your upper arms rest on the pad.
Grip the handles with palms up and arms nearly straight.
Curl the handles towards your shoulders, keeping your elbows on the pad.
Lower slowly back to the start without letting the weight stack drop.
Sit at the machine and set the seat so your armpits sit snugly over the top of the angled pad.
Grip the handles palms up with your arms almost straight.
Curl the handles up by bending your elbows, keeping the backs of your arms on the pad.
Lower slowly, stopping just short of fully locking out to protect your elbows.
Set the seat so the handles start around shoulder height and sit with your back against the pad.
Grip the handles, brace your trunk and keep your feet flat.
Press the handles straight up until your arms are extended.
Lower them back to shoulder height with control.
Adjust the seat so your elbows line up with the machine's pivot and your upper arms rest on the pad.
Grip the handles with your elbows bent.
Straighten your arms to push the handles down or out, squeezing the backs of your arms.
Let the handles return slowly until your elbows are bent again.
Stand facing a partner or a solid wall, feet shoulder width, holding a medicine ball at your chest.
Keep your elbows bent and out slightly, fingers spread behind the ball.
Step forward and push the ball away hard by straightening your arms, finishing with thumbs pointing down.
Catch it back at your chest with soft elbows and reset before the next throw.
Stand side-on to a solid wall or partner, feet wider than your hips, holding a medicine ball at chest height.
Rotate away from the wall, turning through your hips and trunk and letting your back foot pivot.
Unwind quickly and release the ball towards the wall as your chest turns to face it.
Catch the rebound with soft arms and absorb it into the next rotation. Switch sides.

medicine-ball-scoop-throw.muscles: Primary: Shoulders · Secondary: Abs, Hamstrings, Quads
steps: Stand with feet a little wider than your hips, holding a medicine ball in both hands.
Squat and hinge down so the ball is between your knees, back flat and chest up.
Drive through your legs and hips and scoop the ball up and forward or overhead as high as you can.
Let the ball land well clear of you, then retrieve it and reset. Use an open space or a high wall.
Holding a dumbbell in each hand, lie face down on an incline bench with your arms hanging straight down.
Keep your arms straight and your neck relaxed.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together, lifting the dumbbells a short distance without bending your elbows.
Hold for a moment, then let your shoulder blades spread apart slowly.

mixed-grip-chin.muscles: Primary: Mid back · Secondary: Biceps, Lats
steps: Grab a pull-up bar with one hand facing towards you and the other facing away, about shoulder width.
Hang with straight arms, shoulders pulled down and trunk braced.
Pull yourself up until your chin clears the bar, driving your elbows down.
Lower slowly to a full hang. Swap which hand faces you on your next set.
Place a resistance band around your legs just above your knees or ankles, and stand with feet hip width apart.
Bend your knees slightly and push your hips back into a quarter squat, chest up.
Step forward and outward at a diagonal with one foot, keeping tension on the band, then follow with the other.
Keep your knees pushed out and your steps controlled. Walk backwards to return.

mountain-climbers.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Chest, Hamstrings, Shoulders
steps: Start in a high push-up position with your hands under your shoulders and body in a straight line.
Drive one knee towards your chest while keeping your hips level.
Switch legs quickly, pushing the front foot back as the other knee comes in.
Keep your shoulders over your hands and your trunk braced throughout.
Stand tall and walk or jog forward at an easy pace.
Lift one knee, then extend the lower leg and sweep the foot down and back under your hips, like pawing the ground.
Land on the ball of your foot and pull through, then repeat with the other leg.
Keep your trunk upright and the movement smooth. Build speed only once the pattern feels natural.

muscle-snatch.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Glutes, Lower back, Quads, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Start with a barbell over your mid foot, wide snatch grip, hips hinged and back flat.
Stand up with the bar close, then drive through your legs and extend your hips to lift it up your body.
Keep your elbows high and out, then turn them under and press the bar straight overhead without dipping your knees.
Finish with arms locked overhead, then lower the bar with control. Learn it with an empty bar first.

muscle-up.muscles: Primary: Lats · Secondary: Abs, Biceps, Forearms, Mid back, Shoulders, Traps, Triceps
steps: Hang from a bar or rings with a firm grip, arms straight and trunk braced.
Pull hard and high, drawing the bar towards your lower chest rather than your chin.
As you reach the top, lean your chest over the bar and turn your wrists and elbows over it.
Press up into a straight-arm support, then lower yourself back to a hang under control.

narrow-stance-hack-squats.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Stand in the hack squat machine with your back on the pad, shoulders under the pads and feet close together.
Release the safety handles and brace your trunk.
