Bend your knees to lower as deep as you can while your heels stay flat and your back stays on the pad.
Push through your whole foot to stand back up, then re-engage the safeties.

narrow-stance-leg-press.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Sit in the leg press with your back flat on the pad and your feet close together in the middle of the platform.
Release the safeties and hold the handles.
Lower the platform by bending your knees until they are around 90 degrees, keeping your hips on the seat.
Press back up through your whole foot without snapping your knees straight.

narrow-stance-squats.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back
steps: Set the bar in a rack at upper-chest height with safeties just below your bottom position.
Take the bar across your upper back, step back and set your feet about hip width apart.
Take a breath, brace your trunk and squat down, keeping your chest up and knees tracking over your toes.
Go as deep as you can with a neutral back, then drive up through your whole foot.

natural-glute-ham-raise.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Lower back
steps: Kneel on a pad with your ankles held down by a partner or a secure anchor.
Start upright with your body straight from knees to head and your glutes tight.
Lower your body forward slowly by straightening at the knees, resisting with your hamstrings.
Catch yourself with your hands if needed, then push off lightly and curl yourself back up to upright.
Set up on a flat bench in a rack with safeties set just above neck height, or with a spotter.
Take a wide overhand grip and unrack the bar over your upper chest.
Lower the bar slowly towards the base of your neck with your elbows flared out.
Press it back up over your chest. Use a light weight; the path is harder on the shoulders than a normal bench.
Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, fingertips lightly at the sides of your head.
Lift your shoulders off the floor and twist so one elbow moves towards the opposite knee.
Squeeze the side of your waist at the top, without pulling on your neck.
Lower slowly and repeat towards the other side.
Lie on your side on the floor with your legs stacked and knees slightly bent.
Place your top hand lightly behind your head and your bottom arm across your waist.
Crunch sideways, lifting your shoulder towards your hip.
Lower slowly. Finish your set, then switch sides.

olympic-squat.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Set the bar high on your upper back in a rack with safeties at the right height, feet about shoulder width.
Take a breath and brace, then sit straight down between your heels, keeping your torso upright.
Go as deep as you can with a flat back, knees travelling forward over your toes.
Drive up through your whole foot, keeping your chest up.

one-arm-dumbbell-row.muscles: Primary: Mid back · Secondary: Biceps, Lats, Shoulders
steps: Place one knee and the same hand on a flat bench, back flat and roughly parallel to the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in your other hand with your arm hanging straight down.
Pull the dumbbell towards your hip, driving your elbow back and keeping it close to your side.
Lower slowly to a full stretch without twisting your trunk. Switch sides after the set.
Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell in one hand, arm straight above your chest, and hold the bench with your other hand.
Keep a soft bend in your elbow and brace your trunk so you don't tip.
Open your arm out to the side in a wide arc until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Bring it back up along the same arc, squeezing your chest. Switch arms after the set.
Stand side-on to a high pulley, holding the handle overhead with the near hand.
Stand tall with feet hip width apart and your other hand on your hip.
Bend sideways away from the pulley, crunching the side of your waist without twisting.
Return upright slowly. Switch sides after the set.
Lie on your side on an incline bench, holding a light dumbbell in your top hand.
Let the dumbbell hang in front of you with a slight bend in your elbow.
Raise your arm out and up until it points roughly straight up, leading with your elbow.
Lower slowly to the start. Switch sides after the set.

one-arm-kettlebell-clean.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Glutes, Lower back, Shoulders, Traps
steps: Stand over a kettlebell, hinge at the hips with a flat back and grip it in one hand.
Hike it back between your legs, then drive your hips forward to send it up close to your body.
As it rises, pull your elbow in and let the bell roll around your hand into the rack position at your shoulder.
Keep your wrist straight, then drop it back between your legs under control to repeat.
Clean the kettlebell from between your legs up to the rack position at your shoulder.
Dip slightly at the knees with your trunk upright.
Drive up with your legs, push the bell overhead and quickly re-bend your knees to catch it with a locked arm.
Stand up fully, then bring it back to the rack and down between your legs. Practise with a light bell first.
Lie on the floor with knees bent, holding a kettlebell at your chest in one hand with the bell resting on your forearm.
Rest your upper arm on the floor at about 45 degrees to your body.
Press the kettlebell straight up until your arm is locked, keeping your wrist straight.
Lower slowly until your upper arm touches the floor again. Switch arms after the set.

one-arm-kettlebell-jerk.muscles: Primary: Shoulders · Secondary: Calves, Quads, Triceps
steps: Start with the kettlebell in the rack position at your shoulder, feet hip width apart.
Dip slightly at the knees, then drive up hard through your legs.
As the bell rises, re-bend your knees to drop under it, catching it on a straight arm.
Stand up fully with the bell overhead, then lower it back to the rack. Learn the timing with a light bell.
Hold a kettlebell in the rack position at your shoulder, feet hip width apart.
Turn your palm slightly forward and brace your trunk.
Press the bell up and slightly out to the side, leaning your torso a little away from it as it rises.
Lock your arm overhead, then lower it back to your shoulder. Switch sides after the set.
Hold a kettlebell by the handle at shoulder height, elbow out to the side and forearm upright.
Brace your trunk and keep your feet planted about hip width.
Press the kettlebell straight up until your arm is locked out overhead.
Lower it slowly back to the start with your elbow out wide. Switch sides after the set.

one-arm-kettlebell-push-press.muscles: Primary: Shoulders · Secondary: Calves, Quads, Triceps
steps: Hold a kettlebell in the rack position at your shoulder, feet hip width apart.
Dip slightly by bending your knees with your torso upright.
Drive up through your legs and use that momentum to press the bell overhead to a locked arm.
Lower it back to your shoulder with control. Switch sides after the set.

one-arm-kettlebell-row.muscles: Primary: Mid back · Secondary: Biceps, Lats
steps: Hinge forward with a flat back, one hand on a bench or your knee, holding a kettlebell in the other hand.
Let the kettlebell hang straight down below your shoulder.
Row it towards your hip, driving your elbow back and squeezing your shoulder blade.
Lower it slowly without twisting your trunk. Switch sides after the set.

one-arm-kettlebell-snatch.muscles: Primary: Shoulders · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back, Traps, Triceps
steps: Stand over a kettlebell, hinge down with a flat back and grip it in one hand.
Hike it back between your legs, then drive your hips forward hard to send it upward.
Let it float up close to your body and punch your hand through at the top so it lands softly on your forearm, arm locked.
Drop it back down in an arc between your legs to repeat. Learn with a light bell first.

one-arm-kettlebell-split-jerk.muscles: Primary: Shoulders · Secondary: Glutes, Hamstrings, Quads, Triceps
steps: Start with the kettlebell in the rack position at your shoulder, feet hip width apart.
Dip slightly at the knees, then drive up hard through your legs.
As the bell rises, split your feet forward and back and catch it overhead on a straight arm.
Step your front foot back, then your back foot forward, to stand tall before lowering. Learn with a light bell.
Stand over a kettlebell, hinge down with a flat back and grip it in one hand.
Hike it back, then drive your hips forward to send it up close to your body.
As it reaches the top, split your feet forward and back and catch it overhead on a locked arm.
Bring your feet back together, then lower the bell with control. Practise with a light bell first.
Stand with feet a little wider than your hips, kettlebell on the floor just in front of you.
Hinge down with a flat back, grab the handle with one hand and hike it back between your legs.
Snap your hips forward to swing the bell up to about chest height, keeping your arm relaxed.
Let it fall back between your legs, hinging at the hips to absorb it. Switch hands after the set.

one-arm-long-bar-row.muscles: Primary: Mid back · Secondary: Biceps, Lats
steps: Wedge one end of a barbell into a corner or landmine and load the other end.
Stand beside the loaded end, hinge forward with a flat back and grip the bar near the plates.
Row the bar towards your hip, keeping your elbow close and squeezing your back.
Lower slowly to a full stretch without rounding. Switch sides after the set.
Stand with feet shoulder width apart, holding a slam ball in one hand.
Reach the ball up overhead, rising slightly onto your toes.
Slam it down to the floor beside your foot, crunching your trunk and hinging at the hips.
Pick it up with a flat back and repeat. Switch hands after the set. Use a ball made for slamming.

one-arm-open-palm-kettlebell-clean.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Forearms, Glutes, Lower back, Quads, Shoulders
steps: Stand over a kettlebell, hinge down with a flat back and grip it in one hand.
Hike it back, then drive your hips forward to send it upward close to your body.
At the top, release your grip and open your hand to catch the bell on your palm at shoulder height.
Regrip and lower it back between your legs. Start very light while you learn the catch.

one-arm-overhead-kettlebell-squats.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Shoulders
steps: Press or snatch a kettlebell overhead in one hand and lock your arm, feet about shoulder width.
Keep your eyes on the bell or ahead and your trunk braced.
Squat down as deep as your mobility allows, keeping the bell stacked over your shoulder.
Drive up through your whole foot. Switch arms after the set, and start light.

one-arm-side-deadlift.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Abs, Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back, Traps
steps: Stand beside a loaded barbell with it running along the outside of one foot.
Squat and hinge down with a flat back and grab the middle of the bar with one hand.
Brace your trunk and stand up, resisting any lean or twist towards the weight.
Lower the bar back to the floor under control. Switch sides after the set.
Stand tall with a dumbbell in one hand at your side and hold something steady with the other.
Keep a slight bend in your elbow.
Raise your arm out to the side until it reaches shoulder height, leading with your elbow.
Lower slowly without shrugging. Switch arms after the set.
Attach an ankle cuff to a low pulley and fasten it to one ankle, facing the machine.
Hold the machine for balance, stand on your other leg and hinge forward slightly.
Kick your cuffed leg straight back by squeezing your glute, without arching your lower back.
Return slowly to the start. Switch legs after the set.

one-arm-chin-up.muscles: Primary: Mid back · Secondary: Biceps, Forearms, Lats
steps: Grip a bar with one hand, palm facing you, and hang with your arm straight and shoulder engaged.
Brace your trunk and hold your other arm by your side or across your chest.
Pull yourself up until your chin clears the bar, resisting any spin.
Lower slowly to a full hang. Build up with assisted versions before trying it free.
Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell in one hand at chest level and your feet planted.
Brace your trunk so your body doesn't tip towards the weight.
Press the dumbbell up until your arm is straight above your chest.
Lower it slowly back to chest level. Switch arms after the set.
Sit at a preacher bench and rest the back of one arm on the pad, dumbbell in that hand.
Start with your arm almost straight and palm facing up.
Curl the dumbbell towards your shoulder, keeping your arm on the pad.
Lower slowly to just short of straight. Switch arms after the set.
Lie on the floor with a light barbell or have a spotter hand it to you, gripping it in the middle with one hand.
Rest your upper arm on the floor and keep your other hand ready to steady the bar.
Press the bar straight up, keeping it level and stopping it from tipping.
Lower slowly until your upper arm touches the floor. Switch arms after the set.

one-arm-lat-pulldown.muscles: Primary: Lats · Secondary: Biceps, Mid back
steps: Attach a single handle to the high pulley and sit with your thighs under the pads.
Grab the handle with one arm straight overhead.
Pull the handle down towards your shoulder, driving your elbow down and in.
Let it rise slowly until your arm is straight again. Switch arms after the set.
Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell in one hand, arm straight above your shoulder and palm facing your feet.
Keep your upper arm still.
Bend your elbow to lower the dumbbell across towards your opposite shoulder.
Straighten your arm to lift it back up. Switch arms after the set.
Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell in one hand, arm straight above your shoulder and palm facing your head.
Keep your upper arm still.
Bend your elbow to lower the dumbbell towards the same-side shoulder.
Straighten your arm to press it back up. Switch arms after the set.

one-leg-barbell-squat.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Set a barbell in a rack with safeties, place it across your upper back and step out.
Rest the top of one foot on a bench behind you, front foot far enough forward to squat comfortably.
Brace and lower by bending your front knee until your thigh is about parallel with the floor.
Drive up through your front foot. Switch legs after the set, and start light.

open-palm-kettlebell-clean.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Glutes, Lower back, Quads, Shoulders
steps: Stand over a kettlebell, hinge down with a flat back and grip it.
Hike it back between your legs, then drive your hips forward to send it up close to your body.
At the top, let go and catch the bell on your open palm at shoulder height.
Regrip and swing it back between your legs. Start very light while you learn the catch.

otis-up.muscles: Primary: Abs · Secondary: Chest, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Lie on your back with your feet anchored and knees bent, holding a weight plate on your chest.
Sit up, curling your trunk forward until you are upright.
At the top, press the plate straight out or overhead until your arms are straight.
Bring it back to your chest and lower yourself slowly to the floor.
Set both pulleys high and stand centred between them, holding a handle in each hand.
Raise your arms out to the sides at shoulder height, palms up.
Curl the handles towards the sides of your head, keeping your upper arms still.
Straighten your arms slowly back out to the sides.
Stand with feet shoulder width apart, holding a slam ball in both hands.
Lift it overhead, reaching tall with your arms straight.
Throw it down to the floor in front of you as hard as you can, pulling with your lats and bending your hips and knees.
Catch it on the bounce or pick it up with a flat back and repeat. Use a ball made for slamming.

overhead-squat.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Abs, Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Hold a barbell overhead with a wide grip and locked arms, feet about shoulder width. Start with an empty bar.
Push up into the bar and brace your trunk.
Squat down as deep as you can while keeping the bar over your mid foot.
Drive up through your whole foot. If the bar drifts, let it fall forward or back and step away.

pallof-press.muscles: Primary: Abs · Secondary: Chest, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Set a cable at chest height and stand side-on to it, holding the handle at your chest with both hands.
Step away until there is tension, feet shoulder width, knees soft.
Press the handle straight out in front of you, resisting the pull towards the machine.
Hold briefly, then bring it back to your chest. Switch sides after the set.

pallof-press-with-rotation.muscles: Primary: Abs · Secondary: Chest, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Set a cable at chest height and stand side-on to it, holding the handle at your chest with both hands.
Press the handle straight out in front of you.
Rotate your trunk away from the machine slightly, keeping your arms straight and hips square.
Rotate back to centre, then bring the handle to your chest. Switch sides after the set.
Kneel beside a flat bench and rest your forearms on it, wrists just past the edge, a light dumbbell in each hand.
Turn your palms down towards the floor.
Lift the backs of your hands up by bending at the wrist only.
Lower slowly to a comfortable stretch.
Kneel beside a flat bench and rest your forearms on it, wrists just past the edge.
Hold a light barbell with an overhand grip.
Lift the bar by bending at the wrists only, keeping your forearms on the bench.
Lower slowly to a comfortable stretch.
Kneel beside a flat bench and rest your forearms on it, wrists just past the edge.
Hold a barbell with an underhand grip, palms facing up.
Curl the bar up by bending at the wrists, keeping your forearms on the bench.
Lower slowly, letting the bar roll down towards your fingers a little.
Kneel beside a flat bench and rest your forearms on it, wrists just past the edge, a dumbbell in each hand.
Turn your palms up towards the ceiling.
Curl the dumbbells up by bending at the wrists only.
Lower slowly to a comfortable stretch.
Grip the parallel bars and press yourself up to straight arms, shoulders down away from your ears.
Stay fairly upright with your elbows tucked back to focus on your triceps.
Lower yourself until your upper arms are about parallel with the floor, or as far as your shoulders feel comfortable.
Press back up to straight arms.
Sit on an exercise ball and walk your feet forward until your head and shoulders rest on it.
Place your feet flat, hip width apart, knees bent at about 90 degrees.
Lower your hips towards the floor, then drive them back up until your body is level from knees to shoulders.
Squeeze your glutes at the top and keep your ribs down.

pin-presses.muscles: Primary: Triceps · Secondary: Chest, Forearms, Lats, Mid back, Shoulders
steps: Set the pins in a power rack so the bar rests a few centimetres above your chest when you lie on the bench.
Lie under the bar, set your shoulder blades back and grip it.
Brace and press the bar up off the pins until your arms are straight.
Lower it back onto the pins with control and let it settle before the next rep.
Rest on your forearms and toes, elbows directly under your shoulders.
Make a straight line from your head to your heels.
Brace your trunk and squeeze your glutes so your hips neither sag nor lift.
Breathe steadily and hold, then lower your knees to rest.
Place two weight plates together, smooth sides facing out.
Pinch them with your fingers on one side and thumb on the other.
Stand up and hold them by your side with your arm straight.
Hold as long as you can, then lower them to the floor under control.
Sit on the floor with knees bent, holding a weight plate at your chest.
Lean back slightly with a straight back, feet on the floor or lifted.
Rotate your trunk to one side, bringing the plate beside your hip.
Rotate through to the other side with control.
Lie on your back with your heels on a sliding surface such as a towel or slider, knees bent.
Lift your hips into a bridge, keeping your trunk braced.
Slide your heels out slowly until your legs are nearly straight, keeping your hips up.
Pull your heels back in towards your glutes, using your hamstrings.

plie-dumbbell-squat.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Abs, Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Stand with feet wide and toes turned out, holding one dumbbell by the end between your legs.
Keep your chest up and back flat.
Squat down, pushing your knees out over your toes, until your thighs are about parallel.
Drive up through your heels to stand.
Set a kettlebell on the floor and take a push-up position with one hand on its handle and the other on the floor.
Lower your chest towards the floor with your body in a straight line.
Push up explosively so your hands leave the ground, and shift across so the other hand lands on the kettlebell.
Land with soft elbows and go straight into the next rep. Make sure the kettlebell is stable.
Start in a push-up position, hands just outside your shoulders, body straight.
Lower your chest towards the floor under control.
Push up hard enough that your hands leave the ground.
Land with soft elbows and lower straight into the next rep.

power-clean.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Calves, Forearms, Glutes, Lower back, Mid back, Quads, Shoulders, Traps, Triceps
steps: Stand with the bar over your mid foot, grip just outside your knees, back flat and chest up.
Push the floor away to lift the bar, keeping it close to your legs.
When it passes your knees, drive your hips forward and shrug, pulling yourself under the bar.
Catch it on your shoulders in a partial squat, elbows high, then stand. Learn it with a light bar.
Set the bar on blocks at about knee height and stand close, back flat.
Grip just outside your thighs.
Drive your hips forward and shrug to lift the bar, pulling yourself under it.
Catch it on your shoulders in a partial squat with elbows high, then stand. Start light.

power-jerk.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Abs, Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Hold the bar on your shoulders with a firm grip, feet hip width apart.
Dip by bending your knees slightly, keeping your torso upright.
Drive up hard and push the bar overhead, re-bending your knees to catch it with locked arms.
Stand tall with the bar overhead, then lower it to your shoulders. Learn it with an empty bar.
Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand by your sides.
Keep your elbows slightly bent and your trunk braced.
Raise the dumbbells quickly out to the sides until they reach shoulder height.
Lower them with control and continue at a brisk pace, stopping if your form slips.

power-snatch.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Lower back, Quads, Shoulders, Traps, Triceps
steps: Stand with the bar over your mid foot, wide snatch grip, back flat and chest up.
Push the floor away to lift the bar, keeping it close to your legs.
Drive your hips forward and pull yourself under, catching the bar overhead in a partial squat with locked arms.
Stand up, then lower the bar with control. Learn it with an empty bar first.

power-snatch-from-blocks.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Forearms, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back, Shoulders, Traps, Triceps
steps: Set the bar on blocks around knee height and stand close with a wide snatch grip, back flat.
Drive your hips forward and extend your legs to accelerate the bar upward.
Pull yourself under and catch it overhead in a partial squat with locked arms.
Stand fully, then lower it back to the blocks with control. Start light.

power-stairs.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Adductors, Calves, Glutes, Lower back, Quads, Shoulders, Traps
steps: Stand at the bottom of a set of solid steps or boxes, holding the implement by its handles.
Hinge at the hips with a flat back and brace your trunk.
Drive your hips forward to swing the implement up onto the first step.
Step up, then repeat step by step to the top. Learn the pattern with a light load.
Sit at a preacher bench with your armpits snug over the top of the pad.
Hold a barbell or EZ bar with an underhand, shoulder-width grip.
Curl the bar up towards your shoulders, keeping your upper arms on the pad.
Lower slowly to just short of straight arms.
Sit at a preacher bench and rest the backs of your arms on the pad, a dumbbell in each hand.
Turn your palms to face each other.
Curl the dumbbells up, keeping your arms on the pad and your palms facing in.
Lower slowly to just short of straight arms.

press-sit-up.muscles: Primary: Abs · Secondary: Chest, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Lie on a decline bench with your feet anchored, holding a light barbell at your chest.
Sit up, curling your trunk towards your knees.
At the top, press the bar straight up overhead.
Bring the bar back to your chest and lower your torso slowly.
Lie face down on a bench or mat with your legs straight.
Have a partner place their hands on the back of your ankle.
Curl your heel towards your glutes while your partner gives steady resistance.
Lower slowly as they resist the return. Agree on how hard to push before you start.

pull-through.muscles: Primary: Glutes · Secondary: Hamstrings, Lower back
steps: Attach a rope to a low pulley and stand facing away from the machine.
Take the rope in both hands between your legs, then walk forward until the cable is taut.
Hinge at your hips, letting the rope pull through your legs as your back stays flat.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall, squeezing your glutes.

pullups.muscles: Primary: Lats · Secondary: Biceps, Mid back
steps: Grip a pull-up bar with palms facing away, a little wider than your shoulders.
Hang with straight arms, shoulders pulled down.
Pull yourself up until your chin clears the bar, leading with your chest.
Lower slowly to a full hang.

push-up-wide.muscles: Primary: Chest · Secondary: Abs, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Start in a push-up position with your hands wider than your shoulders.
Keep your body straight from head to heels.
Lower your chest towards the floor, elbows angling out.
Push back up to straight arms.
Start in a push-up position with your hands close together under your chest.
Keep your body straight from head to heels.
Lower your chest towards your hands, keeping your elbows tucked close to your sides.
Push back up to straight arms, feeling it in the backs of your arms.
Place your feet on a bench or box and your hands on the floor, just wider than your shoulders.
Keep your body straight from head to heels.
Lower your chest towards the floor under control.
Push back up to straight arms.
Place your shins or feet on an exercise ball and your hands on the floor, just wider than your shoulders.
Brace your trunk to keep the ball steady and your body straight.
Lower your chest towards the floor under control.
Push back up to straight arms without letting your hips sag.
Hold the bar on your shoulders with a shoulder-width grip, feet hip width apart.
Dip by bending your knees slightly, keeping your torso upright.
Drive up through your legs and use that momentum to press the bar overhead to locked arms.
Lower the bar back to your shoulders with control.

push-press-behind-the-neck.muscles: Primary: Shoulders · Secondary: Calves, Quads, Triceps
steps: Hold the bar across your upper back with a wide grip, feet hip width apart. Only do this if your shoulders are comfortable there.
Dip by bending your knees slightly, keeping your torso upright.
Drive up through your legs and press the bar overhead to locked arms.
Lower it back behind your neck with control. Keep the weight moderate.

push-up-to-side-plank.muscles: Primary: Chest · Secondary: Abs, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Start in a push-up position with your body straight.
Lower your chest towards the floor, then push back up.
At the top, rotate to one side, lifting your arm towards the ceiling into a side plank.
Return to the push-up position and repeat, alternating sides.
Start in a push-up position, hands just wider than your shoulders and body straight.
Lower your chest towards the floor, keeping your elbows at about 45 degrees.
Push back up to straight arms.
Start in a push-up position with your hands close together under your chest.
Lower your chest towards the floor, then push back up.
Move your hands out wider than your shoulders and do a push-up in that position.
Keep alternating between the close and wide positions.
Stand with feet hip width apart in front of a low, stable box or a marked spot.
Drop into a quarter squat and swing your arms back.
Explode up and forward, landing softly on the box or the mark with your knees bent.
Step back down or reset quickly, then repeat.
Stand tall holding a light barbell at your hips with a clean-width overhand grip, feet about hip-width apart.
Give a small dip at the knees, then drive up and shrug so the bar floats upwards close to your body.
Whip your elbows round and forward so the bar lands on the front of your shoulders, fingertips under it and elbows high.
Stand still for a moment in that rack position, then lower the bar back to your hips under control. Learn it with light loads first.

rack-pull-with-bands.muscles: Primary: Lower back · Secondary: Forearms, Glutes, Hamstrings, Quads, Traps
steps: Set the pins or blocks so the bar starts around knee height, and loop a band over each sleeve anchored low to the rack.
Stand close with the bar over mid-foot, hinge down and grip just outside your legs. Flatten your back and brace hard.
Push the floor away and drive your hips forward to stand tall. The bands get heavier near the top, so keep driving through.
Stand tall without leaning back, then hinge the bar back down to the pins with control, keeping your back flat.

rack-pulls.muscles: Primary: Lower back · Secondary: Forearms, Glutes, Hamstrings, Traps
steps: Set the bar on pins or blocks at about knee height. Stand close with your feet hip-width apart and the bar over mid-foot.
Hinge at the hips, grip just outside your legs and set a flat back. Take a big breath and brace your stomach.
Drive through your feet and push your hips forward until you are standing straight, shoulders over the bar.
Finish tall without leaning back, then push your hips back and lower the bar to the pins under control.
Take an athletic stance facing a partner or solid wall, knees soft, holding a medicine ball at your chest.
Step or lean forward and push the ball away hard with both hands, straightening your arms fully.
Catch the return at your chest with soft elbows, absorb it, then push it straight back out in one smooth rhythm.
Keep your back neutral and your stomach tight throughout. Choose a ball light enough to throw fast.

reverse-band-bench-press.muscles: Primary: Triceps · Secondary: Chest, Forearms, Lats, Mid back, Shoulders
steps: Hang bands from the top of the rack and loop them round the bar so they help most at the bottom of the lift.
Lie on the bench with eyes under the bar, feet flat, shoulder blades squeezed together. Set safeties and use a spotter if you can.
Unrack and lower the bar under control to your lower chest, tucking your elbows slightly.
Press back up to straight arms. The bands help less as you rise, so keep pushing hard through the top.

reverse-band-box-squat.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Abductors, Adductors, Calves, Forearms, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back
steps: Hang bands from the top of the rack round the bar, and place a box behind you at the depth you want. Set the safeties.
Unrack the bar onto your upper back, step back and set your feet a little wider than shoulder-width. Brace.
Sit back and down onto the box with control, shins fairly upright, keeping your chest up and back flat.
Pause briefly without relaxing, then drive up through your feet to stand tall. The bands help least at the top.

reverse-band-deadlift.muscles: Primary: Lower back · Secondary: Abductors, Adductors, Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Quads
steps: Loop bands from the top of a rack round the bar so they lighten the load at the floor. Stand with the bar over mid-foot.
Hinge down and grip just outside your legs. Flatten your back, pull the slack out of the bar and brace.
Push the floor away, keeping the bar close to your legs, and stand tall with your hips through.
The bands help less as you rise, so finish strongly. Lower the bar back down along your legs with control.

reverse-band-power-squat.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Adductors, Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back
steps: Hang bands from the top of the rack round the bar so they assist you at the bottom. Set the safeties at a sensible height.
Unrack onto your upper back and take a wider stance with toes turned out slightly. Take a big breath and brace.
Sit your hips back and down, knees tracking over your toes, to at least parallel if your mobility allows.
Drive up and slightly back into the bar, keeping your chest up, until you are standing tall.

reverse-band-sumo-deadlift.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Abductors, Adductors, Calves, Forearms, Glutes, Lower back, Quads, Traps
steps: Loop bands from the top of the rack round the bar. Take a wide stance, toes out, with the bar over mid-foot.
Drop your hips and grip the bar inside your knees with straight arms. Push your knees out, flatten your back and brace.
Push the floor apart with your feet and stand up, keeping the bar close and your chest tall.
Lock out with hips through and shoulders back, then return the bar to the floor under control.
Stand tall holding a barbell with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder-width, arms straight in front of your thighs.
Keep your elbows pinned to your sides and curl the bar up towards your shoulders, wrists staying straight.
Squeeze at the top without letting your elbows drift forward.
Lower slowly back to straight arms. Use less weight than a normal curl, as the palms-down grip is weaker.
Sit at a preacher bench with the backs of your upper arms flat on the pad, holding an EZ bar palms down.
Curl the bar up towards your shoulders, keeping your wrists straight and your arms on the pad.
Pause near the top, then lower slowly until your arms are almost straight. Stop short of snapping into lockout.
Attach a straight bar to a low pulley. Stand facing it and hold the bar palms down, hands about shoulder-width.
With elbows tucked at your sides, curl the bar up towards your chest, keeping your wrists in line with your forearms.
Squeeze briefly at the top, then let the bar back down slowly until your arms are straight.
Lie on your back with your arms by your sides, palms down. Lift your legs so your knees are bent at about 90 degrees.
Tighten your stomach and curl your hips up off the floor, bringing your knees towards your chest.
Lower your hips back down slowly without letting your lower back arch or your feet drop to the floor.
Move with your abs, not momentum. Breathe out as you curl up.
Hold a light dumbbell in each hand and hinge forward until your chest is nearly parallel to the floor, back flat.
Let the dumbbells hang below your chest, palms facing each other, elbows slightly bent.
Raise your arms out to the sides in a wide arc until they are level with your body. Feel it in the backs of your shoulders.
Lower slowly back to the start without swinging or lifting your torso.
Hinge forward with a flat back, holding light dumbbells below your chest with elbows bent to about 90 degrees.
Lift your elbows sideways until your upper arms are level with your shoulders.
Keeping the elbows there, rotate your forearms up and back until the dumbbells point towards the ceiling.
Reverse the rotation, then lower your elbows back down slowly. Keep the weights light and the movement smooth.

reverse-grip-bent-over-rows.muscles: Primary: Mid back · Secondary: Biceps, Lats, Shoulders
steps: Hold a barbell with an underhand grip, hands about shoulder-width. Hinge forward to around 45 degrees with a flat back.
Brace your stomach and let the bar hang at arm's length just below your knees.
Pull the bar into your lower stomach, driving your elbows back close to your sides and squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower the bar under control to straight arms, keeping your torso still throughout.
Attach a straight or EZ bar to a high pulley. Hold it palms up, hands about shoulder-width, elbows tucked at your sides.
Push the bar down until your arms are fully straight, keeping your upper arms still.
Squeeze the backs of your arms at the bottom, then let the bar rise slowly until your forearms are just above parallel.
Lie face down on the machine with your hips at the edge of the pad and your legs hanging down. Grip the handles.
Hook your ankles under the roller or strap and let your legs hang straight.
Squeeze your glutes and swing your legs up behind you until they are level with your body. Avoid arching hard at the top.
Let your legs lower back down with control rather than dropping them.
Set the machine for the rear delt position and adjust the seat so the handles are at shoulder height.
Sit facing the pad, chest against it, and grip the handles with your arms out in front and elbows slightly bent.
Sweep your arms out and back in a wide arc until they are in line with your body. Feel it in the backs of your shoulders.
Return the handles forward slowly, stopping before the weight stack touches down.
Stand tall and hold a weight plate by its edges, fingers on top and thumbs underneath, arms straight in front of your thighs.
Keeping your elbows tucked at your sides, curl the plate up towards your chest.
Hold briefly at the top, then lower slowly to straight arms. Keep your wrists firm the whole way.
Lie on a flat bench and take the bar with an underhand grip, hands about shoulder-width. Use a spotter and set safeties.
Unrack with straight arms over your chest, keeping your wrists stacked over your elbows.
Lower the bar slowly to your lower chest, keeping your elbows tucked close to your body.
Press back up to straight arms. Start light, as this grip is awkward and harder to control.

rickshaw-carry.muscles: Primary: Forearms · Secondary: Abs, Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back, Quads, Traps
steps: Step inside the rickshaw frame, feet about hip-width, and grip the handles at your sides.
Brace your stomach, keep your back flat and lift the frame by standing up tall, like a deadlift.
Walk forward with short, quick steps, keeping the frame steady and your shoulders pulled back.
At the finish, hinge and set the frame down under control. Learn it with light loads first.

rickshaw-deadlift.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Forearms, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back, Traps
steps: Stand inside the rickshaw frame with your feet about hip-width, handles beside your feet.
Bend your knees and hips to grip the handles, chest up and back flat. Take a big breath and brace.
Drive through your feet to stand up tall, keeping your arms straight and the frame level.
Lower the frame back to the floor under control by bending at the hips and knees.
Set the rings at about hip height. Grip them and press up to support yourself on straight arms, rings close to your sides.
Keep the rings steady and your body tight, then bend your elbows to lower until your shoulders are just below your elbows.
Push back up to straight arms, turning the rings out slightly at the top.
Only go as deep as your shoulders are comfortable. Build up from bar dips if the rings wobble too much.
Stand with feet about shoulder-width apart, then drop into a quarter squat with your hands near your hips.
Explode upwards, driving your arms overhead and reaching as high as you can with your whole body straight.
Land softly on the balls of your feet, bending your knees to absorb the impact.
Reset your stance before the next jump. Quality over speed.
Stand tall with a barbell across your upper back, taken from a rack set at shoulder height. Feet hip-width apart.
Rise up onto the balls of your feet as high as you can, squeezing your calves at the top.
Lower your heels, then rock back onto your heels and lift your toes to stretch the front of the shin.
Rock forward again into the next raise in a smooth rhythm, keeping your body upright and balanced.

rocky-pull-ups-pulldowns.muscles: Primary: Lats · Secondary: Biceps, Mid back, Shoulders
steps: Take a wide overhand grip on a pull-up bar or lat pulldown bar, arms straight and shoulders set down.
Pull your chest up towards the bar, leading with your elbows, then lower all the way down with control.
Keep alternating smooth reps, staying tight through your stomach and avoiding any swing.
If a full pull-up is too hard, use the pulldown machine with the same grip and path.

romanian-deadlift.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Lower back
steps: Stand tall holding a barbell at your thighs with an overhand grip, feet hip-width apart and knees softly bent.
Push your hips back and let the bar slide down your thighs, keeping your back flat and the bar close.
Lower until you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings, usually just below the knee. Do not round your back to go lower.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall again, squeezing your glutes at the top.

romanian-deadlift-from-deficit.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Forearms, Glutes, Lower back, Traps
steps: Stand on a low, stable platform holding a barbell at your thighs, feet hip-width apart, knees softly bent.
Brace, then push your hips back and slide the bar down your legs, keeping it close and your back flat.
The platform lets you lower a little further. Stop when your hamstrings are fully stretched, before your back rounds.
Push your hips forward to return to standing, finishing tall without leaning back.

rope-climb.muscles: Primary: Lats · Secondary: Biceps, Forearms, Mid back, Shoulders
steps: Grip the rope overhead with both hands and wrap it round one leg, pinning it between your feet.
Squeeze your feet on the rope and stand up on them, then reach your hands higher.
Lift your knees, re-grip the rope with your feet, and repeat to climb in steady stages.
Come down hand under hand with your feet controlling the speed. Never slide down, and climb over a mat.
Attach a rope to a high pulley. Kneel facing the stack and hold the rope ends beside your head.
Keeping your hips still, curl your torso down, bringing your elbows towards your thighs.
Think of rounding your spine rather than bending at the hips. Breathe out as you crunch.
Uncurl slowly back to the start, keeping tension on the cable.
Attach a rope to a high pulley. Stand facing it, hinge forward slightly and hold the rope with arms straight in front.
Keeping your arms nearly straight, sweep the rope down in an arc towards your thighs, pulling the ends apart at the bottom.
Feel your lats doing the work and keep your shoulders down away from your ears.
Let the rope rise slowly back to the start without letting your shoulders shrug up.
Sit on the floor with knees bent and heels down. Lean back until you feel your abs working, back straight.
Hold your hands together in front of your chest, or hold a light weight.
Rotate your shoulders to one side, then turn through the centre to the other side, moving from your ribs.
Keep your chest up and move with control. Lift your feet off the floor only when this feels easy.

sandbag-load.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Abs, Biceps, Calves, Forearms, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back, Mid back, Shoulders, Traps
steps: Stand over the sandbag with feet about shoulder-width, and the platform or target in front of you.
Squat down, wrap your arms under the bag and pull it into your lap, keeping your back as flat as you can.
Stand up explosively, driving your hips forward and hugging the bag high on your chest.
Push the bag up onto the platform. Learn the movement with a light bag first.

scapular-pull-up.muscles: Primary: Traps · Secondary: Lats, Mid back
steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder-width, arms fully straight.
Without bending your elbows, pull your shoulder blades down and together so your body rises a little.
Hold for a moment, feeling the muscles between and below your shoulder blades.
Relax back into a full hang slowly, then repeat.
Start in a lunge, one foot forward and one back, both knees bent and torso upright.
Jump straight up and switch your legs in the air so the back foot lands in front.
Land softly into the lunge on the other side, bending both knees to absorb the landing.
Keep your chest up and your front knee over your foot. Rest if your landings get sloppy.
Anchor a band low in front of you. Sit on a bench or box and loop the band round one or both ankles.
Start with your legs extended and the band under light tension, sitting tall.
Bend your knees to pull your heels back under the seat against the band. Feel it in the backs of your thighs.
Straighten your legs slowly back to the start, controlling the band all the way.
Sit on an upright bench in a rack with your back supported. Set the bar just below shoulder height and the safeties low.
Grip slightly wider than shoulder-width, unrack and hold the bar at the top of your chest. Brace your stomach.
Press the bar straight overhead until your arms are straight, moving your head back slightly to let it pass.
Lower slowly to the top of your chest. Keep your back against the pad throughout.
Sit on the end of a bench with feet flat, and rest an empty or very light bar across your upper back.
Hold the bar with both hands and sit tall, bracing your stomach.
Rotate your torso slowly to one side, then back through the centre to the other side.
Keep your hips facing forward and the movement controlled. Never whip the bar round.
Sit on the end of a bench and lean forward with a flat back, holding a dumbbell in one hand.
Lift that elbow so your upper arm is level with your body, with the forearm hanging down.
Straighten your arm back until it is in line with your body, keeping your upper arm still.
Lower the dumbbell slowly back to the start. Swap arms after the set.
Sit on the end of a bench with feet together and lean forward so your chest is close to your thighs.
Hold light dumbbells under your legs, palms facing each other and elbows slightly bent.
Raise the dumbbells out to the sides until your arms are level with your shoulders.
Lower slowly without lifting your chest or swinging.
Sit on the end of a bench and lean forward with a flat back, a dumbbell in each hand.
Raise both elbows so your upper arms sit level with your body, forearms hanging down.
Straighten both arms back until they are in line with your torso, keeping your upper arms still.
Lower the dumbbells slowly back to the start.

seated-cable-rows.muscles: Primary: Mid back · Secondary: Biceps, Lats, Shoulders
steps: Sit at the row station with your feet on the platform and knees slightly bent. Grab the handle with straight arms.
Sit tall with your chest up and back neutral, leaning back only slightly.
Pull the handle towards your lower stomach, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Let your arms straighten slowly back to the start without rounding your back.
Place a bench between two low pulleys, or use a cable press station. Sit tall and hold the handles at shoulder height.
Brace your stomach and keep your back against the pad if there is one.
Press the handles up until your arms are straight overhead, bringing them slightly together.
Lower slowly back to shoulder height, keeping tension on the cables.
Sit on the machine with the balls of your feet on the platform and the pad resting snugly on your lower thighs.
Release the safety catch and let your heels drop slowly until you feel a stretch in your calves.
Push up onto the balls of your feet as high as you can and squeeze at the top.
Lower slowly back into the stretch. Replace the catch before you get off.
Sit on the end of a bench with feet wide. Hold a light barbell with an underhand grip, hands close together.
Lean forward and rest the backs of your upper arms against your inner thighs, arms straight.
Curl the bar up towards your chest while keeping your arms against your thighs.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly to straight arms.
Sit on a bench with your back upright, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing forward.
Keep your elbows pinned to your sides and curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly to straight arms without swinging.
Sit tall on a bench holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing forward.
Turn your palms slightly outwards so the dumbbells point away from your body.
Curl the dumbbells up and slightly out, keeping your elbows by your sides.
Lower slowly back to straight arms, keeping the same outward angle.
Sit on a bench and rest your forearms on your thighs, palms down, with your wrists just past your knees.
Hold a light dumbbell in each hand and let your wrists bend down gently.
Lift the backs of your hands up as high as you can by bending only at the wrist.
Lower slowly back down. Keep your forearms flat on your thighs.
Sit on a bench and rest your forearms on your thighs, palms up, with your wrists just past your knees.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand and let them lower gently towards the floor, bending at the wrist.
Curl your wrists up as high as you can, keeping your forearms on your thighs.
Lower slowly back into the stretch.
Sit on a bench set upright, back against the pad, holding dumbbells at shoulder height with palms facing forward.
Brace your stomach and keep your feet planted.
Press the dumbbells overhead until your arms are straight, bringing them slightly towards each other.
Lower slowly back to shoulder height with your elbows under your wrists.
Sit on the end of a flat bench and hold its sides behind you. Lean back slightly with legs extended forward.
Tighten your stomach and bring your knees in towards your chest while leaning your chest towards them.
Push your legs back out and lean back again, stopping before your feet touch the floor.
Keep the movement smooth and your back neutral. Breathe out as you pull in.
Sit on the end of a bench with feet wide and flat, and a light barbell across your upper back.
Brace your stomach and sit tall with a neutral spine.
Hinge forward from your hips, keeping your back flat, until your chest nears the bench or your back starts to round.
Squeeze your glutes and lower back to sit upright again. Keep the load light.
Sit on a bench with feet flat, and fit the head harness securely with a light weight hanging from it.
Lean forward, hands on your thighs, and let your head drop gently so your chin comes towards your chest.
Lift your head slowly by extending your neck until you are looking straight ahead.
Lower slowly with control. Start very light and never jerk the weight.
Adjust the machine so your knees line up with its pivot and the lower pad sits just above your heels.
Sit back with the thigh pad locked firmly over your legs, and hold the handles.
Curl your heels down and back as far as you can, squeezing the backs of your thighs.
Let your legs straighten slowly back to the start without letting the weights crash.
Sit on the floor and lean back onto your hands, legs straight out and lifted slightly off the floor.
Pull your knees in towards your chest while bringing your chest slightly forward to meet them.
Straighten your legs back out and lean back again, keeping your feet off the floor if you can.
Keep your back neutral and move smoothly.
Sit on a bench and rest one forearm on your thigh, palm down, with your wrist just past your knee.
Hold a light dumbbell and let your wrist bend down gently.
Raise the back of your hand as high as you can, moving only at the wrist.
Lower slowly, then swap arms after the set.
Sit on a bench and rest one forearm on your thigh, palm up, with your wrist just past your knee.
Let the dumbbell lower slowly by bending your wrist towards the floor.
Curl your wrist up as high as you can, keeping your forearm on your thigh.
Lower slowly, then swap arms after the set.

seated-one-arm-cable-pulley-rows.muscles: Primary: Mid back · Secondary: Biceps, Lats, Traps
steps: Attach a single handle to a low pulley. Sit with feet braced and knees slightly bent, holding the handle in one hand.
Sit tall with your chest up and your arm straight in front, letting your shoulder reach forward a little.
Pull the handle to your side, driving your elbow back close to your body without twisting your torso.
Let your arm straighten slowly back to the start. Swap sides after the set.
Sit on a bench and rest your forearms on your thighs, palms up, holding a barbell with your wrists past your knees.
Let the bar roll down gently by bending your wrists towards the floor.
Curl your wrists up as high as you can, keeping your forearms flat on your thighs.
Lower slowly back down.
Sit on a bench and rest your forearms on your thighs, palms down, holding a light barbell with wrists past your knees.
Let your wrists bend down gently to lower the bar.
Lift the bar by raising the backs of your hands as high as you can, moving only at the wrist.
Lower slowly back down. Use less weight than for the palms-up version.
Sit on the end of a bench, back upright, with a dumbbell in each hand hanging at your sides.
With a slight bend in your elbows, raise the dumbbells out to the sides until your arms are level with your shoulders.
Lead with your elbows and keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.
Lower slowly back to your sides.
Sit on a bench with back support, holding one dumbbell with both hands over your head, arms straight.
Keep your elbows pointing forward and close to your head.
Lower the dumbbell slowly behind your head by bending your elbows until you feel a stretch in the backs of your arms.
Straighten your arms to press it back overhead.
Attach a short bar to a low pulley. Sit on a bench facing it and rest your forearms on your thighs, palms up.
Hold the bar with your wrists just past your knees and let it pull your wrists down gently.
Curl your wrists up as high as you can, keeping your forearms still.
Lower slowly back to the stretch.
Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing forward. Brace your stomach.
Press one dumbbell overhead to a straight arm.
As you lower it, press the other one up, so the arms move like a see-saw.
Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning to either side as you alternate.

shotgun-row.muscles: Primary: Lats · Secondary: Biceps, Mid back
steps: Attach a single handle to a low pulley. Stand facing it with a staggered stance, holding the handle in one hand.
Start with your arm straight and your palm facing down, torso tall and slightly leaned forward.
Row the handle towards your hip, turning your palm to face up as your elbow travels back past your body.
Return slowly to straight arm, turning the palm back down. Swap sides after the set.
With feet about shoulder-width apart, stand on the centre of a resistance band and hold an end in each hand at shoulder height.
Brace your stomach and keep your back neutral.
Press your hands straight overhead until your arms are straight.
Lower slowly back to shoulder height, controlling the band all the way.
Lie on your side with your forearm on the floor, elbow under your shoulder, and legs stacked.
Lift your hips so your body forms a straight line from head to feet.
Hold the position, breathing steadily and keeping your hips from sagging.
Lower slowly and repeat on the other side. Bend your knees to make it easier.

side-hop-sprint.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Abductors, Adductors, Calves, Hamstrings
steps: Stand beside a low cone or line with feet together and knees slightly bent.
Hop sideways over it and back several times, staying light on the balls of your feet.
On the last landing, turn and sprint forward for a short distance.
Walk back to recover before the next round. Keep landings soft and controlled.
Lie on one side with your legs straight and stacked. Place your top hand behind your head.
Squeeze your side and lift your legs while raising your upper body, bringing them together.
Hold briefly at the top, feeling the side of your waist work.
Lower slowly back down, then repeat before switching sides.
Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, feet hip-width apart.
With a slight bend in your elbows, raise the dumbbells out to the sides until your arms are level with your shoulders.
Lead with your elbows and keep your shoulders down.
Lower slowly without swinging. Choose a light weight.
Stand tall with a light dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Raise them out to the sides to shoulder height, then bring your arms round to the front while keeping them at that height.
Lower the dumbbells in front of you to your thighs.
Reverse the path on the next rep: raise to the front, sweep out to the sides and lower. Keep the weight light.

side-standing-long-jump.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Stand side-on to your jumping direction with feet about shoulder-width apart.
Dip into a quarter squat and swing your arms, then jump sideways as far as you can.
Land softly on both feet, bending your knees to absorb the landing and keeping your knees over your toes.
Reset fully, then jump back the other way.

side-to-side-chins.muscles: Primary: Lats · Secondary: Biceps, Forearms, Mid back, Shoulders
steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with a wide overhand grip and your arms straight.
Pull yourself up and towards one hand, so your head moves next to that side of the bar.
Shift across to the other side while still up, then lower slowly to a full hang.
Alternate which side you start with. Keep your body steady and avoid swinging.

side-to-side-box-shuffle.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Abductors, Adductors, Calves, Hamstrings
steps: Stand beside a low box with one foot on top of it and the other on the floor.
Push through the top foot to hop across the box, landing with the other foot on top and the first foot on the floor.
Keep your arms moving and your chest up as you shuffle back and forth.
Stay light on your feet and stop if your landings become heavy.
Set a pulley at shoulder height or above. Stand side-on to it holding the handle in the far-side hand, arm out wide.
Keep a slight bend in your elbow and step away until you feel tension.
Sweep your arm across in front of your body in a wide arc, squeezing your chest.
Let your arm return slowly to the start. Swap sides after the set.
Set one end of a barbell in a landmine or corner and load the other end. Stand facing it in a staggered stance.
Hold the loaded end at shoulder height in one hand, with your elbow bent and tucked.
Dip slightly, then drive through your legs and press the bar up and forward until your arm is straight.
Lower it back to your shoulder with control. Swap sides after the set.
Get into a push-up position with your feet set wide for balance and one hand under your chest.
Put your free hand behind your back and brace your stomach so your hips stay level.
Lower your chest towards the floor with control, keeping your elbow close to your side.
Push back up to a straight arm. Use an incline, such as a bench, to make it easier.

single-cone-sprint-drill.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Place a cone a short distance away and start in an athletic stance.
Sprint to the cone, driving your knees and arms.
Plant, turn tightly round the cone and sprint back to the start.
Walk back and recover fully before the next rep.
Stand in front of a high box with your back to it, standing on one leg with the other foot lifted slightly.
Reach your arms forward for balance and sit your hips back and down until you lightly touch the box.
Keep your knee in line with your toes and your chest up.
Drive through your standing foot to stand back up. Lower the box as you get stronger.

single-leg-hop-progression.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Abductors, Adductors, Calves, Hamstrings
steps: Stand on one leg with your knee slightly bent and arms ready to swing.
Hop forward a short distance and land softly on the same leg, knee over your toes.
Hold the landing for a moment before the next hop.
As you get steadier, lengthen the hop or link hops together. Switch legs after each set.

single-leg-lateral-hop.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Abductors, Adductors, Calves, Hamstrings
steps: Stand on one leg beside a line or low cone, knee slightly bent.
Hop sideways over the line and land softly on the same leg.
Stick the landing with your knee over your toes, then hop back.
Keep your hips level and your chest up. Switch legs after the set.
Adjust the machine so your knee lines up with the pivot and the pad rests on your lower shin.
Sit back and hold the handles, with one leg under the pad.
Straighten that leg until it is fully extended, squeezing the front of your thigh.
Lower slowly. Swap legs after the set.

single-leg-stride-jump.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Abductors, Adductors, Calves, Hamstrings
steps: Stand beside a bench or low box and place your inside foot on top of it.
Swing your arms and push through the top foot to jump as high as you can.
Land with the same foot back on the box and the other on the floor, absorbing the landing.
Reset before the next jump. Switch sides after the set.
Stand tall holding one dumbbell by its handle with both hands in front of your thighs.
Keeping your arms nearly straight, raise the dumbbell in front of you to shoulder height.
Pause briefly without leaning back.
Lower slowly back to your thighs.
Stand tall on one leg with a slight bend in the knee.
Jump up and kick the heel of your free leg towards your bottom.
Land softly on the same foot and go straight into the next jump.
Stay tall and light. Switch legs after the set.
Lie on your back with one knee bent, foot flat, and the other leg straight or held up.
Push through the heel of your planted foot and lift your hips until your body is straight from shoulder to knee.
Squeeze your glutes at the top and keep your hips level.
Lower slowly. Swap legs after the set.
Stand facing a low box with one foot on top of it.
Push hard through the top foot to jump straight up, swinging your arms.
Land with the same foot back on the box, bending your knee to absorb the landing.
Reset and repeat. Switch legs after the set.
Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat. Cross your arms on your chest or rest your fingertips by your ears.
Tighten your stomach and curl up, lifting your head, shoulders and back until you are sitting up.
Lower back down slowly, one part of your spine at a time.
Avoid pulling on your head. Breathe out as you rise.

sled-drag-harness.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Put on the harness and attach it to the sled with enough strap to walk freely.
Lean forward slightly and walk or drive forward, pushing through the balls of your feet.
Keep your back neutral and your steps strong and steady.
Take short, powerful strides and keep the strap taut.

sled-overhead-backward-walk.muscles: Primary: Shoulders · Secondary: Calves, Mid back, Quads
steps: Attach straps to the sled. Face it and hold the straps with arms straight overhead.
Step back until the straps are taut, bracing your stomach.
Walk backwards with steady steps, keeping your arms overhead and your ribs down.
Choose a light sled. Stop if you lose your overhead position.
Attach straps to a light sled. Face away from it and hold the straps with hands behind your head, elbows bent and pointing up.
Step forward until the straps are taut and lean slightly forward.
Straighten your arms forward overhead, keeping your elbows high.
Bend your elbows to return, take a step forward, and repeat.

sled-push.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Chest, Glutes, Hamstrings, Triceps
steps: Stand behind the sled and grip the poles with your arms straight or bent, depending on the height.
Lean forward so your body is at an angle and brace your stomach.
Drive the sled forward with short, powerful steps, pushing through the balls of your feet.
Keep your back neutral and your head in line with your body.
Attach straps to a light sled. Face it and hold a strap in each hand with your arms straight out in front.
Step back until the straps are taut.
Pull your arms out to the sides in a wide arc, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Bring your arms back in, step back, and repeat.

sled-row.muscles: Primary: Mid back · Secondary: Biceps, Lats
steps: Attach straps to the sled. Face it and hold a strap in each hand with your arms straight.
Step back until the straps are taut, sink into a quarter squat and brace your stomach.
Row the straps to your ribs, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades.
Straighten your arms, step back and repeat.

sledgehammer-swings.muscles: Primary: Abs · Secondary: Calves, Forearms, Lats, Mid back, Shoulders
steps: Stand in front of a tyre with feet about shoulder-width apart, holding the sledgehammer with both hands.
Lift the hammer up and over one shoulder, sliding your top hand down towards the head as you swing.
Bring the hammer down onto the tyre, bending your knees and tightening your stomach.
Control the rebound and alternate shoulders. Keep your back neutral throughout.
Set an incline bench under the Smith machine bar. Lie back and hold the bar with straight arms over your chest.
Keep your arms straight and your elbows locked.
Push the bar up by reaching your shoulders forward and lifting your shoulder blades off the bench.
Lower the bar slowly by letting your shoulder blades settle back onto the bench.
Set the Smith machine bar at about hip height. Stand with your back to it and grip it behind you, arms straight.
Unhook the bar and stand tall.
Shrug your shoulders straight up towards your ears, keeping your arms straight.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly.
Set a flat bench in the Smith machine so the bar sits over your lower chest. Set the safety stops.
Lie down, grip slightly wider than your shoulders, and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Unhook the bar and lower it slowly to your lower chest.
Press it back up to straight arms. Rehook the bar at the end.

smith-machine-bent-over-row.muscles: Primary: Mid back · Secondary: Biceps, Lats, Shoulders
steps: Set the Smith machine bar at knee height. Stand close to it and grip it with your hands shoulder-width apart.
Hinge forward from your hips with a flat back until your torso is at about 45 degrees.
Unhook the bar and row it towards your lower stomach, driving your elbows back.
Lower slowly to straight arms, keeping your back flat.
Stand on a small raised block under the Smith machine bar, with the balls of your feet on the edge.
Rest the bar on your upper back, unhook it and stand tall.
Rise onto your toes as high as you can, squeezing your calves.
Lower your heels slowly into a stretch, then repeat.
Set a flat bench in the Smith machine so the bar sits over your lower chest. Set the safety stops.
Lie down and grip the bar with your hands about shoulder-width apart.
Unhook the bar and lower it slowly to your lower chest, keeping your elbows tucked in.
Press it back up to straight arms. Rehook the bar at the end.
Set a decline bench in the Smith machine so the bar sits over your lower chest. Set the safety stops.
Lie down with your legs secured, grip slightly wider than your shoulders.
Unhook the bar and lower it slowly to your lower chest.
Press it back up to straight arms. Rehook the bar at the end.

smith-machine-hang-power-clean.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Glutes, Lower back, Quads, Shoulders, Traps
steps: Set the Smith machine bar at mid-thigh. Stand close, grip just outside your legs and unhook the bar.
Hinge slightly with a flat back, then drive up through your legs and hips.
Shrug and pull the bar upwards, then quickly turn your elbows under to catch it at shoulder height.
Stand tall, then lower the bar back to your thighs with control. Learn it with light loads first.
Set the Smith machine bar low. Lie on your back under it and press the soles of your feet against the bar.
Hold the floor or the machine for support and keep your knees bent.
Unhook the bar and push it upwards by curling your hips off the floor.
Lower slowly back down. Set the safety stops to catch the bar.
Set an incline bench in the Smith machine so the bar sits over your upper chest. Set the safety stops.
Lie down and grip slightly wider than your shoulders, pulling your shoulder blades back.
Unhook the bar and lower it slowly to your upper chest.
Press it back up to straight arms. Rehook the bar at the end.

smith-machine-leg-press.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Lie on your back under the Smith machine and place your feet on the bar about hip-width apart.
Set the safety stops so they catch the bar if you lose control.
Unhook the bar and bend your knees to lower it slowly towards your chest.
Press it back up to straight legs. Rehook the bar at the end.
Stand side-on to the Smith machine and grip the bar in the middle with one hand.
Unhook the bar and stand tall with your arm straight.
Lift the bar towards your chest by raising your elbow up and out to the side.
Lower slowly. Swap sides after the set.
Set a bench upright in the Smith machine so the bar lowers to your upper chest. Set the safety stops.
Sit tall and grip slightly wider than your shoulders.
Unhook the bar and press it overhead until your arms are straight.
Lower slowly to your upper chest. Rehook the bar at the end.

smith-machine-pistol-squat.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Set the Smith machine bar at shoulder height and rest it on your upper back. Stand on one leg with the other lifted forward.
Unhook the bar and set the safety stops to catch it if you lose balance.
Squat slowly down on your standing leg, keeping your knee over your toes.
Push back up to standing. Swap legs after the set.
Stand with your heels on a raised block under the Smith machine bar, toes hanging off the edge.
Rest the bar on your upper back, unhook it and stand tall.
Lift your toes up towards your shins as far as you can.
Lower slowly back into a stretch.

smith-machine-squat.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back
steps: Set the Smith machine bar at shoulder height and set the safety stops.
Step under the bar, rest it on your upper back and set your feet slightly forward of your hips.
Unhook the bar and sit down into a squat, keeping your chest up and knees over your toes.
Push back up to standing. Rehook the bar at the end.

smith-machine-stiff-legged-deadlift.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Glutes, Lower back
steps: Set the Smith machine bar at thigh height. Stand close to it and grip it at shoulder width.
Unhook the bar and stand tall with your knees softly bent.
Push your hips back and lower the bar down your legs until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Drive your hips forward to stand back up. Keep your back flat throughout.

smith-machine-upright-row.muscles: Primary: Traps · Secondary: Biceps, Mid back, Shoulders
steps: Set the Smith machine bar at thigh height. Stand close and grip it with your hands shoulder-width apart.
Unhook the bar and stand tall with your arms straight.
Lift the bar towards your chest by raising your elbows up and out to the sides.
Lower slowly. Keep the bar close to your body.

smith-single-leg-split-squat.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Set the Smith machine bar at shoulder height and set the safety stops.
Rest the bar on your upper back and take a long step forward with one foot, back heel lifted.
Unhook the bar and lower your back knee towards the floor, keeping your front knee over your toes.
Push through your front foot to stand back up. Swap legs after the set.

snatch.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Biceps, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back, Shoulders, Traps, Triceps
steps: Stand with the bar over mid-foot and grip it wide. Squat down with your back flat and chest up.
Push through your legs and lift the bar close to your body until it passes your knees.
Drive your hips forward and shrug hard, then pull yourself under the bar.
Catch it overhead with straight arms in a squat, then stand up. Learn it with light loads and coaching.

snatch-balance.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Rest a light barbell on your upper back with a wide snatch grip, feet hip-width apart.
Dip slightly at the knees, then push the bar up while quickly dropping into a squat.
Catch the bar overhead with straight arms at the bottom of the squat.
Stand up with the bar overhead. Learn it with light loads.

snatch-deadlift.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Forearms, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back, Quads, Traps
steps: Stand with the bar over mid-foot and grip it wide. Squat down with your back flat and chest up.
Brace hard and push through your legs to lift the bar, keeping it close to your body.
Stand tall with your hips through, keeping your arms straight.
Lower the bar back to the floor with control.

snatch-pull.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Lower back, Quads, Traps
steps: Stand with the bar over mid-foot and grip it wide. Squat down with your back flat and chest up.
Push through your legs to lift the bar past your knees, keeping it close to your body.
Drive your hips forward and shrug hard, rising onto your toes.
Lower the bar back to the floor with control. Learn it with light loads.
Stand tall holding a barbell with a wide snatch grip, arms straight and bar at your thighs.
Brace your stomach and keep your back flat.
Shrug your shoulders straight up towards your ears as high as you can.
Lower slowly back down.

snatch-from-blocks.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Forearms, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back, Shoulders, Traps, Triceps
steps: Set the bar on blocks at the height you want and grip it wide. Stand close with your back flat and chest up.
Push through your legs and drive your hips forward, keeping the bar close.
Shrug hard and pull yourself under the bar, catching it overhead in a squat with straight arms.
Stand up, then lower the bar back to the blocks. Learn it with light loads and coaching.
Anchor a band low behind you. Face away from it and hold the ends with your hands behind your head, elbows up.
Step forward until the band is taut and brace your stomach.
Straighten your arms quickly overhead, keeping your elbows high.
Bend your elbows slowly to return, then repeat with speed.

speed-box-squat.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Set a box behind you at the depth you want and set the safety stops. Rest a lighter barbell on your upper back.
Take a wide stance and brace your stomach.
Sit back onto the box with control, keeping your chest up and shins upright.
Stand up explosively. Move the bar fast rather than using heavy weight.

speed-squats.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back
steps: Load a light barbell, well below your normal squat weight, and set it on your upper back with the rack safeties at a height just below your lowest squat position.
Stand with feet about shoulder-width apart, brace your midsection and take a breath.
Sit down under control to your usual depth, keeping your chest up and knees tracking over your toes.
Drive up out of the bottom as fast as you can while staying balanced. Speed is the point, not the load.
Reset your breath and brace at the top before each rep so every one is quick and clean.
Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, a light dumbbell in each hand held down by one hip.
Brace your abs and turn your trunk, swinging both dumbbells up and across your body towards the opposite shoulder.
Let your hips and feet pivot slightly so the rotation comes from your trunk, not a twisting lower back.
Bring the dumbbells back down past the starting hip with control, then continue to the other side.

spider-crawl.muscles: Primary: Abs · Secondary: Chest, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Start in a high plank with hands under your shoulders and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Step one hand forward and bring the knee on the same side up and out towards that elbow.
Lower your chest a little as you move if you can, keeping your hips low and your back flat.
Switch sides with each step and crawl forward slowly, keeping your abs tight throughout.
Set an incline bench at a steep angle and lie face down on it, chest at the top edge, holding an EZ bar with an underhand grip.
Let your arms hang straight down in front of the bench, upper arms vertical.
Curl the bar up towards your shoulders without letting your elbows drift forward.
Squeeze your biceps at the top, then lower slowly until your arms are straight again.

split-clean.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Forearms, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back, Shoulders, Traps
steps: Learn this with light weight first. Stand over the bar, feet hip-width, grip just outside your legs, back flat and chest up.
Push the floor away to lift the bar past your knees, then extend hips, knees and ankles hard as it reaches your upper thighs.
As the bar rises, pull yourself under it and split your feet, one forward and one back, catching the bar on your shoulders with elbows high.
Stabilise, then step the front foot back and the back foot forward until your feet are level before lowering the bar.

split-jerk.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Glutes, Hamstrings, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Practise with light weight first. Hold the bar across the front of your shoulders, elbows slightly forward, feet hip-width.
Brace, dip a few centimetres by bending your knees with your torso upright, then drive up hard through your legs.
As the bar leaves your shoulders, push yourself under it and split your feet front and back, locking your arms overhead.
Hold steady, step the front foot back halfway, then bring the back foot forward to meet it. Lower the bar to your shoulders under control.

split-jump.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Stand in a split stance, one foot forward and one back, both knees slightly bent and your torso upright.
Dip into a shallow lunge, then jump straight up, using your arms to help.
Swap your legs in the air so the other foot lands in front.
Land softly on the balls of your feet, bend into the next lunge and go again. Stop if your landings get heavy or sloppy.

split-snatch.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Calves, Forearms, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back, Quads, Shoulders, Traps, Triceps
steps: Learn this with an empty bar or very light load. Take a wide grip, stand over the bar with a flat back and chest up.
Lift the bar steadily off the floor, then extend hips, knees and ankles explosively as it passes your upper thighs.
Pull yourself under the bar and split your feet front and back, catching it overhead on straight, locked arms.
Stabilise, bring your feet together with small steps, then lower the bar to your hips and back to the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand by your sides and take a long step forward so you are in a split stance, back heel raised.
Keep your torso upright and lower straight down until your back knee is just above the floor.
Push through the whole front foot to stand back up, keeping your front knee in line with your toes.
Finish all your reps on one side before switching legs.

squat-jerk.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Shoulders, Triceps
