steps: This demands good overhead mobility, so learn it with light weight. Hold the bar on the front of your shoulders, feet hip-width.
Brace, dip straight down a few centimetres, then drive up hard through your legs.
As the bar rises, drop into a full squat underneath it, catching it overhead with locked arms.
Hold it steady, stand up with the bar still overhead, then lower it to your shoulders under control.

squat-with-bands.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Adductors, Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back
steps: Attach a band to each end of the barbell and anchor them to the base of the rack or to heavy dumbbells. Set the safeties just below your bottom position.
Unrack the bar onto your upper back, step back and set your feet about shoulder-width apart.
Brace hard and sit down under control. The bands will feel lighter as you go down.
Drive up through your whole foot, staying braced as the bands pull harder near the top.

squat-with-chains.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Adductors, Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back
steps: Hang a chain from each end of the barbell so part of it rests on the floor when you stand. Set the safeties just below your bottom position.
Unrack the bar onto your upper back, step back and set your feet about shoulder-width apart.
Brace and squat down with control. More of the chain settles on the floor, so the load gets lighter as you descend.
Drive up steadily, keeping your chest up as the chain lifts off the floor and the weight increases.

squat-with-plate-movers.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Abductors, Adductors, Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Set up a barbell back squat with the extra loading attachments fitted to the bar ends, and set the rack safeties just below your bottom position.
Unrack the bar onto your upper back, step back and place your feet about shoulder-width apart.
Brace your midsection and sit down under control to your normal depth, knees tracking over your toes.
Drive back up through your whole foot, staying tight as the load changes through the lift. Rack the bar carefully when done.

squats-with-bands.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back
steps: Stand on the middle of a long resistance band with feet shoulder-width apart, and loop the other end over your shoulders or hold it at shoulder height.
Brace your abs and push your hips back as you bend your knees, keeping your chest up.
Squat as low as you can while your back stays neutral and your heels stay down.
Drive up to standing against the band's pull and squeeze your glutes at the top.
Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell at each shoulder with palms facing forward.
Brace your abs and squeeze your glutes so your lower back does not arch.
Press one dumbbell straight overhead until your arm is straight, keeping the other at your shoulder.
Lower it back to your shoulder with control, then press the other side.
Take a barbell from a rack onto your upper back as you would for a squat, and stand with the balls of your feet on a low, stable block if you have one.
Keep your knees almost straight and your body tall and braced.
Rise up onto your toes as high as you can and pause briefly at the top.
Lower your heels slowly until you feel a stretch in your calves, then go again.
Only do this if you can hold the bar behind your head comfortably. Take the bar from a rack onto your upper back with a grip wider than shoulders.
Stand tall, brace your abs and squeeze your glutes. Keep your head neutral, not pushed forward.
Press the bar straight up until your arms are locked out overhead.
Lower it slowly behind your head to about ear level, stopping short of any discomfort in your shoulders.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand, hinge forward from your hips with a flat back and rest your other hand on your thigh or a bench.
Lift your working elbow so your upper arm is level with your torso, elbow bent at 90 degrees.
Straighten your arm back behind you, moving only at the elbow, and squeeze your triceps.
Lower the dumbbell slowly back to the bent position without letting your upper arm drop.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand, bend your knees slightly and hinge forward until your torso is nearly level with the floor, back flat.
Bring your upper arms up alongside your body, elbows bent so the dumbbells hang beneath them.
Straighten both arms back behind you, keeping your upper arms still.
Pause with your triceps squeezed, then bend your elbows slowly back to the start.
Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and hold it with an underhand grip, arms straight, standing close to the stack.
Stand tall with your elbows tucked in at your sides.
Curl the bar up towards your shoulders without swinging or leaning back.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly until your arms are straight.
Hold a barbell across the front of your shoulders with a grip a little wider than shoulder-width, standing tall and braced.
Press the bar up just far enough to clear the top of your head.
Guide it back to rest lightly behind your head, then press it up and forward again to the front.
Keep the movement smooth and use a light weight. Skip the behind-the-head part if it bothers your shoulders.
Set both pulleys around chest height, take a handle in each hand and step forward so the cables are under tension.
Stand in a staggered stance, handles beside your chest, elbows slightly below shoulder height.
Brace your abs and press the handles forward until your arms are nearly straight in front of your chest.
Let the handles come back slowly to your chest without letting the stack pull you off balance.
Set a pulley at its lowest point and stand side-on to it, holding the handle with both hands near your outside knee.
Stand with feet wider than hips and knees slightly bent, abs braced.
Pull the handle diagonally up and across your body to above the opposite shoulder, turning your trunk and pivoting your back foot.
Return along the same line with control, then finish your reps before switching sides.
Set a pulley at its highest point and stand side-on to it, holding the handle with both hands above the near shoulder.
Stand with feet wider than hips and knees soft, arms nearly straight.
Pull the handle down and across your body towards your opposite hip, rotating through your trunk and pivoting your back foot.
Let the handle travel back up the same path slowly. Finish one side, then turn around.
Set the shoulder pads so you can stand under them with the balls of your feet on the platform edge and heels hanging off.
Stand tall with knees straight but not locked, and your body braced.
Push up onto your toes as high as you can and pause at the top.
Lower your heels slowly below the platform until you feel a stretch in your calves.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand and bend forward from your hips, resting your free hand on a bench or your knee.
Let your working arm hang straight down, palm facing forward.
Curl the dumbbell up towards your shoulder, keeping your upper arm still and pointing at the floor.
Squeeze your biceps at the top, then lower slowly until your arm is straight.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand by your sides and stand with the balls of your feet on a step, heels hanging off.
Stand tall with knees nearly straight. Keep a light touch on something for balance if you can.
Rise up onto your toes as high as you can and pause at the top.
Lower your heels slowly until you feel a stretch in your calves, then rise again.
Stand with feet hip-width apart and hold a dumbbell at each shoulder, palms facing forward.
Brace your abs and squeeze your glutes so your lower back stays neutral.
Press both dumbbells overhead until your arms are straight, bringing them slightly in towards each other.
Lower them back to your shoulders under control.
Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip, palms facing behind you.
Keep your elbows tucked in at your sides and your wrists straight.
Curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders without swinging your body.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight. You should feel this in your forearms as well as your biceps.
Stand tall holding a light dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs, palms facing your legs.
Brace your abs and keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise the dumbbells forward and up in front of you until your arms point overhead, without leaning back.
Lower them slowly along the same arc back to your thighs.
Stand tall and hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands cupping the top end, arms straight.
Brace your abs so your lower back does not arch, and keep your elbows pointing forward.
Bend your elbows to lower the dumbbell behind your head until you feel a stretch in your triceps.
Straighten your arms to lift it back overhead, keeping your upper arms close to your head.
Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs, palms facing you.
Lead with your elbows and lift the dumbbells up along the front of your body.
Stop when your elbows reach about shoulder height, or lower if you feel any pinching in your shoulders.
Lower the dumbbells slowly back to your thighs.
Stand tall holding a light barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand, shoulder-width grip.
Brace your abs. Your arms stay long, with just a slight bend at the elbows.
Raise the bar forward and up until it is overhead, without leaning back or arching your lower back.
Lower it slowly back down in front of you to your thighs.
Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing in.
Curl the dumbbells up while turning your palms to face up, and let them travel slightly outwards away from your body.
Keep your elbows at your sides and squeeze your biceps at the top.
Lower the dumbbells slowly back to your sides, turning your palms to face in again.
Adjust the machine so the pad sits just above the back of your ankle and your knee lines up with the pivot.
Hold the handles, stand tall on your support leg and keep your hips square.
Curl your heel up towards your glutes, keeping your thigh still.
Lower the weight slowly until your leg is nearly straight, then switch legs after your set.

standing-long-jump.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart behind a line, on a surface that is not slippery.
Swing your arms back as you bend your knees and hips into a quarter squat.
Swing your arms forward and drive through your legs to jump as far forward as you can.
Land softly on both feet with knees bent, absorbing the landing. Walk back and reset fully between jumps.
Stand side-on to a low pulley and take the handle in your far hand, so the cable runs across the front of your body.
Hold something steady with your free hand, and keep a slight bend in your working elbow.
Raise your arm out to the side until your hand is about shoulder height.
Lower slowly back across your body. Finish your set, then switch sides.
Stand facing away from a low pulley holding a single handle in one hand, and raise that arm so your elbow points up beside your head.
Let the cable pull your hand down behind your head so your elbow is bent and your triceps are stretched.
Straighten your arm overhead, keeping your upper arm still.
Bend your elbow slowly to return. Finish your set, then switch arms.
Set the bar in a rack at upper-chest height. Take a grip just wider than shoulders and unrack it onto the front of your shoulders.
Stand with feet hip-width apart, brace your abs and squeeze your glutes.
Press the bar straight up, moving your head back slightly to let it pass, then bring your head through once it clears.
Lock out overhead with the bar over your mid-foot, then lower it under control to your shoulders.
Stand tall and pinch a weight plate between your fingers and thumb, smooth sides out, arm hanging by your side.
Keep your shoulders back and your wrist straight.
Squeeze hard and hold the plate for as long as you can keep a firm grip.
Set it down under control before your grip gives out, rather than letting it drop. Swap hands.
Attach a single handle to a low pulley and hold it in one hand with your palm facing up, arm straight.
Stand tall with your elbow tucked in at your side.
Curl the handle towards your shoulder, keeping your upper arm still.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly. Finish one arm before switching.
Stand behind an incline bench and drape the back of your working arm over the backrest, holding a dumbbell with palm up.
Let your arm extend down the pad until it is nearly straight.
Curl the dumbbell towards your shoulder, keeping your upper arm pressed into the bench.
Lower slowly without letting your elbow lock hard at the bottom. Swap arms after your set.
Stand tall holding a dumbbell in one hand, arm straight overhead with your elbow close to your head.
Brace your abs so your lower back stays neutral.
Bend your elbow to lower the dumbbell behind your head, keeping your upper arm still.
Straighten your arm to lift it back overhead. Finish your set, then switch arms.
Stand tall holding a light barbell or EZ bar overhead with a narrow overhand grip, arms straight.
Brace your abs and keep your elbows pointing forward, close to your head.
Bend your elbows to lower the bar behind your head until you feel a stretch in your triceps.
Straighten your arms to press the bar back overhead without letting your elbows flare.
Stand tall holding a dumbbell at one shoulder with your palm facing in.
Brace your abs and keep your hips and shoulders square. Rest your free hand on your hip.
Press the dumbbell straight up until your arm is straight, without leaning to the side.
Lower it back to your shoulder with control. Finish your set, then switch sides.
Stand with feet hip-width apart holding a dumbbell at each shoulder, palms facing each other.
Brace your abs and squeeze your glutes so your lower back does not arch.
Press both dumbbells straight overhead until your arms are straight.
Lower them back to your shoulders under control, keeping your palms facing in.
Stand tall holding a barbell behind your back at arm's length, hands shoulder-width apart and palms facing behind you.
Keep your arms still and let the bar roll down slightly towards your fingertips.
Curl your wrists up to lift the bar as high as you can.
Lower slowly back to the start. Only your wrists should move.
Attach a rope to a high pulley. Stand facing it and hold the rope ends beside your head.
Set your feet hip-width apart and keep your knees slightly bent.
Curl your trunk down, bringing your ribs towards your hips. The movement comes from your abs, not your arms or hips.
Uncurl slowly back to upright, keeping tension on your abs.
Stand tall and hold one end of a towel overhead with one hand, elbow bent so your hand is behind your head.
Reach your other hand behind your lower back and grab the other end of the towel.
Straighten the top arm while the bottom hand pulls down to create resistance.
Let the top elbow bend back slowly against the bottom hand's pull. Swap arms after your set.
Face a solid wall or a partner, holding a medicine ball with both hands. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Take the ball overhead and slightly behind your head, keeping your abs braced.
Throw it forward hard, driving from your trunk and following through with your arms.
Catch it or collect it, reset your stance and go again.

star-jump.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Shoulders
steps: Stand with feet together and arms by your sides, then bend into a quarter squat.
Jump up explosively, spreading your arms and legs wide into a star shape in the air.
Bring your arms and legs back together before you land.
Land softly with bent knees, reset and jump again.
Stand facing a sturdy box or bench about knee height.
Put one whole foot on the box and push through that heel to step up.
As you stand up, drive the other knee up to hip height and hold your balance briefly.
Step back down with the same leg under control. Finish your set, then switch legs.

stiff-legged-barbell-deadlift.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Glutes, Lower back
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart holding a barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip.
Keep your knees slightly bent and fixed, brace your midsection and keep your back flat.
Push your hips back and lower the bar down the front of your legs until you feel a strong hamstring stretch.
Drive your hips forward to stand back up, keeping the bar close to your legs.

stiff-legged-dumbbell-deadlift.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Glutes, Lower back
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs.
Soften your knees slightly and keep them there. Brace your abs and keep your back flat.
Hinge at your hips to lower the dumbbells along your legs until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Squeeze your glutes to stand back up, keeping the dumbbells close to your body.

stiff-leg-barbell-good-morning.muscles: Primary: Lower back · Secondary: Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Start light. Set a barbell across your upper back as for a squat and stand with feet hip-width apart.
Keep your legs nearly straight with just a slight bend at the knees, and brace your midsection.
Push your hips back and lower your chest forward with a flat back until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Drive your hips forward to return to standing, keeping your back neutral throughout.

straight-arm-dumbbell-pullover.muscles: Primary: Chest · Secondary: Lats, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Lie on a flat bench and hold one dumbbell above your chest with both hands cupping the top end.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and plant your feet firmly on the floor.
Lower the dumbbell back in an arc over your head until your arms are roughly in line with your body, or until you feel a good stretch.
Pull it back over your chest along the same arc, keeping your arms nearly straight.
Attach a straight bar to a high pulley. Stand facing it and hold the bar with an overhand, shoulder-width grip.
Step back, hinge slightly forward from your hips and keep your arms nearly straight.
Pull the bar down in an arc towards your thighs, driving with your lats rather than bending your elbows.
Let the bar rise slowly back to about head height, keeping your arms straight.

straight-bar-bench-mid-rows.muscles: Primary: Mid back · Secondary: Biceps, Lats
steps: Lie face down on a raised flat bench with a straight barbell on the floor beneath you, and grip it overhand about shoulder-width.
Let your arms hang straight and keep your chest in contact with the bench.
Row the bar up towards the underside of the bench, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower it slowly until your arms are straight again.
Set a bench to a low incline and lie face down on it, holding a light barbell with an overhand grip, arms hanging down.
Keep your chest on the pad and a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise the bar forward and up in front of you until your arms are level with your ears.
Lower slowly back down. Use a light load; your upper back and shoulders do all the work here.

stride-jump-crossover.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Abductors, Adductors, Calves, Hamstrings
steps: Stand beside a low, sturdy bench or box with the foot nearest it resting on top.
Push through the foot on the box and jump up and across to the other side.
Land with your other foot on the box and your first foot on the floor beyond it.
Land softly and keep crossing back and forth. Stop if your landings become unsteady.

sumo-deadlift.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Adductors, Forearms, Glutes, Lower back, Mid back, Quads, Traps
steps: Stand with a wide stance, toes turned out, and the bar over your mid-foot. Grip it inside your legs with arms straight down.
Push your knees out over your toes, drop your hips, lift your chest and keep your back flat.
Brace hard, then push the floor apart with your feet to drive the bar up, keeping it close to your body.
Lock out by squeezing your glutes, then lower the bar with control by pushing your hips back and bending your knees.

sumo-deadlift-with-bands.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Adductors, Forearms, Glutes, Lower back, Mid back, Quads, Traps
steps: Loop a band over each end of the bar and anchor them under the platform or to heavy dumbbells so they tighten as you stand.
Take a wide stance with toes turned out and grip the bar inside your legs, knees pushed out and back flat.
Brace and drive through your feet to lift, keeping the bar close. Expect it to get harder near the top.
Finish tall with your glutes squeezed, then lower under control. Do not let the bands snap the bar down.

sumo-deadlift-with-chains.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Abductors, Adductors, Forearms, Glutes, Lower back, Mid back, Quads, Traps
steps: Hang a chain from each end of the bar so most of it rests on the floor at the start.
Take a wide stance with toes turned out and grip the bar inside your legs, knees pushed out and back flat.
Brace and drive through your feet to lift, keeping the bar close. The chains lift off the floor and add weight as you rise.
Lock out with your glutes, then lower with control, pushing your hips back and bending your knees.
Lie on your back on the floor, knees bent, holding a medicine ball at your chest. A partner stands over you, or use a light ball you can catch.
Keep your elbows bent and your abs braced.
Push the ball straight up as hard as you can, as if doing an explosive chest press.
Catch the ball with soft, bending arms and bring it back to your chest before the next throw.

supine-one-arm-overhead-throw.muscles: Primary: Abs · Secondary: Chest, Lats, Shoulders
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, holding a light medicine ball in one hand stretched out overhead. Have a partner or a wall ahead of you.
Brace your abs and keep your lower back pressed towards the floor.
Sit up quickly and throw the ball forward from overhead with one arm.
Collect the ball, lie back down with control and repeat. Switch arms after your set.

supine-two-arm-overhead-throw.muscles: Primary: Abs · Secondary: Chest, Lats, Shoulders
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, holding a medicine ball in both hands with arms extended overhead. Face a partner or a wall.
Brace your abs so your lower back stays in contact with the floor.
Sit up explosively and throw the ball forward from overhead with both arms.
Catch or collect the ball, then lower yourself back down with control.

suspended-fallout.muscles: Primary: Abs · Secondary: Chest, Lower back, Shoulders
steps: Set suspension straps at about knee height. Hold the handles with straight arms and lean forward so your body forms a straight line.
Brace your abs and squeeze your glutes so your hips do not sag.
Let your arms move forward and up overhead as your body tilts towards the floor, only as far as you can keep your back flat.
Pull your arms back down towards your hips to bring yourself back upright.
Set suspension straps so the handles hang a few centimetres off the floor. Hold them and set up in a push-up position with arms straight.
Keep your body straight from head to heels, abs braced.
Lower your chest between the handles, keeping them steady and close to your sides.
Push back up until your arms are straight, without letting the straps wobble outwards.
Hook your feet into suspension straps set low and walk your hands out into a push-up position.
Keep your arms straight and your shoulders over your hands.
Draw your knees in towards your chest, rounding your lower back slightly.
Extend your legs back out slowly to a straight plank, without letting your hips sag.

suspended-row.muscles: Primary: Mid back · Secondary: Biceps, Lats
steps: Hold the suspension strap handles and walk your feet forward so you lean back with arms straight and body in a straight line.
Brace your abs and keep your hips up. The more upright you stand, the easier it is.
Pull your chest towards the handles, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower yourself back under control until your arms are straight.

suspended-split-squat.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Abductors, Adductors, Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Stand facing away from suspension straps set at shin height and place the top of one foot in the foot cradle behind you.
Hop your front foot forward into a split stance and stand tall.
Bend your front knee and lower straight down, letting your back leg slide back in the strap.
Push through your front foot to stand back up. Finish your set, then switch legs.

svend-press.muscles: Primary: Chest · Secondary: Forearms, Shoulders, Triceps
steps: Stand tall and press two small weight plates together between your palms, held in front of your chest.
Squeeze the plates hard so they stay together throughout.
Press the plates straight out in front of you until your arms are almost straight.
Bring them back to your chest slowly, still squeezing.

t-bar-row-with-handle.muscles: Primary: Mid back · Secondary: Biceps, Lats
steps: Load one end of a bar anchored in a corner or landmine and straddle it. Fit a handle under the bar near the plates.
Bend your knees and hinge forward with a flat back, arms straight, holding the handle.
Brace your midsection and row the handle towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower it slowly until your arms are straight, keeping your back flat throughout.
Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand pressed up over your chest, palms facing your feet.
Bend your elbows outwards so the dumbbells lower inwards towards the centre of your chest, ends touching.
Keep your upper arms still as the dumbbells come down to lightly touch your chest.
Straighten your elbows to press them back up, squeezing your triceps.
Sit in the abductor machine with your back against the pad and the pads on the outside of your knees.
Hold the handles and keep your back and hips still.
Push your knees apart as far as is comfortable, squeezing the outside of your hips.
Let them come back together slowly without letting the weight stack crash.
Sit in the adductor machine with your back against the pad and the pads on the inside of your knees.
Set the starting width so you feel a mild stretch in your inner thighs, not a strain.
Squeeze your knees together until the pads nearly meet.
Open your legs slowly back to the starting width, keeping control.

tire-flip.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Chest, Forearms, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back, Shoulders, Traps, Triceps
steps: Learn with a tyre well within your ability. Crouch close to the tyre with feet about shoulder-width, chest against it and fingers under the edge.
Keep your back flat and chest up, with hips lower than your shoulders.
Drive through your legs and hips to lift, pushing the tyre forward and up rather than deadlifting it.
As it rises past your hips, step in and push it over with your hands. Reset carefully before the next flip.
Stand inside the trap bar with feet hip-width apart, centred between the handles.
Bend your hips and knees to grip the handles, chest up and back flat.
Brace hard and push the floor away with your legs to stand up tall.
Lower the bar under control by bending your hips and knees together.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand and support yourself with your other hand and knee on a bench, back flat.
Lift your working elbow so your upper arm is level with your body, elbow bent at 90 degrees.
Straighten your arm back behind you, moving only at the elbow.
Lower the dumbbell slowly back to 90 degrees. Swap arms after your set.
Attach a rope to a pulley at about chest or head height. Face away from it and hold the rope behind your head.
Step forward into a staggered stance, lean slightly forward and point your elbows forward.
Straighten your arms forward and up until they are fully extended, keeping your upper arms still.
Bend your elbows slowly to let the rope come back behind your head.
Clip a straight or angled bar onto a high pulley and take hold of it with an overhand grip.
Stand tall and tuck your elbows in at your sides, forearms roughly level with the floor.
Push the bar down until your arms are straight, keeping your elbows still.
Let the bar rise slowly back to the start without letting your elbows move forward.
Attach a rope to a high pulley and hold an end in each hand, palms facing each other.
Stand tall with your elbows tucked at your sides.
Push the rope down and spread the ends apart at the bottom as your arms straighten.
Return slowly to the start, keeping your upper arms still.
Attach a V-bar to a high pulley and hold it with an overhand grip.
Stand tall with your elbows tucked at your sides.
Push the bar down until your arms are straight, squeezing your triceps.
Let it rise slowly back until your forearms are about level with the floor.
Lie on your back and bring your knees up towards your chest, hands lightly by your head or crossed over your chest.
Brace your abs and keep your neck relaxed.
Curl your shoulders off the floor and bring your knees in until they nearly meet your chest.
Uncurl slowly back to the start without letting your feet touch the floor.
Sit at a preacher bench and rest the backs of your upper arms on the pad, a dumbbell in each hand, palms up.
Start with your arms nearly straight, keeping a slight bend at the elbows.
Curl both dumbbells up towards your shoulders, keeping your arms on the pad.
Lower them slowly back down, stopping just short of locking your elbows.

two-arm-kettlebell-clean.muscles: Primary: Shoulders · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back, Traps
steps: Learn with light bells. Stand with two kettlebells on the floor between your feet, feet slightly wider than hips.
Hinge at your hips with a flat back to grip both handles, then hike them back slightly between your legs.
Drive your hips forward and pull the bells up close to your body, letting them turn over to rest on the backs of your forearms at your shoulders.
Stand tall with elbows tucked. Reverse the path to let them swing back down, then set them down carefully.

two-arm-kettlebell-jerk.muscles: Primary: Shoulders · Secondary: Calves, Quads, Triceps
steps: Practise with light bells first. Hold two kettlebells at your shoulders, resting on your forearms, elbows tucked.
Dip a few centimetres by bending your knees with your torso upright, then drive up hard with your legs.
As the bells rise, drop under them into a second small dip, locking your arms overhead.
Stand up fully with arms locked, then lower the bells back to your shoulders under control.
Clean two kettlebells to your shoulders so they rest on your forearms, elbows tucked in.
Stand tall, brace your abs and squeeze your glutes.
Press both bells overhead until your arms are straight, biceps near your ears.
Lower them slowly back to your shoulders.

two-arm-kettlebell-row.muscles: Primary: Mid back · Secondary: Biceps, Lats
steps: Stand with two kettlebells between your feet, bend your knees and hinge forward with a flat back to grip them.
Lift them just off the floor, arms straight and torso nearly level.
Row both bells towards your lower ribs, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight, keeping your back flat.

underhand-cable-pulldowns.muscles: Primary: Lats · Secondary: Biceps, Mid back, Shoulders
steps: Sit at a lat pulldown with your thighs under the pads and hold the bar with an underhand, shoulder-width grip.
Lean back slightly and lift your chest.
Pull the bar down to your upper chest, driving your elbows down towards your sides.
Let the bar rise slowly until your arms are straight.
Stand tall holding a barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip about shoulder-width.
Lead with your elbows and lift the bar up close to your body.
Stop when your elbows reach about shoulder height, or lower if your shoulders feel pinched.
Lower the bar slowly back to your thighs.
Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and hold it with an overhand grip about shoulder-width, standing close to the stack.
Stand tall with the bar resting against your thighs.
Lead with your elbows and pull the bar up along your body until your elbows reach about shoulder height.
Lower it slowly back to your thighs.
Stand on the middle of a resistance band with feet hip-width apart, holding an end in each hand in front of your thighs.
Stand tall with your abs braced.
Lead with your elbows and pull your hands up along your body until your elbows reach about shoulder height.
Lower slowly back down, keeping tension in the band.

v-bar-pulldown.muscles: Primary: Lats · Secondary: Biceps, Mid back, Shoulders
steps: Attach a V-bar to the high pulley and sit with your thighs under the pads, holding the handles with palms facing each other.
Lean back slightly and lift your chest, arms straight.
Pull the handle down to your upper chest, driving your elbows down and back.
Let it rise slowly until your arms are fully straight.

v-bar-pullup.muscles: Primary: Lats · Secondary: Biceps, Mid back, Shoulders
steps: Hang a V-bar over a pull-up bar and grip both handles, palms facing each other, hanging with arms straight.
Brace your abs and pull your shoulders down away from your ears.
Pull yourself up, bringing your chest towards the handles.
Lower yourself slowly until your arms are straight again.

vertical-swing.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Glutes, Quads, Shoulders
steps: Stand with feet wider than hips, holding one dumbbell by an end with both hands, arms straight.
Hinge at your hips with a flat back so the dumbbell swings back between your legs.
Drive your hips forward powerfully to swing the dumbbell up in front of you and overhead.
Let it swing back down along the same path and hinge again to absorb it. Keep a firm grip.

weighted-ball-hyperextension.muscles: Primary: Lower back · Secondary: Glutes, Hamstrings, Mid back
steps: Lie face down with your hips on an exercise ball and your feet braced against a wall, holding a weight to your chest.
Let your upper body drape over the ball with your back neutral.
Lift your chest by extending your hips and back until your body forms a straight line.
Lower slowly back over the ball. Do not arch past straight.
Lie on your side over an exercise ball with your feet braced against a wall, holding a light weight to your chest or by your head.
Let your upper body bend down over the ball towards the floor.
Lift your torso sideways, bringing your ribs towards your hip.
Lower slowly back over the ball. Finish your set, then switch sides.
Sit on the edge of a bench, hands beside your hips, and place your feet on another bench in front of you. Have a partner place a plate on your lap.
Slide off the edge so your arms take your weight, elbows pointing back.
Bend your elbows to lower your body until your upper arms are about level with the floor, or less if your shoulders complain.
Push back up until your arms are straight.
Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, holding a medicine ball against your chest.
Brace your abs and keep your neck relaxed.
Curl your shoulders off the floor, bringing your ribs towards your hips.
Lower slowly back down under control.

weighted-jump-squat.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back
steps: Use a light barbell. Set it on your upper back and stand with feet about shoulder-width apart.
Hold the bar firmly to your back, brace and dip into a quarter squat.
Jump straight up explosively, keeping the bar pinned to your back.
Land softly on the balls of your feet, bend your knees to absorb it, and reset before the next jump.

weighted-pull-ups.muscles: Primary: Lats · Secondary: Biceps, Mid back
steps: Attach a weight to a dip belt around your waist, or hold a dumbbell between your feet. Grip the bar overhand, a little wider than shoulders.
Hang with arms straight, abs braced and legs still.
Pull yourself up until your chin clears the bar, driving your elbows down.
Lower yourself slowly until your arms are straight.

weighted-sissy-squat.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart holding a light plate to your chest, with your other hand on a support for balance.
Rise onto the balls of your feet and push your knees forward while leaning your torso back in a straight line from knees to head.
Lower as far as your knees allow comfortably, keeping your hips extended.
Push through the balls of your feet to return to upright.
Lie on a decline bench with your feet secured, a band anchored behind you and held at your chest, or a weight held to your chest.
Brace your abs and keep your chin slightly tucked.
Curl up towards your knees, lifting your back off the bench one section at a time.
Lower slowly back down against the band's pull, keeping control.

weighted-squat.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Attach a weight to a dip belt around your hips and stand on two sturdy platforms, the weight hanging between them.
Stand tall with feet about shoulder-width, hands on a support for balance if needed.
Squat down, keeping your chest up and knees tracking over your toes, until your thighs are about parallel.
Drive through your feet to stand back up.
Lie on a flat bench with your eyes under the bar. Use a spotter or safety arms, and grip well wider than shoulder-width.
Plant your feet, squeeze your shoulder blades together and unrack the bar over your chest.
Lower it slowly to your mid-chest, keeping your wrists over your elbows.
Press it back up until your arms are straight, keeping your shoulders pinned to the bench.
Set yourself on a decline bench with your legs secured. Use a spotter, and take a grip well wider than shoulder-width.
Unrack the bar and hold it over your lower chest with arms straight.
Lower it slowly to your lower chest, elbows at a moderate angle from your body.
Press it back up to straight arms, keeping your shoulder blades squeezed together.
Lie on a decline bench with your legs secured, holding a light barbell over your chest with a wide grip.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Lower the bar back in an arc behind your head until you feel a stretch in your chest and lats. Do not force the range.
Pull it back over your chest along the same arc.

wide-grip-lat-pulldown.muscles: Primary: Lats · Secondary: Biceps, Mid back, Shoulders
steps: Sit at the lat pulldown with your thighs under the pads, holding the bar overhand and wider than shoulders.
Lean back slightly and lift your chest, arms straight.
Pull the bar down to your upper chest, driving your elbows down towards your sides.
Let it rise slowly until your arms are straight.

wide-grip-pulldown-behind-the-neck.muscles: Primary: Lats · Secondary: Biceps, Mid back, Shoulders
steps: Only do this if your shoulders are comfortable with it. Sit at the pulldown, thighs under the pads, with a wide overhand grip.
Sit upright and tip your head slightly forward so the bar can pass behind it.
Pull the bar down behind your head to about the base of your neck, keeping your elbows under the bar.
Let it rise slowly until your arms are straight.

wide-grip-rear-pull-up.muscles: Primary: Lats · Secondary: Biceps, Mid back, Shoulders
steps: Only try this if your shoulders are mobile enough. Grip a pull-up bar overhand, well wider than shoulders.
Hang with arms straight, abs braced, and tip your head slightly forward.
Pull yourself up so the bar passes behind your head, bringing it towards the base of your neck.
Lower yourself slowly until your arms are straight.
Stand tall holding a barbell with an underhand grip wider than shoulder-width, arms straight.
Keep your elbows at your sides and your body still.
Curl the bar up towards your shoulders without leaning back.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly until your arms are straight.

wide-stance-barbell-squat.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back
steps: Set the safeties just below your bottom position and place the bar on your upper back.
Step back and set your feet wider than shoulder-width with toes turned out.
Brace, then sit down between your legs, pushing your knees out over your toes and keeping your chest up.
Drive up through your whole foot to stand tall.

wide-stance-stiff-legs.muscles: Primary: Hamstrings · Secondary: Adductors, Glutes, Lower back
steps: Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width, toes slightly out, holding a barbell in front of your thighs.
Keep a slight bend in your knees, brace your midsection and keep your back flat.
Push your hips back and lower the bar towards the floor until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings and inner thighs.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall, keeping the bar close to your legs.
Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, arms straight and shoulders active.
Brace your abs so your body stays still and does not swing.
Drive one knee up towards your chest, then lower it as you drive the other up, like running in the air.
Keep alternating at a steady pace, stopping before your grip or form fades.
Hold a wrist roller with both hands, overhand, arms straight out in front of you at shoulder height, with a light weight on the cord.
Keep your arms still and your shoulders down.
Turn the handle one hand at a time to wind the cord up until the weight reaches the handle.
Unwind it slowly under control until the weight is back down.
Stand tall holding a light barbell in front of you with an overhand grip, arms hanging straight.
Keep your elbows and shoulders still.
Rotate your wrists back and forth in small circles, moving only at the wrist.
Keep the movement smooth and steady until your forearms tire, then set the bar down.

yoke-walk.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Abs, Abductors, Adductors, Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings, Lower back
steps: Learn this with a light load. Set the yoke crossbar at upper-back height, get under it and brace hard.
Stand up to lift the yoke, gripping the uprights to keep it steady.
Walk forward with short, quick steps, staying tall and braced.
Stop under control and set the yoke down by bending your knees, not by dropping it.

zercher-squats.muscles: Primary: Quads · Secondary: Calves, Glutes, Hamstrings
steps: Set the bar in a rack at about waist height and the safeties just below your bottom position. Hold the bar in the crooks of your elbows.
Clasp your hands together, lift the bar out and step back with feet shoulder-width apart.
Brace and squat down, keeping your chest up and elbows inside your knees.
Drive up to standing, keeping your upper back tight so the bar stays level.
Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing forward.
Curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders, keeping your elbows at your sides.
At the top, turn your wrists so your palms face down.
Lower the dumbbells slowly with palms down, then turn them back to face up at the bottom.
Sit at a preacher bench with the backs of your upper arms on the pad, a dumbbell in each hand, palms up.
Curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders, keeping your arms on the pad.
At the top, turn your wrists so your palms face down.
Lower slowly with palms down, then turn them back up at the bottom before the next rep.
